data.title: I Tried to Buy an Actual Barrel of Crude Oil (2015)
data.author: niklasbuschmann
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：石油交易及相关行业的细节与轶事

不同观点：
• **hodder**: 作为石油交易商，每天购买约20万桶石油，强调石油交易量巨大，即使是小交易商也是如此。他还分享了石油交易中的单位换算细节（如"cubes"和km3），并表示愿意回答行业相关问题。
• **timoth3y**: 提到NPR的《Planet Money》节目曾追踪过一桶石油从购买到精炼的整个过程，提供了有关石油行业的详细信息，并附上了相关链接。
• **throw0101d**: 提供了2020年石油价格跌至负值的新闻链接，突显了石油市场波动的极端情况。
• **ahazred8ta**: 以调侃的方式将hodder的石油交易轶事与一个期货交易员误将一船煤运至曼哈顿办公室的故事进行类比，带有幽默色彩。

补充讨论：
• **nickdothutton**: 分享了自己学习地质学时的经历，特别是对不同种类原油的直观认识，描述了原油的气味和特性。
• **ANarrativeApe**: 提出了对比特币当前价值的疑问，将讨论引向数字货币与传统商品（如石油）的对比。
• **austinallegro**: 以调侃方式表示想购买猪肉肚和冷冻浓缩橙汁，将讨论引向其他商品交易。
• **niklasbuschmann**: 提供了存档链接，但未进一步阐述具体观点。
• **steveBK123**: 提到一个名为Odd Lots的播客，并称赞其内容有趣且富有信息量。
• **thenthenthen**: 提到了《The Toaster Project》一书，认为该书在某种程度上涉及石油行业话题，并提供了链接。
• **helsinkiandrew**: 回忆了2015年和2020年在Hacker News上出现过的类似讨论，提供了历史讨论链接。
• **bubblethink**: 以调侃方式提到"The Gang Solves the Gas Crisis"，未深入讨论具体观点。
• **timewizard**: 提供了纽约商品交易所（NYMEX）规则手册的链接，讨论了期货合约的详细交付规定，特别是轻甜原油期货的交付细节。
• **maCDzP**: 推荐了NPR的《The Onion King》节目，认为对商品交易感兴趣的人会喜欢。
• **metalman**: 分享了自己在商品交易中的经验，提到私人拥有的油井和工业环境中的交易细节，强调了耐心和尊重在获取小量商品交易机会中的重要性。

争议焦点：
• 讨论中并无明显争议，主要是分享石油交易及相关行业的经验和趣闻。唯一潜在的争议点在于对石油市场极端波动情况的看法（throw0101d提供的负油价新闻），但未展开详细讨论。

总结：
讨论围绕石油交易的庞大规模和复杂性展开，涉及单位换算、市场波动、行业轶事及相关商品交易。参与者分享了各自的见解和经验，提供了丰富的背景信息和参考链接。

data.title: Show HN: Colanode, open-source and local-first Slack and Notion alternative
data.author: hakanshehu
data.article_summary: Colanode是一款开源、本地优先的协作平台，类似于Slack和Notion，但更加注重用户的数据控制和隐私保护。它支持实时聊天、富文本页面编辑（如文档、维基）、可定制数据库以及文件管理等功能，适合个人和小团队使用。Colanode采用本地优先的工作流，所有更改先保存在本地SQLite数据库，然后同步到服务器，支持离线操作。它利用CRDTs技术实现无冲突的实时协作，并提供自托管选项，用户可通过Docker自行部署。平台目前处于测试阶段，提供免费的云服务器，未来将公布定价方案。Colanode基于Apache 2.0许可证发布。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对Colanode产品的功能、技术实现、商业模式及竞争比较的讨论

不同观点：
• mdaniel：对产品动画和整体印象表示赞赏，但对定价页面的提前展示表示不解。同时对技术实现中的Valkey和Redis使用提出疑问，并建议明确Minio的许可证问题以及固定Docker镜像版本。
• regnerba：关注是否有移动应用计划，认为移动应用是其使用的重要前提。
• alok-g：期待更多文档以了解产品，并将Colanode与Notesnook进行比较，指出Notesnook在细节处理上的优点及自托管时的问题。
• esperent：认为市场竞争激烈但仍有改进空间，关注跨平台实时通知功能，尤其是自托管情况下的实现方式。
• itomato：对数据导出和迁移功能表示关注，以Notion为例，强调导出功能的重要性。
• nashashmi：尝试理解和定义新一代笔记/生产力工具的共同特性，并提出这些工具普遍具有的“块内容”、“内嵌页面”、“关系表”和“动态视图引擎”等功能。
• ThinkBeat：对开源与商业模式的结合表示怀疑，关注未来的定价结构及开放源码的范围。
• badmonster：建议添加节点之间的可编程逻辑或自动化功能。
• plextoria：对产品表示期待，但遇到带宽问题，关注单点登录（SSO）功能的实现或计划。
• handfuloflight：询问是否可以自定义字体和颜色方案，而不需要自行修改代码。
• eterps：询问Electron桌面客户端的必要性，是否有浏览器版本。
• frizlab：将Colanode与Huly进行比较，询问两者区别。
• drcongo：关注任务管理功能，认为这是团队工作中减少干扰的关键，并对现有工具的任务实现表示不满。

补充讨论：
• 技术实现和功能细节是讨论的核心，用户对具体技术选择、功能实现及与其他产品的比较有较多关注。
• 用户对开源和商业模式的结合存在一定疑虑，尤其是未来的定价和开放源码的范围。
• 移动应用、SSO、自定义界面、跨平台通知等功能需求被多次提及，显示出用户对产品灵活性和多平台支持的期待。
• 与竞争产品（如Notesnook、Huly）的比较也是讨论的重点，用户希望了解Colanode的独特优势和改进之处。

Colanode
Open-source & local-first collaboration workspace that you can self-host
Colanode is an all-in-one platform for easy collaboration, built to prioritize your data privacy and control. Designed with a
local-first
approach, it helps teams communicate, organize, and manage projects—whether online or offline. With Colanode, you get the flexibility of modern collaboration tools, plus the peace of mind that comes from owning your data.
What can you do with Colanode?
Real-Time Chat:
Stay connected with instant messaging for teams and individuals.
Rich Text Pages:
Create documents, wikis, and notes using an intuitive editor, similar to Notion.
Customizable Databases:
Organize information with structured data, custom fields and dynamic views (table, kanban, calendar).
File Management:
Store, share, and manage files effortlessly within secure workspaces.
Built for both individuals and teams, Colanode adapts to your needs, whether you're running a small project, managing a team, or collaborating across an entire organization. With its self-hosted model, you retain full control over your data while enjoying a polished, feature-rich experience.
How it works
Colanode includes a desktop app and a self-hosted server. You can connect to multiple servers with a single app, each containing one or more
workspaces
for different teams or projects. After logging in, you pick a workspace to start collaborating—sending messages, editing pages, or updating database records.
Local-first workflow
All changes you make are saved to a local SQLite database first and then synced to the server. A background process handles this synchronization so you can keep working even if your computer or the server goes offline. Data reads also happen locally, ensuring immediate access to any content you have permissions to view.
Concurrent edits
Colanode relies on
Conflict-free Replicated Data Types (CRDTs)
- powered by
Yjs
- to allow real-time collaboration on entries like pages or database records. This means multiple people can edit at the same time, and the system gracefully merges everyone’s updates. Deletions are also tracked as specialized transactions. Messages and file operations don’t support concurrent edits and use simpler database tables.
Get started for free
To begin using Colanode,
download the official desktop app
from the
website
. Once installed, you can connect to any Colanode server—including our free beta cloud servers:
Colanode Cloud (EU)
– hosted in Europe.
Colanode Cloud (US)
– hosted in the United States.
Both cloud servers are currently in beta and free to use; pricing will be announced soon.
Self-host with Docker
If you prefer to host your own Colanode server, simply use the Docker Compose file in the root of this repository. In the near future, we’ll provide more detailed instructions for other environments, including Kubernetes. For now, here’s what you need to run Colanode yourself:
Postgres
with the
pgvector
extension.
Redis
(any Redis-compatible service will work, e.g., Valkey).
S3-compatible storage
(supporting basic file operations and presigned URLs).
Colanode server API
, provided as a Docker image.
All required environment variables for the Colanode server can be found in the docker-compose file.
License
Colanode is released under the
Apache 2.0 License
.

data.title: Fundamental flaws of SIMD ISAs (2021)
data.author: fanf2
data.article_summary:
本文讨论了SIMD（单指令多数据流）架构的特点和其在现代消费级CPU中的应用，特别是非谓词打包SIMD ISA。打包SIMD架构将多个数据元素打包进固定宽度的寄存器中，例如128位寄存器可包含16个字节或4个单精度浮点数。自1990年代中期以来，这种架构非常流行，包括x86（如MMX、SSE、AVX）、ARM（NEON）、POWER（AltiVec）等。

然而，这种架构存在几个缺陷。首先，固定寄存器宽度限制了硬件并行性的扩展，新一代SIMD需要新增指令和寄存器，导致ABI、操作系统和编译器需更新，且每代之间缺乏二进制兼容性。其次，流水线问题要求循环展开以避免流水线停滞，但这会降低代码密度并增加寄存器使用压力。最后，当处理数组元素数量不是寄存器元素数量的倍数时，需要额外的尾部处理逻辑。

这些缺陷影响了打包SIMD架构的性能和易用性，尽管其旨在提高数据处理性能。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：SIMD与Vector ISA的优劣以及在实际应用中的表现

不同观点：
• stephencanon认为，很多批评SIMD的文章使用过于简单的例子（如SAXPY）来说明问题，忽视了现实世界中复杂的SIMD应用场景，如数据编码、像素处理等。他主张结合固定宽度SIMD和向量ISA的优点来解决问题。
• TinkersW不同意stephencanon的观点，认为固定宽度的SIMD使得代码更简单，且可以通过特殊容器处理尾部数据，而不需要掩码或标量循环。
• Someone提出可以通过动态获取寄存器大小来适应不同硬件的并行能力，并询问是否已有架构实现这一方案。
• xphos强调在SIMD中结合load和increment地址寄存器的单指令价值，认为这可以避免von Neumann瓶颈。
• sweetjuly解释循环展开主要是为了分摊循环成本，而不是因为流水线问题。
• pornel提出替代方案，如通过指令更新机制或SIMT来解决SIMD的问题，认为这些方法可以提高性能。
• codedokode认为 packed SIMD 在各方面都优于 Vector SIMD，尤其是在性能和编译方面，并对RISC-V社区偏好Vector架构表示不解。
• pkhuong提醒SIMD的应用范围广泛，不仅仅是BLAS。
• bob1029主张通过高层次的抽象来处理SIMD，而不是直接与底层指令交互。
• dragontamer以GPU为例，说明固定宽度的SIMD设计在实践中没有问题，且更易于设计和实现。
• freeone3000提到x86 SIMD的寄存器别名问题，认为vectorized指令没有这种问题。
• gitroom表达了对低层次控制以获得更流畅性能的必要性。
• lauriewired指出行业正在向Vector-length-agnostic的架构发展，如Arm的SVE和RISC-V的向量扩展。
• convolvatron补充缺乏水平操作和更通用的通信模型也是SIMD的问题。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于SIMD和Vector ISA在实际应用中的表现以及各自的优缺点。

According to Flynn’s taxonomy
SIMD
refers to a computer architecture that can process multiple data streams with a single instruction (i.e. “Single Instruction stream, Multiple Data streams”). There are different taxonomies, and within those several different sub-categories and architectures that classify as “SIMD”.
In this post, however, I refer to packed SIMD ISA:s, i.e. the type of SIMD
instruction set architecture
that is most common in contemporary consumer grade CPU:s. More specifically, I refer to
non-predicated packed SIMD
ISA:s where the details of packed SIMD processing is exposed to the software environment.
Packed SIMD
The common trait of packed SIMD architectures is that several data elements are packed into a single register of a fixed width. Here is an example of possible configurations of a packed 128 bits wide SIMD register:
For instance, a 128-bit register can hold sixteen integer bytes or four single precision floating-point values.
This type of SIMD architecture has been wildly popular since the mid 1990s, and some packed SIMD ISA:s are:
x86:
MMX
,
3DNow!
,
SSE
,
SSE2
, …, and
AVX
,
AVX2
,
AVX-512
1
ARM: ARMv6 SIMD,
NEON
POWER:
AltiVec
(a.k.a. VMX and VelocityEngine)
MIPS:
MDMX
,
MIPS-3D
,
MSA
,
DSP
SPARC:
VIS
Alpha:
MVI
1
AVX and later x86 SIMD ISA:s (especially AVX-512) incorporate features from
vector processing
, making them packed SIMD / vector processing hybrids (thus some of the aspects discussed in this article do not fully apply).
The promise of all those ISA:s is increased data processing performance, since each instruction executes several operations in parallel. However, there are problems with this model.
Flaw 1: Fixed register width
Since the register size is fixed there is no way to scale the ISA to new levels of hardware parallelism without adding new instructions and registers. Case in point: MMX (64 bits) vs SSE (128 bits) vs AVX (256 bits) vs AVX-512 (512 bits).
Adding new registers and instructions has many implications. For instance, the
ABI
must be updated, and support must be added to operating system kernels, compilers and debuggers.
Another problem is that each new SIMD generation requires new instruction opcodes and encodings. In fixed width instruction sets (e.g. ARM) this may prohibit any new extensions, since there may not be enough opcode slots left for adding the new instructions. In variable width instruction sets (e.g. x86) the effect is typically that instructions get longer and longer (effectively hurting code density). Paradoxically each new SIMD generation essentially renders the previous generations redundant (except for supporting binary backwards compatibility), so a large number of instructions are wasted without adding much value.
Finally, any software that wants to use the new instruction set needs to be rewritten (or at least recompiled). What is worse, software developers often have to target several SIMD generations, and add mechanisms to their programs that dynamically select the optimal code paths depending on which SIMD generation is supported.
Flaw 2: Pipelining
The packed SIMD paradigm is that there is a 1:1 mapping between the register width and the execution unit width (this is usually required to achieve reasonable performance for instructions that mix inputs from several lanes). At the same time many SIMD operations are pipelined and require several clock cycles to complete (e.g. floating-point arithmetic and memory load instructions). The side effect of this is that the result of one SIMD instruction is not ready to be used until several instructions later in the instruction stream.
Consequently, loops have to be
unrolled
in order to avoid stalls and keep the pipeline busy. This can be done in advanced (power hungry) hardware implementations with register renaming and speculative out-of-order execution, but for simpler (usually more power efficient) hardware implementations loops have to be unrolled in software. Many software developers and compilers aiming to support both in-order and out-of-order processors simply unroll all SIMD loops in software.
However, loop unrolling hurts code density (i.e. makes the program binary larger), which in turn hurts instruction cache performance (fewer program segments fit in the instruction cache, which reduces the cache hit ratio).
Loop unrolling also increases
register pressure
(i.e. more registers must be used in order to keep the state of multiple loop iterations in registers), so the architecture must provide enough SIMD registers to avoid
register spilling
.
Flaw 3: Tail handling
When the number of array elements that are to be processed in a loop is not a multiple of the number of elements in the SIMD register, special loop tail handling needs to be implemented in software. For instance if an array contains 99 32-bit elements, and the SIMD architecture is 128 bits wide (i.e. a SIMD register contains four 32-bit elements), 4*24=96 elem
43783416.article_summary:
本文讨论了SIMD（单指令多数据流）架构的特点和其在现代消费级CPU中的应用，特别是非谓词打包SIMD ISA。打包SIMD架构将多个数据元素打包进固定宽度的寄存器中，例如128位寄存器可包含16个字节或4个单精度浮点数。自1990年代中期以来，这种架构非常流行，包括x86（如MMX、SSE、AVX）、ARM（NEON）、POWER（AltiVec）等。

然而，这种架构存在几个缺陷。首先，固定寄存器宽度限制了硬件并行性的扩展，新一代SIMD需要新增指令和寄存器，导致ABI、操作系统和编译器需更新，且每代之间缺乏二进制兼容性。其次，流水线问题要求循环展开以避免流水线停滞，但这会降低代码密度并增加寄存器使用压力。最后，当处理数组元素数量不是寄存器元素数量的倍数时，需要额外的尾部处理逻辑。

这些缺陷影响了打包SIMD架构的性能和易用性，尽管其旨在提高数据处理性能。

data.title: Asymmetric Content Moderation in Search Markets: The Case of Adult Websites
data.author: amadeuspagel
data.article_summary: 这篇文章研究了一个主导在线平台的内容审核对竞争的影响。作者通过一个外生冲击，即最大的成人内容平台删除非验证内容（占视频库80%），发现该政策导致平台流量在一个月内下降41%。然而，大部分流失的流量被其他竞争平台吸收，尤其是较少监管的边缘网站，其访问量在六个月内增加了55%，而主流平台仅增长10%。搜索引擎在流量重新分配中起关键作用，边缘平台通过搜索推荐和聚合器获得更多流量。主导平台则更积极地使用版权投诉移除竞争对手内容。研究强调，内容审核的不对称影响可以重塑市场竞争，推动用户流向较少监管的平台。

Asymmetric Content Moderation in Search Markets: The Case of Adult Websites
80 Pages

Leonardo Madio
University of Padua - Department of Economics and Management; CESifo (Center for Economic Studies and Ifo Institute)

Rotman School of Management
Martin Quinn
Erasmus University Rotterdam (EUR)
Carlo Reggiani
The University of Manchester
Date Written: February 01, 2025
Abstract
We study the competitive impact of content moderation by a dominant online platform. We exploit an exogenous shock that led the largest adult content platform to remove all non-verified content, eliminating 80\% of its video library. Using a difference-in-differences approach and leveraging on daily website-country level traffic data, we find that this policy resulted in a 41% drop in traffic within one month, suggesting strong user preferences for the removed content. However, much of the displaced traffic was absorbed by competing platforms, including both mainstream rivals and less regulated fringe websites. Over six months, fringe sites experienced a 55% increase in visits, far outpacing the 10% growth of mainstream competitors.  Search engines played a critical role in this reallocation: fringe platforms saw a surge in traffic from search referrals and aggregators, as users actively sought alternative content sources. We document an intensification of competition in search: the leading platform became more aggressive towards copyright-infringing rivals, strategically using DMCA filings to remove competing content from search results. Our findings highlight how asymmetric exposure to content moderation shocks can reshape market competition, drive consumers toward less regulated spaces, and alter substitution patterns across platforms.
Keywords:
Content moderation, Platforms, digital services act, adult websites, porn, platform competition, platform regulation

data.title: Show HN: Infat – Declaritive application assocation manager for macOS
data.author: philocalyst
data.article_summary:
Infat是一个macOS上的命令行工具，用于管理文件类型和URL scheme的默认打开应用。它允许用户列出和设置特定文件扩展名或URL scheme的默认应用程序，并通过TOML配置文件进行声明式管理。主要功能包括：

1. 查看文件扩展名或URL scheme的默认应用。
2. 设置文件扩展名或URL scheme的默认应用。
3. 通过TOML文件配置关联规则。
4. 支持详细日志和脚本化操作，适合高级用户和系统管理员。

安装方式包括通过Homebrew或从源码构建。Infat使用Swift开发，遵循MIT许可证。

Infat is an ultra-powerful, macOS-native CLI tool for declaritively managing both file-type and URL-scheme associations. Avoid the hassle of navigating sub-menus to setup your default browser or image viewer, and the pain of doing that
every time
you get a new machine. Setup the rules once, and bask in your own ingenuity forevermore. Take back control, and bind your openers to whatever. You. Want. Override everything! Who's going to stop you?
Summary
List which apps open a given file extension or URL scheme
Set a default application for a file extension or URL scheme
Load associations from a TOML config (
[files]
and
[schemes]
tables)
Verbose, scriptable, and ideal for power users and admins
Get Started
Get started by installing Infat — jump to the
Install
section below.
Tutorial
1. Listing Associations
#
Show the default app for .txt files
infat list txt
#
Show all registered apps for .txt files
infat list --assigned txt
2. Setting a Default Application
#
Use TextEdit for .md files
infat
set
TextEdit --file-type md
#
Use VSCode for .json files
infat
set
VSCode --file-type json
3. Binding a URL Scheme
#
Use Mail.app for mailto: links
infat
set
Mail --scheme mailto
4. Configuration
Place a TOML file at
$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/infat/config.toml
(or pass
--config path/to/config.toml
) with two tables:
[
files
]
md
=
"
TextEdit
"
html
=
"
Safari
"
pdf
=
"
Preview
"
[
schemes
]
mailto
=
"
Mail
"
web
=
"
Safari
"
Run without arguments to apply all entries.
infat --config
~
/.config/infat/config.toml
Design Philosophy
Minimal & Scriptable
Infat is a single-binary tool that plays well in shells and automation pipelines.
macOS-First
Leverages native
NSWorkspace
, Launch Services, and UTType for robust integration.
Declarative Configuration
TOML support allows you to version-control your associations alongside other dotfiles.
Building and Debugging
You’ll need
just
and Swift 5.9+:
#
Debug build
just build
#
Release build
just build-release
#
Run in debug mode
just run
"
list txt
"
#
Enable verbose logging for troubleshooting
infat --verbose list pdf
Install
Homebrew
brew install philocalyst/tap/infat
From Source
git clone https://github.com/philocalyst/infat.git
cd
infat
just build-release
cp .build/release/infat /usr/local/bin/infat

43785350.article_summary:
Infat是一个macOS上的命令行工具，用于管理文件类型和URL scheme的默认打开应用。它允许用户列出和设置特定文件扩展名或URL scheme的默认应用程序，并通过TOML配置文件进行声明式管理。主要功能包括：

1. 查看文件扩展名或URL scheme的默认应用。
2. 设置文件扩展名或URL scheme的默认应用。
3. 通过TOML文件配置关联规则。
4. 支持详细日志和脚本化操作，适合高级用户和系统管理员。

安装方式包括通过Homebrew或从源码构建。Infat使用Swift开发，遵循MIT许可证。

data.title: OpenVSX, which VSCode forks rely on for extensions, down for 24 hours
data.author: aaronvg
data.article_summary: 截至2025年4月24日，官方主页、查询API、搜索API和VSCode资产API等服务因后端存储问题导致宕机，正在努力修复。该问题从4月23日11:31am EDT开始，目前仍在解决中。此前已有4次更新记录，显示持续处理该事故。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：开源项目和开发工具的现状，特别是关于去中心化与中心化托管的争议，以及对VSCode及其替代品的讨论。

不同观点：
• [0xbadcafebee] 认为过去开源项目通过多个随机镜像托管，去中心化的方式更加自由和可靠，而现在依赖大公司的免费服务，导致个人信息和数据的让渡。他主张改变现状，回归更简单的时代。
• [fr4nkr] 分享了使用VSCodium的负面体验，指出其对中心化仓库（OpenVSX）的依赖导致功能缺失，并对比了Emacs的手动安装简便性，认为VSCodium的努力是徒劳的。
• [joshstrange] 将VSCode比作Android，认为其开源版本（VSCodium）在没有市场和插件支持的情况下几乎不可用，批评微软的商业模式。
• [exceptione] 推荐Eclipse Theia作为VSCode的替代品，认为其完全开放且无“间谍软件”，同时批评微软的销售公司本质。
• [loloquwowndueo] 指出VSCode设计上就是为了“分裂”，其分支是其设计的一部分。
• [jamisonbryant] 讨论了GitLab对OpenVSX的支持，强调了扩展支持对开发团队的重要性。

补充讨论：
• [john-h-k] 提到了Helix编辑器，并推荐给那些寻找Vim/Emacs替代品的人。
• [gchamonlive] 推荐了Lazy Vim，并分享了其易用性和配置经验。
• [khimaros] 提到了Lapce编辑器，认为其是该领域的一个有趣竞争者。
• [mdaniel] 提供了关于Eclipse Foundation服务中断的技术细节，强调了中心化托管的潜在问题。
• [jononor] 寻求现代、开箱即用、支持多种开发领域的开源IDE替代品。
• [thomond] 建议手动下载和安装扩展，以解决中心化托管服务中断的问题。
• [Dwedit] 提出使用IPFS/IPNS作为去中心化备份方案。
• [Havoc] 分享了学习neovim的经验，认为其避免了VSCode对Remote SSH扩展的依赖。
• [throwaway42167] 指出可以配置VSCodium使用微软的扩展库，并通过一些技巧使其兼容VSCode插件，但由于法律原因无法开箱即用。

争议焦点：
• 中心化托管（如VSCode和其插件市场）的可靠性与去中心化托管的对比。
• 开源项目对大公司免费服务的依赖是否会导致个人数据和隐私的让渡。
• VSCode及其开源替代品（如VSCodium和Eclipse Theia）在功能和易用性上的差异。

data.title: PyGraph: Robust Compiler Support for CUDA Graphs in PyTorch
data.author: mfiguiere
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一种名为PyGraph的方法，旨在为PyTorch提供对CUDA Graphs的强大编译器支持。CUDA Graphs旨在通过捕捉和启动一系列GPU任务来减少CPU开销，但由于其静态结构和数据复制开销，实际部署中往往导致性能下降。PyGraph通过三项关键优化解决这些问题：扩大CUDA Graphs的适用范围、减少GPU内核参数复制开销、基于成本效益分析选择性部署CUDA Graphs。PyGraph无缝集成到PyTorch2的编译工具链中，无需手动修改代码即可提升性能。实验表明，PyGraph在多种机器学习基准测试中显著提升了性能。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Python包命名、可复现性与实用性、技术实现细节与优化、对相关研究和机构的认可、源代码的缺失

不同观点：
• damnitbuilds认为该Python包用于CUDA Graphs，因此建议命名为"PyCudaGraph"更为合适，而不是"PyGraph"，以避免与其他类型的Python图形库混淆。

• infocollector指出，由于缺乏可直接通过pip安装的软件包（如"pip install pygraph"），难以全面评估该工作的可复现性和实际应用性。

• saagarjha对该技术表示赞赏，但希望看到其整合到PyTorch中，而不仅仅是一篇论文。他讨论了技术细节，指出图形中"bake-in"参数的问题，并建议通过间接引用指针来解决，同时提到这种方法可能带来的开销和信息丢失问题。他还提出未来可以探索在PyTorch中更好地支持CUDA图形，如条件节点。

• tho423i43234对印度科学学院（IISc）的研究工作表示认可，并提到相关研究人员和机构，如Pluto框架和PolyMage Labs，以及IISc的ArtPARK initiative，显示出对学术和产业结合的支持。

• OutOfHere抱怨评论中没有提供源代码，可能影响对该工作的进一步理解和应用。

补充讨论：
• 技术实现中的细节问题，如指针间接引用和开销，以及在实际应用中可能需要的进一步探索和优化。
• 对研究工作和相关机构的认可，反映出对学术和产业结合的积极态度。
• 缺乏可直接安装的软件包和源代码，可能影响该工作的可复现性和实际应用性。

Title:
PyGraph: Robust Compiler Support for CUDA Graphs in PyTorch
Authors:
Abhishek Ghosh
,
Ajay Nayak
,
Ashish Panwar
,
Arkaprava Basu
View a PDF of the paper titled PyGraph: Robust Compiler Support for CUDA Graphs in PyTorch, by Abhishek Ghosh and 3 other authors
View PDF
HTML (experimental)
Abstract:
CUDA Graphs -- a recent hardware feature introduced for NVIDIA GPUs -- aim to reduce CPU launch overhead by capturing and launching a series of GPU tasks (kernels) as a DAG. However, deploying CUDA Graphs faces several challenges today due to the static structure of a graph. It also incurs performance overhead due to data copy. In fact, we show a counter-intuitive result -- deploying CUDA Graphs hurts performance in many cases.
We introduce PyGraph, a novel approach to automatically harness the power of CUDA Graphs within PyTorch2. Driven by three key observations, PyGraph embodies three novel optimizations: it enables wider deployment of CUDA Graphs, reduces GPU kernel parameter copy overheads, and selectively deploys CUDA Graphs based on a cost-benefit analysis. PyGraph seamlessly integrates with PyTorch2's compilation toolchain, enabling efficient use of CUDA Graphs without manual modifications to the code. We evaluate PyGraph across various machine learning benchmarks, demonstrating substantial performance improvements over PyTorch2.

data.title: Tarpit ideas: What they are and how to avoid them (2023) [video]
data.author: dgs_sgd
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于“tarpit想法”（即看似可行但实际难以成功的想法）的讨论，特别是在科技、教育科技（EdTech）、创业和风投领域的应用。

不同观点：
• **kristopolous的观点**：许多技术或商业模式在特定背景下才能成功。例如，YouTube得益于DSL时代的到来，AI的突破依赖于数据和计算能力的提升，电动汽车依赖于电池技术的进步。许多创新（如无接触支付、触屏、LCD面板等）在早期并不实用，直到环境条件成熟才得以广泛应用。因此，识别背景变化是关键，许多“tarpit想法”可能在条件成熟时变得可行。

• **cjs_ac的观点**：在教育科技（EdTech）领域，许多想法是“tarpit想法”。教师行业有严格的职业标准，且教育心理学研究不断更新，导致很多教育工具只是一时的潮流，难以建立稳定的商业模式。如果要向学校销售软件，应该关注行政管理问题，而不是课堂教学工具。

• **asimpleusecase的观点**：从风投的角度看，“tarpit想法”通常是那些听起来不错但已有许多失败案例的想法。判断一个想法是否是tarpit，需要深入研究过去失败的原因，并确保有用户愿意付费使用产品。Tarpit并不是绝对的概念，随着技术或文化的变化，tarpit想法可能变成蓝海机会。

• **dzink的观点**：YC（Y Combinator）本可以成为一个分享失败经验和探索新领域的科学中心，但目前这些失败经验被浪费了。公开失败的想法和方法可以避免新的创业者重蹈覆辙，并有助于提高风投回报。

• **FinnLobsien的观点**：许多“tarpit想法”对于小规模软件企业是可行的，但不具备风投所追求的巨大市场潜力。特别是在B2C领域，很多想法难以获得大规模成功，除非能产生网络效应。

• **bob1029的观点**：B2B比B2C更容易成功。B2C需要不断吸引用户注意，而B2B只需搞定第一个客户后就能进入指数增长阶段。B2C创业者往往缺乏B2B销售的技能和网络。

• **davidedicillo的观点**：有些想法明确就是“tarpit想法”，但如果只是作为业余项目没有商业化野心，那也无所谓。

• **Scene_Cast2的观点**：有些想法现在是“tarpit想法”，但随着技术进步可能变得可行。例如，基于室内WiFi/BLE的定位技术在过去不准确，但随着技术进步现在变得更实用。

• **debarshri的观点**：一些“tarpit想法”可能因为创始人的执行力而成功。创业本身就像是一个tarpit，需要 perseverance 和勇气才能成功。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中多次提到如何识别和避免“tarpit想法”，包括研究过去的失败案例、确保有付费用户、避免需要大量资金投入才能吸引用户注意的项目等。
• 有人建议建立一个类似于HN（Hacker News）的wiki，记录那些失败的想法和公司，以供参考。
• 讨论中也提到了AI领域的“tarpit想法”，但未深入展开。

data.title: Scientists Develop Artificial Leaf, Uses Sunlight to Produce Valuable Chemicals
data.author: gnabgib
data.article_summary: 文章主要介绍了一个多机构合作项目——液态阳光联盟（LiSA），其目标是利用太阳能将二氧化碳转化为液态燃料。研究人员开发了一种基于钙钛矿和铜的装置，能将二氧化碳转化为C2产物，这些产物是塑料聚合物和喷气燃料等许多日常产品的前体。该研究由劳伦斯伯克利国家实验室和国际合作者共同完成，标志着人工光合作用研究的重要进展。该装置模仿植物叶片的光合作用，使用铅卤化物钙钛矿作为光吸收材料，铜作为电催化剂。虽然铜的选择性低于生物材料，但其更耐用和稳定。未来，研究团队计划提高系统效率并扩大装置尺寸以增加可扩展性。这项工作得到了美国能源部科学办公室的支持。

• Changoplatanero对新过程的效率与传统太阳能板发电后再合成化学品的效率进行了比较，提出了效率比较的疑问。

• Init7通过对比自然界的叶子与人类建造的结构，反思人类技术的持久性问题。

43788053.article_content:
Article
Materials
Key Takeaways
The Liquid Sunlight Alliance is a multi-institutional collaboration working to develop the tools needed to use energy from sunlight to produce liquid fuels.
Researchers built a perovskite and copper-based device that converts carbon dioxide into C
2
products
–
precursory chemicals of innumerable products in our everyday lives, from plastic polymers to jet fuel.
This proof-of-concept research opens new opportunities for energy research.
Researchers from the Department of Energy’s Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory (Berkeley Lab) along with international collaborators have brought us one step closer to harnessing the sun’s energy to convert carbon dioxide into liquid fuel and other valuable chemicals. In a recent
publication
in
Nature Catalysis
, the researchers debut a self-contained carbon-carbon (C2) producing system that combines the catalytic power of copper with
perovskite
, a material used in photovoltaic solar panels. This advance builds on over 20 years of research and brings the scientific community one step closer to replicating the productivity of a green leaf in nature.
This work is part of a larger initiative, the Liquid Sunlight Alliance (
LiSA
), which is a Fuels from Sunlight Energy Innovation Hub funded by the U.S. Department of Energy. Led by Caltech in close partnership with Berkeley Lab, LiSA brings together more than 100 scientists from national lab partners at SLAC and the National Renewable Energy Laboratory, and university partners at UC Irvine, UC San Diego, and the University of Oregon
.
Researchers involved in this multi-institutional collaboration have made advances in developing our understanding of and the tools needed to develop liquid fuels generated from sunlight, carbon dioxide, and water. (Learn more about the LiSA collaboration in this
roundup
, “Five Ways LiSA is Advancing Solar Fuels.”)
“Nature was our inspiration,” said Peidong Yang, a senior faculty scientist in Berkeley Lab’s Materials Sciences Division and UC Berkeley professor of chemistry and materials science and engineering involved in the published work. “We had to work on the individual components first, but when we brought everything together and realized that it was successful, it was a very exciting moment.”
To build a system that mimics photosynthesis, Yang and his team followed the natural processes that occur in the leaf of a plant. Each individual component of a leaf’s photosynthesizing elements had to be replicated and refined. Tapping into the decades’ worth of research, the scientists used lead halide perovskite photoabsorbers to imitate a leaf’s light-absorbing chlorophyll. And inspired by enzymes that regulate photosynthesis in nature, they designed electrocatalysts made of copper that resemble tiny flowers.
Previous experiments have successfully replicated photosynthesis through the use of biological materials, but this work incorporated an inorganic material, copper. While the selectivity of copper is lower than biological alternatives, the inclusion of copper presents a more durable, stable, and longer-lasting option for the artificial leaf system design.
Work led by researchers in the LiSA project developed the cathode and anode components of the new device. Instruments at Berkeley Lab’s
Molecular Foundry
allowed Yang’s team to integrate the device with metal contacts. During the experiments in Yang’s lab, a solar simulator mimicking a consistently bright sun was used to test the selectivity of the new device.
Prior innovations across research groups enabled an organic oxidation reaction to take place in the photoanode chamber and created C2 products in the photocathode chamber. This breakthrough created a realistic artificial-leaf architecture in a device about the size of a postage stamp
–
it converts CO
2
into a C2 molecule using only sunlight.
The C2 chemicals produced from this device are precursory ingredients for many industries that produce valuable products in our everyday lives
–
from plastic polymers to fuel for larger vehicles that can’t yet run off a battery, like an airplane. Building upon this fundamental research milestone, Yang is now aimed to increase the system’s efficiency and expand the size of the artificial leaf to begin increasing the scalability of the solution.
The
Molecular Foundry
is a user facility at Berkeley Lab.
This work was supported by the
DOE Office of Science
.
###
Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory
(Berkeley Lab) is committed to groundbreaking research focused on discovery science and solutions for abundant and reliable energy supplies. The lab’s expertise spans materials, chemistry, physics, biology, earth and environmental science, mathematics, and computing. Researchers from around the world rely on the lab’s world-class scientific facilities for their own pioneering research. data.title: Mistaking Mary Magdalene
data.author: benbreen
data.article_summary: 这篇文章探讨了基督教中玛利亚·玛达肋纳（Mary Magdalene）的复杂形象及其历史争议。她是继耶稣母亲之后新约中最著名的女性，出现在四部福音书中，尤其在耶稣复活后扮演重要角色，被十三世纪神学家托马斯·阿奎那称为“使徒中的使徒”。然而，教会历史上对她的描绘充满矛盾：在东方正教会中她备受尊崇，而在西方教会中她既被视为圣人，也被描绘为罪人、妓女，甚至有人猜测她是耶稣的妻子。文章提到，新约中关于她的描述有限，且与其他多名同名玛丽混淆，导致其形象模糊不定。宗教学者伊莱恩·帕格斯（Elaine Pagels）指出，早期福音书中女性角色常被弱化，而《菲利普福音》等非正典文本则赋予玛达肋纳更大的影响力，视其为神圣智慧的体现。文章还讨论了玛达肋纳被误解为妓女的起源，指出这一形象源于公元591年教皇格里高利的布道，而非新约本身。最终，玛达肋纳成为一个充满神秘和矛盾的人物，象征着不确定性和边缘人群的守护。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对评论内容的解读和可信性存在争议，特别是关于抹大拉的马利亚（Magdalene）相关历史和宗教叙述的解释。

不同观点：
• graemep认为原文中有很多推测和猜测的成分。虽然有些内容是公认的（如Gregory在声称马利亚是妓女中的角色），但这些信息在文中的解读值得怀疑。通常这些内容应被理解为耶稣对被传统标签为“坏”的人（如马太）的态度的体现。此外，graemep指出，某些内容非常荒谬，例如“耶稣可能在清理抹大拉的马利亚的脉轮”这一说法。

• gryfft提供了存档链接（https://archive.ph/lQqM9），但没有直接表达对原文内容的立场，可能是为了提供进一步的背景资料或让其他读者自行查阅相关讨论内容。

An ancient depiction of a naked woman hung on the wall of my father’s study. Skeletal, stupefied, and wildly bedheaded, she contemplated distances across time and space, as saints and mystics do. As with many of the unsettling religious tchotchkes scattered around the rectory where I spent my childhood, I didn’t give much thought to the unkempt icon, until more recently, when I grew curious about Mary Magdalene and began to read into the controversies swirling around her.
Magdalene is the most famous woman in Christianity after Jesus’ mother; she is also arguably the most hotly contested figure in the New Testament. A companion to Jesus in all four Gospels, she is present at his tomb, and, in some versions, is the first to see him after his Resurrection. In the Book of John, Jesus commissions her to share the good news of his return with the other disciples, which is why Thomas Aquinas, the thirteenth-century theologian, names her “the apostle to the apostles.” Nonetheless, Magdalene has been maligned by Church fathers throughout the centuries; in the present day, feminist scholars have championed her.
Magdalene, appearing in scripture only fourteen times, belongs to a tangle of at least six women named Mary. This multitude of Marys leaves considerable room for disagreement over which Biblical threads are authentically woven into Magdalene’s story, and which aren’t. In the Eastern Orthodox Church, she has a long and unassailed history of veneration. In the West, she’s been sanctified, but also portrayed as a sinner, a nun, a mystic, and Jesus’ wife. She remains, above all, a liminal figure. The patron saint of outcasts, she embodies uncertainty.
“There are so many disparate stories,”
Elaine Pagels
, the renowned religious scholar, told me on the sunporch of her home, in Princeton, New Jersey. To underscore the point, Pagels went to fetch a copy of “The New Oxford Annotated Bible,” flipping between the Books of Matthew, Mark, Luke, and John, and pausing over discrepancies between their Magdalene narratives. “The writers of the New Testament didn’t seem much interested in women except in their subsidiary roles,” she said. She poked around in the Book of Luke to show me how the author diminished Mary Magdalene’s significance. She’s present at the Resurrection, but only among other women. Instead of encountering the risen Lord, these women see two angels. “Luke deprecates her role,” Pagels said.
Pagel’s expertise, however, stretches far beyond the four Gospels that, by the start of the fifth century, had become the official canon. She has explored a much larger body of texts, many of which include women in more authoritative roles. Consider, she suggested, the Gospel of Philip—a third-century text discovered with similar documents near Nag Hammadi, in Egypt, in 1945—in which Magdalene is described as the woman “who always walked with the Lord” and “the one who was called his companion.” In its telling, her expansive influence transcends the terrestrial. As Pagels put it, “She’s seen as a manifestation of divine wisdom.”
Along with icons of anorexic saints, my childhood home was a place of books. Pagels’s “
The Gnostic Gospels
” shared a shelf with “
The Complete Poems of Emily Dickinson
” and Carl Jung’s “
Memories, Dreams, Reflections
.” Each, in its own way, invited a friendly skepticism of orthodoxy and imbued value in people and ideas previously relegated to the edge. As Dickinson writes, “Tell all the truth but tell it slant.”
Mary Magdalene is a cipher for slantwise truth; to engage with her story requires divine imagination. Beyond the scant scriptural references, a rich treasury of myth can be found. My favorite, a thirteenth-century French narrative known as the Golden Legend, features Magdalene and Jesus’ friend Lazarus, who in this and some other accounts is said to be her brother. With a handful of followers, the two board a boat fourteen years after Jesus’ crucifixion and land on the southern coast of France. There, Magdalene lives and teaches until her death. Two duelling French monasteries still claim to hold her relics. On July 22nd, her feast day, they venerate her as their patron saint.
Magdalene is rendered more complex by associations with sexual desire: in the popular imagination, she’s a repentant prostitute. Yet, as I read more about who Mary Magdalene was, I was startled to learn that nothing in the New Testament associates her with licentiousness. Instead, this claim originated in a series of sermons given by Pope Gregory in 591. Gregory argued that Magdalene should be understood as highly sinful, referring to a story, in the Book of Luke, in which Jesus exorcised seven demons from her body. (Feminist scholars have questioned this interpretation, raising the possibility that Magdalene’s seven demons reflect the Eastern concept of seven chakras rather than a sinful nature. Maybe Jesus was clearing Magdalene’s chakras.)
Pope
43748025.article_summary: 这篇文章探讨了基督教中玛利亚·玛达肋纳（Mary Magdalene）的复杂形象及其历史争议。她是继耶稣母亲之后新约中最著名的女性，出现在四部福音书中，尤其在耶稣复活后扮演重要角色，被十三世纪神学家托马斯·阿奎那称为“使徒中的使徒”。然而，教会历史上对她的描绘充满矛盾：在东方正教会中她备受尊崇，而在西方教会中她既被视为圣人，也被描绘为罪人、妓女，甚至有人猜测她是耶稣的妻子。文章提到，新约中关于她的描述有限，且与其他多名同名玛丽混淆，导致其形象模糊不定。宗教学者伊莱恩·帕格斯（Elaine Pagels）指出，早期福音书中女性角色常被弱化，而《菲利普福音》等非正典文本则赋予玛达肋纳更大的影响力，视其为神圣智慧的体现。文章还讨论了玛达肋纳被误解为妓女的起源，指出这一形象源于公元591年教皇格里高利的布道，而非新约本身。最终，玛达肋纳成为一个充满神秘和矛盾的人物，象征着不确定性和边缘人群的守护。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点： notation作为思维工具的作用及其在不同领域的应用和影响

不同观点：
• [jamesrom] 认为，新的符号系统不仅仅是表达式的替代，还代表了对问题的新思考方式，历史上许多重大发现都伴随着新符号的引入。新的符号系统可以帮助解决目前尚未解决的问题。
• [mathgradthrow] 指出，虽然数学家和计算机科学家容易接受符号系统对思维的影响，但在语言学和教育领域却存在争议。提到了萨丕尔-沃夫假说，认为学习的语言会影响思维方式，并指出由于自然语言的文化属性，这种观点在学术界是禁忌。同时批评教育中禁止学生学习有助于解决问题的符号系统。
• [talkingtab] 对萨丕尔-沃夫假说进行了延伸讨论，认为不完美的语言可能限制思维。探讨了社会机制（如社交媒体的"关注"和"点赞"）如何影响互动方式，并提出是否存在其他机制可以促进更好的集体思考。
• [FilosofumRex] 认为APL语言的衰落是不幸的，本可以有更大的影响。尽管有潜力，但行业选择了像Excel这样的工具，阻碍了APL的发展。
• [InfinityByTen] 对数学符号的普遍性提出质疑，认为符号系统如果与可视化和问题的工效学分离，会带来高成本。主张在某一领域内不应只有一种标准符号，以避免限制创造性和探索性。

补充讨论：
• [dang] 提供了关于"Notation as a Tool of Thought"文章的历史讨论链接，显示了该主题在不同时间点的讨论热度。
• [Duanemclemore] 分享了个人经验，将APL的概念应用于建筑学教学中，并提出让学生创建自己的符号系统的梦想课程。
• [colbyn] 提到自己正在开发一个适用于STEM领域的笔记应用，并分享了示例。
• [karaterobot] 推荐了一个关于符号系统影响思维的自述文件，并提供了链接。
• [jweir] 分享了学习APL语言的个人经验，指出其代码可以非常简洁但难以编写。
• [andymatuschak] 指出"Notation as a Tool of Thought"一文首次使用了"tool of thought"这一短语，并演变为今天的"tools for thought"。
• [Pompidou] 和 [xelxebar] 都分享了APL语言对个人思维方式的深刻影响，尤其是其在处理复杂性方面的独特方法。
• [cess11] 提到了一次对Iverson的采访，并认为1979年时的APL并不像今天这样边缘化。
• [alganet] 对符号系统普遍性的观点提出质疑，认为不应害怕没有明确符号引导的问题。

争议焦点：
• 符号系统在不同领域中的普遍性和适用性。
• 教育中是否应鼓励学生学习有助于解决问题的符号系统。
• 自然语言和符号系统对思维方式的影响及其在学术界的接受度。

data.title: Observability 2.0 and the Database for It
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary:
**Observability 2.0**，由Honeycomb的Charity Majors提出，是对传统可观察性方法的进化。传统可观察性依赖于**指标（metrics）**、**日志（logs）**和** traces（ traces）**这三个支柱，但这些方法在应对现代系统复杂性时面临诸多问题，如数据孤岛、预聚合取舍、非结构化日志、静态检测和数据冗余。

**Observability 2.0**采用**宽事件（wide events）**作为核心数据结构，保留原始、高保真的事件数据，作为唯一的真实数据来源。宽事件是高维度、高基数、上下文丰富的记录，允许团队事后进行探索性分析，动态生成指标、日志和traces。这种方法旨在解决传统方法的局限性，更有效地处理复杂系统。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：观察系统（Observability）中数据压缩、存储、查询及其实现工具的优缺点

不同观点：
• **支持使用压缩感知和AI模型进行数据压缩**：[rlupi] 提出利用压缩感知和AI模型来压缩数据，从线性存储转为对数存储，尤其适用于移动设备的观察系统。他认为可以通过训练小模型来捕捉系统行为，并将其应用于边缘计算。

• **强调查询能力和现有工具（如Elasticsearch和Opensearch）的成熟性**：[jillesvangurp] 认为像Elasticsearch和Opensearch这样的工具已经解决了存储和查询问题，尤其是它们提供了快速访问和高效查询的能力。他指出，仅仅解决存储问题是不够的，查询能力才是关键。

• **推荐ClickHouse作为分析工作负载的标准工具**：[jsumrall] 支持使用ClickHouse，认为它在处理分析和观察工作负载方面表现出色，并且比Postgres更适合不需事务的场景。

• **主张保留原始数据和开放工具链的完整性**：[sunng] 强调保持原始数据和上下文的重要性，并提到其团队正在开发开源数据库以应对宽事件的挑战。他们还关注从数据传输到工具链的完整性。

• **认为宽事件模型只是结构化日志的再包装**：[nexo-v1] 认为宽事件模型只是结构化日志的一个新概念，现有的工具如Loki或ELK堆栈已经能够很好地处理这些需求。

• **质疑存储和传输所有遥测数据的必要性**：[algorithmsRcool] 对存储所有请求的遥测数据以获取简单指标的做法表示怀疑，认为这样会增加不必要的开销。

• **关注实现宽事件模型的开发开销**：[awoimbee] 提到宽事件模型虽然是一个统一模型，但实现这些事件的开发开销依然很大。

• **担忧存储和查询复杂性及成本**：[the_duke] 对“存储原始数据”的方法持怀疑态度，认为这会增加查询复杂性和存储成本，主张使用能高效存储数据的列式数据库。

• **提出处理原始数据的创新方法**：[Drahflow] 介绍其quuxLogging系统，强调通过优化查询大量文本数据来从日志中提取指标，解决指标基数爆炸问题。

• **对宽事件模型的实际应用感到困惑**：[fuzzy2] 对宽事件模型作为单独事件收集方法的优越性感到困惑，质疑其在追踪和指标方面的覆盖能力。

补充讨论：
• **对统一数据库框架的需求**：[teleforce] 提出需要一种能同时处理原始和处理后数据的通用数据库框架，类似于D4M模型。

• **对现有观察工具的成本和复杂性的反馈**：[zaptheimpaler] 分享了他们从付费工具转向开源解决方案的经历，指出大量收集的观察数据往往未被使用，导致资源浪费。

争议焦点：
• **数据存储和查询的优先级**：一方认为压缩和减少数据存储是关键，另一方则强调查询能力和现有工具的成熟性。
• **宽事件模型的实际应用价值**：部分评论者认为宽事件模型只是已有方法的再包装，其实际应用和开发成本仍需考量。

43789625.article_content:
Observability 2.0 is a concept introduced by
Charity Majors of Honeycomb
, though she later
expressed reservations about labeling it as such
(follow-up).
Despite its contested naming, Observability 2.0 represents an evolution
from the foundational "three pillars" of observability, metrics, logs, and traces
, which have dominated the field for nearly a decade. Instead, it emphasizes a single source of truth paradigm as a data foundation of observability. This approach prioritizes high-cardinality, wide-event datasets over traditional siloed telemetry, aiming to address modern system complexity more effectively.
What is Observability 2.0 and Wide Events
​
For years, observability has relied on the three pillars of metrics, logs, and traces. These pillars spawned countless libraries, tools, and standards—including
OpenTelemetry
, one of the most successful cloud-native projects, which is built entirely on this paradigm. However, as systems grow in complexity, the limitations of this approach become evident.
The Downsides of Traditional Observability
​
Data silos
: Metrics, logs, and traces are often stored separately, leading to uncorrelated, or even inconsistent, data without meticulous management.
Pre-aggregation trade-offs
: Pre-aggregated metrics (counters, summaries, histograms) were originally designed to reduce storage costs and improve performance by sacrificing granularity. However, the rigid structure of time-series data limits the depth of contextual information, forcing teams to generate millions of distinct time-series to capture necessary details. Ironically, this practice now incurs exponentially higher storage and computational costs—directly contradicting the approach’s original purpose.
Unstructured logs
: While logs inherently contain structured data, extracting meaning requires intensive parsing, indexing, and computational effort.
Static instrumentation
: Tools rely on predefined queries and thresholds, limiting detection to 'known knowns'. Adapting observability requires code changes, forcing it to align with slow software development cycles.
Redundant data
: Identical information is duplicated across metrics, logs, and traces, wasting storage and increasing overhead.
Wide Events: The Approach of Observability 2.0
​
Observability 2.0 addresses these issues by
adopting wide events as its foundational data structure
. Instead of precomputing metrics or structuring logs upfront, it preserves raw, high-fidelity event data as the single source of truth. This allows teams to perform exploratory analysis retroactively, deriving metrics, logs, and traces dynamically from the original dataset.
Boris Tane, in
his article Observability Wide Event 101
, defines a wide event as a context-rich, high-dimensional, and high-cardinality record. For example, a single wide event might include:

43789625.article_summary:
**Observability 2.0**，由Honeycomb的Charity Majors提出，是对传统可观察性方法的进化。传统可观察性依赖于**指标（metrics）**、**日志（logs）**和** traces（ traces）**这三个支柱，但这些方法在应对现代系统复杂性时面临诸多问题，如数据孤岛、预聚合取舍、非结构化日志、静态检测和数据冗余。

**Observability 2.0**采用**宽事件（wide events）**作为核心数据结构，保留原始、高保真的事件数据，作为唯一的真实数据来源。宽事件是高维度、高基数、上下文丰富的记录，允许团队事后进行探索性分析，动态生成指标、日志和traces。这种方法旨在解决传统方法的局限性，更有效地处理复杂系统。

主要讨论点：观察系统（Observability）中数据压缩、存储、查询及其实现工具的优缺点

不同观点：
• **支持使用压缩感知和AI模型进行数据压缩**：[rlupi] 提出利用压缩感知和AI模型来压缩数据，从线性存储转为对数存储，尤其适用于移动设备的观察系统。他认为可以通过训练小模型来捕捉系统行为，并将其应用于边缘计算。

• **强调查询能力和现有工具（如Elasticsearch和Opensearch）的成熟性**：[jillesvangurp] 认为像Elasticsearch和Opensearch这样的工具已经解决了存储和查询问题，尤其是它们提供了快速访问和高效查询的能力。他指出，仅仅解决存储问题是不够的，查询能力才是关键。

• **推荐ClickHouse作为分析工作负载的标准工具**：[jsumrall] 支持使用ClickHouse，认为它在处理分析和观察工作负载方面表现出色，并且比Postgres更适合不需事务的场景。

• **主张保留原始数据和开放工具链的完整性**：[sunng] 强调保持原始数据和上下文的重要性，并提到其团队正在开发开源数据库以应对宽事件的挑战。他们还关注从数据传输到工具链的完整性。

• **认为宽事件模型只是结构化日志的再包装**：[nexo-v1] 认为宽事件模型只是结构化日志的一个新概念，现有的工具如Loki或ELK堆栈已经能够很好地处理这些需求。

• **质疑存储和传输所有遥测数据的必要性**：[algorithmsRcool] 对存储所有请求的遥测数据以获取简单指标的做法表示怀疑，认为这样会增加不必要的开销。

• **关注实现宽事件模型的开发开销**：[awoimbee] 提到宽事件模型虽然是一个统一模型，但实现这些事件的开发开销依然很大。

• **担忧存储和查询复杂性及成本**：[the_duke] 对“存储原始数据”的方法持怀疑态度，认为这会增加查询复杂性和存储成本，主张使用能高效存储数据的列式数据库。

• **提出处理原始数据的创新方法**：[Drahflow] 介绍其quuxLogging系统，强调通过优化查询大量文本数据来从日志中提取指标，解决指标基数爆炸问题。

• **对宽事件模型的实际应用感到困惑**：[fuzzy2] 对宽事件模型作为单独事件收集方法的优越性感到困惑，质疑其在追踪和指标方面的覆盖能力。

补充讨论：
• **对统一数据库框架的需求**：[teleforce] 提出需要一种能同时处理原始和处理后数据的通用数据库框架，类似于D4M模型。

• **对现有观察工具的成本和复杂性的反馈**：[zaptheimpaler] 分享了他们从付费工具转向开源解决方案的经历，指出大量收集的观察数据往往未被使用，导致资源浪费。

争议焦点：
• **数据存储和查询的优先级**：一方认为压缩和减少数据存储是关键，另一方则强调查询能力和现有工具的成熟性。
• **宽事件模型的实际应用价值**：部分评论者认为宽事件模型只是已有方法的再包装，其实际应用和开发成本仍需考量。

data.article_summary:
文章介绍了通过可视化方式理解Rust中的异步执行。作者创建了一个程序，通过计算正弦函数的值并使用`matplotlib`和`pyo3`绘制出结果，来观察异步任务的执行顺序和并发情况。程序中，多个异步任务交替执行，并通过通道发送计算结果。为了更清晰地展示每个任务的执行时间，作者在样本中加入了计算开始和结束的时间戳，并通过图形化显示这些时间。

文章还解释了并发和并行的区别：并发是任务交替执行，而并行则是任务同时执行。最后，作者通过引入更耗时的CPU操作（如`sin_high_cpu`），展示了CPU密集型任务如何阻塞异步执行器，并影响其他异步操作的执行。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Rust中的异步编程及其相关问题，包括CPU密集型任务、阻塞I/O操作、以及与其他语言/平台的比较。

不同观点：
• OskarS：认为CPU密集型任务必然会占用CPU资源，但可以通过将任务拆分为小块并使用`.await`或后台线程来缓解。更严重的问题是阻塞I/O操作，它不仅占用CPU，还阻碍事件循环，导致资源利用率低下。如果选择异步I/O，所有I/O操作都需要是异步的，否则会丧失异步的优势。

• Inglor：指出Node.js中可以使用`worker_threads`或者类似Tokio的API（如Piscina）来实现任务 spawn 和 futures 运行。同时提到Rayon在处理CPU密集型任务时表现良好，可以与Tokio混合使用，尽管有一些注意事项。

• Vermilingua：提出文章中未提及的一个问题，即在spawned线程上运行的计算生成的正弦波曲线有变形，质疑这是绘图问题还是Tokio线程时间跟踪不准确。

• Jdnier：以幽默方式评论生成的正弦波像多声部音乐谱，并提到可能受其他运行进程影响的音高变化。

• Binary132：希望看到类似的跨多个运行时的比较，而不仅限于Rust。

• Rc00：只是分享了一个相关的Hacker News链接，未发表具体观点。

• Jwufasdfsds：提到可以通过使用Plan9或Inferno来避免异步灾难，但并不作为对async-rust的批评，认为在Linux等传统平台上仍需使用异步Rust。

• ModernMech：对“drop pennies”这一表达感到困惑，询问其含义。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及了Rust异步编程中的实际问题，如阻塞I/O和CPU密集型任务的处理，以及与其他语言和平台（如Node.js）的比较。
• 有人提到具体工具和库（如Rayon和Piscina）的实际应用经验，提供了对异步和多线程编程的具体解决方案和建议。
• 对文章中未提及的技术细节（如正弦波变形问题）进行了补充讨论，提出了可能的技术问题或误解。
• 最后，有人对英语习语“drop pennies”的含义感到困惑，显示出对技术文章中文化表达的理解差异。

A Visual Journey Through Async Rust
I'm a visual and experimental learner. To truly understand something, I need to tinker with it and see it run with my own eyes. To truly understand async execution, I want to visualize it. What order are things happening in? Do concurrent futures affect each other? How do tasks and threads relate? Plotting network calls or file system operations is boring. Let's draw something.

• OskarS：认为CPU密集型任务必然会占用CPU资源，但可以通过将任务拆分为小块并使用`.await`或后台线程来缓解。更严重的问题是阻塞I/O操作，它不仅占用CPU，还阻碍事件循环，导致资源利用率低下。如果选择异步I/O，所有I/O操作都需要是异步的，否则会丧失异步的优势。

• Inglor：指出Node.js中可以使用`worker_threads`或者类似Tokio的API（如Piscina）来实现任务 spawn 和 futures 运行。同时提到Rayon在处理CPU密集型任务时表现良好，可以与Tokio混合使用，尽管有一些注意事项。

• Vermilingua：提出文章中未提及的一个问题，即在spawned线程上运行的计算生成的正弦波曲线有变形，质疑这是绘图问题还是Tokio线程时间跟踪不准确。

• Jdnier：以幽默方式评论生成的正弦波像多声部音乐谱，并提到可能受其他运行进程影响的音高变化。

• Binary132：希望看到类似的跨多个运行时的比较，而不仅限于Rust。

• Rc00：只是分享了一个相关的Hacker News链接，未发表具体观点。

• Jwufasdfsds：提到可以通过使用Plan9或Inferno来避免异步灾难，但并不作为对async-rust的批评，认为在Linux等传统平台上仍需使用异步Rust。

• ModernMech：对“drop pennies”这一表达感到困惑，询问其含义。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及了Rust异步编程中的实际问题，如阻塞I/O和CPU密集型任务的处理，以及与其他语言和平台（如Node.js）的比较。
• 有人提到具体工具和库（如Rayon和Piscina）的实际应用经验，提供了对异步和多线程编程的具体解决方案和建议。
• 对文章中未提及的技术细节（如正弦波变形问题）进行了补充讨论，提出了可能的技术问题或误解。
• 最后，有人对英语习语“drop pennies”的含义感到困惑，显示出对技术文章中文化表达的理解差异。

Faasta: a Faster FaaS Platform
Faasta is a cutting-edge Function-as-a-Service (FaaS) platform designed for exceptional speed and efficiency. With
cold start times under 1ms
and a
memory overhead of less than 1KB
, Faasta delivers unparalleled performance through its modern WebAssembly architecture.
Key Features
Runs your code as
WebAssembly modules
using the WASI P2 standard
Leverages
WASIHTTP
for high-performance HTTP request handling
Provides
secure isolation
between functions through WebAssembly's sandboxed execution model
Achieves
ultra-fast cold starts
without the overhead of traditional containerization
Self-hostable
with simple setup - run your own Faasta instance anywhere
Standards-compliant
with WASI P2 and WASIHTTP, making your functions portable
Powered by
Wasmtime
for efficient WebAssembly execution
Includes a
free hosted instance
at
faasta.xyz
Your code is compiled to WebAssembly with
strict safety requirements
, ensuring:
🔒 Secure execution within the WebAssembly sandbox
✅ Whitelisted dependencies
🌐 Standards-compliant implementation using WASI P2 and WASIHTTP
Getting Started
Install the Faasta CLI:
cargo install cargo-faasta
Create a new Faasta project:
cargo faasta init
#
or
cargo faasta new my-function
Build your function for WebAssembly:
cargo faasta build
Login with your GitHub account:
cargo faasta login
Deploy your function:
cargo faasta deploy
Your function will be available at
https://your-function-name.faasta.xyz
WASI P2 and WASIHTTP
Faasta implements the WebAssembly System Interface (WASI) Preview 2 specification and the WASIHTTP standard to enable:
Standardized HTTP request and response handling
Component-based architecture for better modularity
Consistent interface for interacting with the host system
Portable functions that can run on any WASI P2 compatible runtime
Because Faasta uses these open standards, your functions are not locked to a specific platform and can be hosted anywhere that supports these standards.
Self-Hosting
Faasta is fully self-hostable. You can run your own instance of the Faasta server to host your functions on your own infrastructure.
⚠️
Experimental Status
Faasta is currently experimental. There will be breaking changes that will interupt service on the faasta.xyz instance.

data.title: Some __nonstring__ Turbulence
data.author: jwilk
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了Linux内核开发中因新编译器版本引入新警告而引发的问题。GCC 15引入的`-Wunterminated-string-initialization`警告旨在提醒开发者未终止的字符串初始化问题，但某些情况下，开发者故意不使用终止符（NUL），如在查找表中。新警告导致了编译问题，尤其是在Fedora 42提前搭载GCC 15预发布版后，Linus Torvalds升级系统并发现内核编译出错。由于部分修复补丁未及时合并，Torvalds在发布6.15-rc3前做了紧急修改，却导致在旧版GCC上编译失败。最终，他撤回了这些更改并禁用了新警告。开发者Kees Cook对问题的处理方式提出异议，指出他已提供了解决方案。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕Linux内核开发中使用测试版编译器及C语言中NUL终止字符串的讨论，涉及技术选择、开发者行为和代码安全等问题。

不同观点：
• [AceJohnny2] 和 [jaapz] 认为Linus Torvalds在此次事件中不应责备内核维护者，反而应该承认自己的错误。AceJohnny2特别指出Torvalds在未仔细审查的情况下进行了更改，并批评Fedora在新版本中使用测试版编译器。jaapz则认为Torvalds通常对维护者的批评是有理由的，但这次他应该承认错误。

• [Ukv] 质疑C语言中NUL终止字符串的设计选择，认为这种设计导致了许多问题，如字符串操作效率低、无法处理包含NUL的数据、以及潜在的安全问题。Ukv认为NUL终止字符串可能是一个不幸的设计选择，而非特性。

• [Philpax] 批评Linus Torvalds的行为，并质疑在C语言开发中为何使用字符串而不是字节数组或字面量。Philpax认为这可能是更合适的选择。

• [Incipient] 对为何在RC阶段没有发现使用测试版编译器的问题感到困惑，并提出RC版本应该通过所有官方编译器和架构的测试才能发布。

• [jey] 讨论了C语言变量初始化的问题，认为在char数组中忽略NUL终止符是错误的。bjourne对此表示赞同，并强调了C语言初学者应遵循的变量赋值规则。

• [mastax] 惊讶于Linux内核没有官方的持续集成（CI）系统，暗示这可能有助于避免类似问题。

补充讨论：
• 关于C语言中NUL终止字符串的争议是讨论的一个重点，涉及其效率和安全性问题。
• 对Linus Torvalds在事件中的行为存在批评，部分评论者认为他应为错误决定承担责任。
• 评论还涉及开发流程中的技术选择和测试实践，如使用测试版工具的合理性和RC版本的测试标准。

争议焦点：
• Linus Torvalds是否应为此次事件中的错误承担责任并承认错误。
• C语言中NUL终止字符串的设计是否合理，以及是否有更好的替代方案。

The following subscription-only content has been made available to you
by an LWN subscriber.  Thousands of subscribers depend on LWN for the
best news from the Linux and free software communities.  If you enjoy this

By
Jonathan Corbet
April 24, 2025
New compiler releases often bring with them new warnings; those warnings
are usually welcome, since they help developers find problems before they
turn into nasty bugs.  Adapting to new warnings can also create disruption
in the development process, though, especially when an important developer
upgrades to a new compiler at an unfortunate time.  This is just the
scenario that played out with the
6.15-rc3
kernel release
and the implementation of
-Wunterminated-string-initialization
in GCC 15.
Consider a C declaration like:
char foo[8] = "bar";
The array will be initialized with the given string, including the normal
trailing NUL byte indicating the end of the string.  Now consider this
variant:
char foo[8] = "NUL-free";
This is a legal declaration, even though the declared array now lacks the
room for the NUL byte.  That byte will simply be omitted, creating an
unterminated string.  That is often not what the developer who wrote that
code wants, and it can lead to unpleasant bugs that are not discovered
until some later time.  The
-Wunterminated-string-initialization
option emits a warning for this kind of initialization, with the result
that, hopefully, the problem — if there is a problem — is fixed quickly.
The kernel community has worked to make use of this warning and, hopefully,
eliminate a source of bugs.  There is only one little problem with the new
warning, though: sometimes the no-NUL initialization is exactly what is
wanted and intended.  See, for example,
this
declaration
from
fs/cachefiles/key.c
:
static const char cachefiles_charmap[64] =
"0123456789"			/* 0 - 9 */
"abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz"	/* 10 - 35 */
"ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ"	/* 36 - 61 */
"_-"				/* 62 - 63 */
;
This
char
array is used as a lookup table, not as a string, so
there is no need for a trailing NUL byte.  GCC 15, being unaware of
that usage, will emit a false-positive warning for this declaration.  There
are many places in the kernel with declarations like this; the ACPI code,
for example, uses a lot of four-byte string arrays to handle the equally
large set of four-letter ACPI acronyms.
Naturally, there is a way to suppress the warning when it does not apply
by adding an attribute to the declaration indicating that the
char
array is not actually holding a string:
__attribute__((__nonstring__))
Within the kernel, the macro
__nonstring
is used to shorten that
attribute syntax.  Work has been ongoing, primarily by Kees Cook, to fix
all of the warnings added by GCC 15.  Many patches have been
circulated; quite a few of them are in linux-next.  Cook has also been
working with the GCC developers to improve how this annotation works and to
fix a
problem
that the kernel project ran into.  There was some time left
to get this job done, though, since GCC 15 has not actually been
released — or so Cook thought.
Fedora 42
has
been released, though, and the Fedora developers, for
better or worse, decided to include a pre-release version of GCC 15
with it as the default compiler.  The Fedora project, it seems, has decided
to follow
a venerable Red Hat tradition
with this release.  Linus Torvalds, for better or worse,
decided to update his development systems to Fedora 42 the day before
tagging and releasing 6.15-rc3.  Once he tried building the kernel with the
new compiler, though, things started to go wrong, since the relevant
patches were not yet in his repository.  Torvalds responded with a series
of changes of his own, applied directly to the mainline about two hours
before the release, to fix the problems that he had encountered.  They
included
this patch
fixing warnings in the ACPI subsystem, and
this one
fixing
several others, including the example shown above.  He then tagged and
pushed out 6.15-rc3 with those changes.
Unfortunately, his last-minute changes broke the build on any version of
GCC prior to the GCC 15 pre-release — a problem that was likely to
create a certain amount of inconvenience for any developers who were not
running Fedora 42.  So, shortly after the 6.15-rc3 release, Torvalds
tacked on
one more
patch
backing out the breaking change and disabling the new warning
altogether.
This drew
a somewhat
grumpy note
from Cook, who said that he had already sent patches fixing
all of the problems, including the build-breaking one that Torvalds ran
into.  He asked Torvalds to revert the changes and use the planned fixes,
adding: "

• 对Linus Torvalds在事件中的行为存在批评，部分评论者认为他应为错误决定承担责任。
• 评论还涉及开发流程中的技术选择和测试实践，如使用测试版工具的合理性和RC版本的测试标准。

争议焦点：
• Linus Torvalds是否应为此次事件中的错误承担责任并承认错误。
• C语言中NUL终止字符串的设计是否合理，以及是否有更好的替代方案。

data.article_summary: GCC 15.1已于2025年4月25日发布，是GNU编译器集合的重大更新版本，包含新功能及多项改进。GCC最初代表GNU C Compiler，但现在支持多种编程语言。此次发布感谢了众多贡献者，他们是GCC成功的重要支持者。更多信息可访问GCC项目网站或联系开发邮件列表。获取GCC可通过镜像站点或版本控制系统。使用问题可查阅GCC手册或联系帮助邮箱。反馈欢迎发送至开发者列表。本文可自由复制，但需保留版权声明。页面由GCC团队维护。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：C/C++语言标准及编译器行为的变化、新特性支持、对具体改进内容的需求

不同观点：
• Calavar指出，在C/C++中，union的`{0}`初始化器不再保证清零整个union（静态存储期除外），而只是将union的第一个成员初始化为零。他认为这将悄无声息地破坏现有代码，尤其是基于union的类型变换（type punning）。他建议为了兼容旧代码，应该让`{0}`和`{}`都对整个union进行零初始化，并对当前情况的反转表示困惑。

• Omoikane则对C语言中`#embed`预处理指令的支持感到兴奋，并提供了相关讨论链接，显示出对新特性的积极态度。

• Elvircrn对C++模块的所谓“巨大改进”表示疑问，希望能具体了解这些改进到底是什么。

• Codr7对musttail特性的即将实现表示期待。

• Pjmlp提到Modula-2前端的改进也值得关注，显示出对多语言前端进展的兴趣。

• Fithisux则表达了对HaikuOS和Winlibs支持的希望，尤其是对GDC（GNU Compiler Collection的D语言前端）的支持。

补充讨论：
• Calavar对编译器行为变化的担忧，尤其是对现有代码的潜在影响，与其他评论者对新特性的期待形成了对比。
• 对C++模块改进内容的具体需求（elvircrn）和Modula-2前端进展的兴趣（pjmlp）显示出社区对不同语言和特性的关注。
• Fithisux的需求（HaikuOS和Winlibs的支持）则反映了对特定平台和工具链支持的期望。

争议焦点：
• Calavar提出的编译器行为变化可能导致现有代码的兼容性问题，这是争议的核心，尤其是如何平衡新特性引入和旧代码兼容性。

data.title: Petition to the Open Source Initiative: Publish the Full 2025 Election Results
data.author: richardfontana
data.article_summary: 这篇文章是一份要求开放源代码促进会（OSI）公布2025年董事会选举完整结果的请愿书。请愿者对OSI在选举后移除部分候选人选票并公布修改后的结果表示担忧，认为此举损害了OSI的公信力。具体来说，OSI在2025年选举后排除了三名候选人的选票，其中包括主张改革的Bradley Kuhn和Richard Fontana。请愿者指出，选举规则在过程中被改变，且结果被修改，这破坏了选举的公正性。他们呼吁OSI以透明方式公布完整、未经修改的选举结果，以恢复其 integrity 和声誉。请愿书强调透明度对OSI的健康发展至关重要，不涉及对特定候选人或政策立场的支持。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：开放源代码和开放源代码促进会（OSI）的定位与作用，特别是在企业影响下的演变和争议。

不同观点：
• **tedivm的观点**：认为开放源代码AI定义（OSAID）是对开放源代码社区的背叛。其主要论据是允许公司重新定义“开放”，以包括封闭组件，违背了OSI应该代表的理念。批评这是为了让大公司将其封闭模型伪装成开放。

• **remon的观点**：对OSI的实际作用提出疑问。作为多个开源项目的参与者，remon表示在合规、治理、教育等方面从未见到OSI被提及，质疑其存在的影响力。

• **lolinder的观点**：回顾OSI的成立背景，指出其初衷是作为企业友好的替代方案，以替代斯塔尔曼的自由软件基金会（FSF）。lolinder认为，OSI的演变是将“自由软件”的道德框架淡化，以更迎合企业的商业利益。lolinder主张，要解决自由和开源软件（FOSS）运动中的问题，需要摆脱企业影响，回归以道德为基础的自由软件运动，并指出GPL和AGPL许可证是少数未被企业利益吞噬的许可证，因为它们基于深厚的伦理原则。

补充讨论：
• **争议的焦点**：OSI是否应该允许公司将封闭组件定义为开放，以及其在现代开源和自由软件运动中的角色和影响力。tedivm和lolinder明显反对企业对开源定义的影响，而remon则对OSI的存在和作用提出质疑。

• **历史背景**：lolinder提供了OSI成立时的背景信息，强调其从一开始就是作为企业友好选项，与自由软件基金会的道德立场形成对比。这一历史视角为当前的争议提供了背景支持。

• **许可证讨论**：lolinder特别提到GPL和AGPL许可证，认为它们是少数未被企业利益影响的许可证，强调其基于伦理原则，与开放源代码的商业化趋势形成对比。

README.md
Petition to the Open Source Initiative: Publish the Full 2025 Election Results
We, the undersigned, petition the Open Source Initiative
(OSI) to release the complete, unaltered results of its 2025 Board of
Directors elections
. We believe that by removing candidates and votes
after
voting concluded, OSI has damaged its credibility.
We call for transparency as a first step toward repairing
OSI's integrity and reputation.
Background context
OSI relies entirely on community deference and respect
for its authority in promoting Open Source and the
consistent use of the term "Open Source."
In 2012, OSI shifted toward operating as a member-driven organization.
Every year since 2013, OSI has held elections where Individual and Affiliate members
vote on directors to represent them.
Although OSI is not legally bound to accept the results,
the elections have been a key part of community and membership engagement,
and OSI has always worked to follow best practices for public elections.
Until 2025, OSI has published the full results of elections.
2025 election
In 2025, OSI excluded all votes for three candidates before publishing results.
The announcement of the
altered voting results
did not name the removed candidates, but they were Bentley Hensel,
Bradley Kuhn, and Richard Fontana (incidentally, a former OSI director).
Notably, Kuhn and Fontana campaigned on a joint
OSI Reform platform
which included four proposals, the most significant being a call to repeal
the newly-adopted Open Source AI Definition (OSAID).
They also advocated for revising the
OSI Board Member Agreement
,
because they interpreted the clause requiring members to "support publicly all Board
decisions" as being overly expansive and stifling. They proposed clarifying or
limiting the clause to achieve a better balance.
Normally, as in prior years, as with other organizations, and as stated during
candidate orientation, signing of the Board Agreement would happen only
with the election winners as part of getting seated as new directors.
Kuhn and Fontana say that they brought up their concerns about the Agreement
during candidate orientation and came away with the understanding that they
would be able to discuss how to resolve the issue later if they won the election.
Then,
about one hour after voting ended, OSI emailed a
new
requirement
to the 11 non-incumbent candidates. They gave a 47-hour deadline for all to
sign the board member agreement or be disqualified.
Hensel missed the deadline simply by not checking his email soon enough.
Having no chance to otherwise resolve or discuss their agreement
concerns, Fontana and Kuhn returned signed board member agreements that included
their proposed changes. OSI then published the announcement which
excluded all votes for the three candidates.
Ramifications
In general, changing election rules mid-process and altering vote counts
undermines the integrity of any election.
Results must be published transparently — regardless of whether a
candidate withdraws, dies, or is disqualified for any reason. Once a
candidate appears on the ballot, the only way to respect voters is to
count and report the votes as cast. Presenting altered voting results
misrepresents
and disrespects the electorate.
Regardless of particular concerns about the Board Agreement, for the
current OSI Board to remove critical candidates while hiding
the voting results presents a clear conflict of interest and invites
community speculation about motives and corruption. As
LWN
OSI election coverage
noted, "a cynical person might conclude that the last-minute
requirement to sign the agreement was to disqualify one or both because
they would have won otherwise; and that the OSI leadership was unwilling
to have even a minority number of board members who might seek to steer
the ship in a different direction."
Call for resolution
We are community members who care deeply about OSI’s mission.
We want to see OSI governed with integrity and transparency.
This petition does not endorse particular candidates or policy positions.
We believe that everyone should care about transparency

data.title: Privacy folks – what's your take on using LLMs at work?
data.author: adeebaslam
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：大型语言模型（LLM）在处理公共和私有数据时的隐私与安全问题，以及是否应依赖专有模型或本地模型。

不同观点：
• [whs] 认为只应使用LLM搜索公共信息，不应用其处理专有数据。同时，他对模型训练数据中包含其代码表示不满，认为这违反了版权，特别是在未遵循相关许可的情况下。
• [gbraad] 不信任将代理（agent）用于处理客户代码或个人身份信息（PII）。他选择在虚拟机或容器中运行代码，以避免本地激活相关工具。
• [bnolsen] 建议可以在本地运行LLM，但要注意版权问题。他批评依赖专有工具提升技能的做法，认为这是LLM提供商为了收回投资而采取的策略。
• [AaronAPU] 对隐私保护持怀疑态度，尤其不信任自称为“隐私AI”的公司。
• [mvieira38] 表示已经放弃完全保护隐私的努力，选择使用ChatGPT并接受其隐私设置，尽管不完全信任它们。
• [jart] 推荐使用本地运行且保护隐私的LLM，如Mozilla的llamafile。
• [HelloUsername] 没有直接回答问题，但提供了一个可能相关的链接供参考。
• [rabid_turtle] 表示只会在LLM中输入可以公开的信息，不担心LLM知道其正在进行的编码项目。
• [hengheng] 质疑云服务在隐私方面与本地服务的竞争，暗示云服务可能成为“蜜罐”（吸引攻击的目标）。
• [underseacables] 提到曾询问LLM是否会保护其数据隐私，LLM给出了肯定的回答，但对其可信度表示不确定。
• [fortyseven] 避免使用云服务，只在本地运行LLM，除非像GitHub Copilot这样由雇主支付且早期就使用的工具。
• [axegon_] 对法国公司Mistral持相对信任态度，因为其需遵守GDPR。总体上更倾向于本地运行LLM，认为数据若需联网处理，便不再完全属于自己。
• [rhabarba] 对使用LLM持否定态度，尤其在工作环境中，建议不要使用。

补充讨论：
- 争议焦点在于是否信任LLM提供商对隐私的保护，尤其是当模型用于处理专有代码或敏感信息时。
- 一些用户（如gbraad、fortyseven）更倾向于在本地或受控环境中运行LLM，以避免隐私泄露。
- 版权问题也被提及，尤其是当用户的代码被包含在训练数据中而未遵循相关许可时。
- 对云服务和本地运行的LLM在隐私保护方面的优劣存在不同看法。

• [HelloUsername] 没有直接回答问题，但提供了一个可能相关的链接供参考。
• [rabid_turtle] 表示只会在LLM中输入可以公开的信息，不担心LLM知道其正在进行的编码项目。
• [hengheng] 质疑云服务在隐私方面与本地服务的竞争，暗示云服务可能成为“蜜罐”（吸引攻击的目标）。
• [underseacables] 提到曾询问LLM是否会保护其数据隐私，LLM给出了肯定的回答，但对其可信度表示不确定。
• [fortyseven] 避免使用云服务，只在本地运行LLM，除非像GitHub Copilot这样由雇主支付且早期就使用的工具。
• [axegon_] 对法国公司Mistral持相对信任态度，因为其需遵守GDPR。总体上更倾向于本地运行LLM，认为数据若需联网处理，便不再完全属于自己。
• [rhabarba] 对使用LLM持否定态度，尤其在工作环境中，建议不要使用。

补充讨论：
- 争议焦点在于是否信任LLM提供商对隐私的保护，尤其是当模型用于处理专有代码或敏感信息时。
- 一些用户（如gbraad、fortyseven）更倾向于在本地或受控环境中运行LLM，以避免隐私泄露。
- 版权问题也被提及，尤其是当用户的代码被包含在训练数据中而未遵循相关许可时。
- 对云服务和本地运行的LLM在隐私保护方面的优劣存在不同看法。

The $20,000 American-made electric pickup with no paint, no stereo, and no touchscreen
﻿Is the market ready for a four-wheeled digital detox?
by
Tim Stevens

Link
Facebook
Threads
Ask just about anybody, and they’ll tell you that new cars are too expensive. In the wake of tariffs
shaking the auto industry
and with the Trump administration pledging to
kill the federal EV incentive
, that situation isn’t looking to get better soon, especially for anyone wanting something battery-powered. Changing that overly spendy status quo is going to take something radical, and it’s hard to get more radical than what Slate Auto has planned.
Meet the Slate Truck, a sub-$20,000 (after federal incentives) electric vehicle that enters production next year. It only seats two yet has a bed big enough to hold a sheet of plywood. It only does 150 miles on a charge, only comes in gray, and the only way to listen to music while driving is if you bring along your phone and a Bluetooth speaker. It is the bare minimum of what a modern car can be, and yet it’s taken three years of development to get to this point.
But this is more than bargain-basement motoring. Slate is presenting its truck as minimalist design with DIY purpose, an attempt to not just go cheap but to create a new category of vehicle with a huge focus on personalization. That design also enables a low-cost approach to manufacturing that has caught the eye of major investors, reportedly including Jeff Bezos. It’s been engineered and will be manufactured in America, but is this extreme simplification too much for American consumers?
Simplify, Then Embrace Damage
If you haven’t seen the leaks and the reports of weirdly wrapped trucks
hiding in plain sight
, the Slate Truck is the first product from Michigan-based Slate Auto. Think “American kei truck” and you’re not far off. It’s a machine designed to be extremely basic, extremely customizable, and extremely affordable. Those are not your typical design goals, but then the Slate Truck isn’t the fruit of your typical design process.
Wander through any automotive design studio anywhere in the world and you’ll inevitably come across a mood board or two, sweeping collages of striking photos meant to align the creative flows of passers-by. They’re a tool for helping a disparate design team to create a cohesive product, but where many such mood boards feature glamour shots of exotic roads and beautiful people, front and center in the Slate’s mood board was something different: a big, gray shark, covered in scrapes and scars.
“It looks like a shark that has definitely been in more than one brawl and clearly has come out ahead because it’s still swimming,” says Tisha Johnson, head of design at Slate and who formerly spent a decade at Volvo. That aesthetic, of highlighting rather than hiding battle scars, is key to the Slate ethos.
Instead of steel or aluminum, the Slate Truck’s body panels are molded of plastic. Or, as Slate calls them, “injection molded polypropylene composite material.” The theory is that this makes them more durable and scratch-resistant, if only because the lack of paint means they’re one color all the way through. Auto enthusiasts of a certain age will remember the same approach used by the now-defunct Saturn Corporation, a manufacturing technique that never caught on across the industry.
Slate continues the theme through to the upholstery, too, a heathered textile that was designed to get better looking as it wears. The idea is to lean into the aged aesthetic.
But not everybody will dig the shark theme, and so the Slate Truck is designed to be customizable to a degree never seen before on a production vehicle. Johnson says this is in contrast to the overly curated experience offered by many brands.
She says over-curation by automotive designers results in situations like premium, luxury cars that are only available in a palette of disappointingly bland colors: “There’s usually only a fraction that you actually want, and those are always more expensive,” she says.
Disparaging other brands for offering limited color choices might seem disingenuous coming from the designer of a vehicle available in a single shade. The Slate Truck, though, was designed to take advantage of the current trend of
vinyl-wrapping cars
. Its simple shape and minimal trim pieces mean that even amateurs can do the job. Slate will offer DIY kits that newbies can slap on in an afternoon and replace just as quickly based on mood.
However, the biggest benefit of this monochromatic thinking might come in production.

data.title: Eurorack Knob Idea
data.author: po
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一种创新的Eurorack模块旋钮设计，旨在解决因空间限制而导致的模块面板混乱问题。作者与Dave Cranmer合作，设计了一个结合3.5mm插头和磁编码器（AS5600）的旋钮，通过磁铁将插头变为旋钮和接线插头的混合体。作者详细描述了制作过程，包括切割插头、嵌入磁铁、3D打印填充件以及电路设计和组装步骤。最终设计使用I2C接口读取角度数据，并可通过PWM或DAC输出模拟电压。整个设计经过多次实验和调整，最终成功实现预期功能，为Eurorack模块提供了更整洁的面板解决方案。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：模块化合成器的设计与用户界面创新，特别是关于旋钮与接口插孔的功能组合以及成本控制问题。

不同观点：
• **支持复杂设计（bondarchuk, dimal, JKCalhoun 部分观点）**：bondarchuk 提到理想的设计是旋钮与插孔结合，当插入电缆时，旋钮变成输入的衰减器，否则作为独立旋钮使用。dimal 进一步指出最好的模块已经具备这种功能，并且 Eurorack 的魅力在于插拔线缆的直观操作。

• **简化与低成本设计（smj-edison, dylan604, JKCalhoun 部分观点）**：smj-edison 提出通过减少物理旋钮，用旋钮编码器和按钮组合来大幅降低成本，尽管操作体验不如专用旋钮。dylan604 则认为这种设计虽然昂贵，但对不同经济能力的用户有不同影响。JKCalhoun 认为很多音乐人追求的是简化而非复杂的模块化系统，更倾向于少量但高质量的旋钮设计。

• **技术与实践可行性（joemi, arnorhs, diggan）**：joemi 认为讨论的设计只是解决了表面问题，实际问题是模块设计者或用户过度追求小型化。arnorhs 进一步指出该设计虽然有趣，但实际应用可能受限，特别是与其他模块的兼容性问题。diggan 则关注实际操作手感，担心快速且精确的操作在这种设计中难以实现，并提出可配置阻力的想法。

• **创新与扩展（alnwlsn, csours, buescher）**：alnwlsn 提到可以加入加速度计、MCU等创新设计，提升功能性。csours 则激进地建议扩展到多维度控制器设计，甚至结合线性滑动器。buescher 对这种创新表示赞赏，但质疑其是否真正解决了实际问题，认为创新需要持续推进。

补充讨论：
• **移动端音频设计（m_kos）**：m_kos 提出了移动端软件合成器的设计挑战，特别是旋钮与滑块的用户体验问题，并寻求设计指南。

• **视觉与表达方式（jimbokun, d--b）**：jimbokun 赞赏视频中通过手势和视觉辅助解释设计，认为这种表达方式非常有效。d--b 则以幽默方式将模块化合成器设计与函数式编程概念联系起来。

争议焦点：
• 主要争议在于复杂性与简化设计的平衡，以及用户体验与成本之间的取舍。支持复杂设计的人强调功能性和操作直观性，而支持简化设计的人则关注成本与操作简便性。

43793288.article_content:
Eurorack Knob Idea
24 Apr 2025
Progress: Complete
Last year I designed a eurorack module, as a collaboration with Dave Cranmer. When I say designed it, I mean we got about 90% of the way there, then got distracted. With any luck, that module will get finished and released sometime soon.
But it had me thinking about Eurorack and the weird compromises people often make to fit more and more modules into a tiny case. I know a thing or two about tiny synthesizers. But my creations are often whimsical and useless. When it comes to Eurorack, where people spend crazy amounts of money on their setups, it's weird to see people compromise on the main aspect that gives it an edge over simulating the whole thing in software.
To clean up our Eurorack panels, perhaps we need a new knob idea? Watch the following video for a prototypical demo.
In essence, we're using a 3.5mm jack in front of a magnetic encoder chip, and a small magnet embedded in the plug turns it into a knob and patch cable hybrid.
The magnetic encoder in question is an AS5600. These are not the cheapest parts but they do make prototyping very easy. It has two hall sensors in an XY configuration and a dollop of DSP to give us an angle and a magnitude. They're easily available on breakout boards and have an i2c interface.
The board also comes with a specially polarised magnet with the field across the diameter instead of axially. We're not going to use that.
Building the knob
I started by taking a dremel cutting disk to the end of a TRS plug. This was just done by eye. Edge-on, it's not quite centred but it'll work fine.
This cheap plug is in fact partially hollow, and is made from plated brass.
Into this slot I glued a small neodymium magnet. It's 2mm diameter, 1mm thickness. I also bought some 2mm thickness magnets, but that would need a slightly wider slot, which would probably require a more precise cutting method.
I used a medium viscosity cyanoacrylate glue. Once set, the excess can be scraped away with a razor blade.
I turned away the threaded section, trimmed the metal tab, and 3D printed a filler piece so the back of the plug is just a straight cylinder to which we can fit a knob.
And to that, we fitted the knob. The 3D printed plastic is quite pliable, so the set screw embeds itself a little and gets a solid grip.
Circuit design
I was unsure if the tiny magnet would be sufficient, and how close it would need to be held to the soic-8 sensor chip. I did some tests, just holding this magnetic knob over one of the breakout boards.
There's both a PWM output and a DAC on the AS5600, with the idea that we can use it, once configured, to output an analog voltage. I had a assumed there was some zero-config mode that would just turn magnetic fields into voltages, but it seems we need to set it up via i2c to get any output. If that's the case, for the sake of this test we might as well just read out the angle via i2c as well.
After a few experiments I was convinced it was going to work, so I set about building a circuit board that could house the AS5600 under a TRS socket.
A common style of vertical-mount TRS socket looks like this (I believe it's a PJ398SM):
With our magnetic knob fitted, we can see that there's almost zero clearance between the tip of the TRS plug and the plane of the circuit board.
There might be a vertical-mount TRS jack out there somewhere that has enough clearance underneath it, but the through-mount pins are long enough here that we can just lift up the socket off the board. I considered 3D printing or laser-cutting a frame to elevate it, but better still is to use PCB material (FR4) as we can tack it onto the same circuit board order.
The height of the AS5600 is about 1.47mm; a 1.6mm board will work nicely. There are some diagrams in the datasheet illustrating how the magnet should be situated relative to the chip.
I stacked the two part footprints, and then laid out a second version of the socket footprint with a cutout for the chip.
I like to model the board outline exactly, with a 2mm endmill in mind, it makes it explicitly clear what we expect to receive from the board house. If you specify tight inside corners, they will probably use their judgement as to how tight a corner you were expecting. Drawing these out in KiCad is a bit tedious, but at this point I'm used to it.
I optimistically added a CH32V003 and a bunch of LEDs so we can show the value. I also chucked the usual clamping diodes and ~100K input impedance, made of 33K and 66K resistors, which divide a 0-5V signal down to 0-3.3V.
Since the encoder chip will be buried, I also added pads underneath so that if it comes to it, we can probe any leg of the chip.
The design was blasted off to China and a short while later the boards were in my hands.
Assembly and test
Assembly was uneventful. I was especially careful to get the AS5600 perfectly centred on the pads.

主要讨论点：模块化合成器的设计与用户界面创新，特别是关于旋钮与接口插孔的功能组合以及成本控制问题。

不同观点：
• **支持复杂设计（bondarchuk, dimal, JKCalhoun 部分观点）**：bondarchuk 提到理想的设计是旋钮与插孔结合，当插入电缆时，旋钮变成输入的衰减器，否则作为独立旋钮使用。dimal 进一步指出最好的模块已经具备这种功能，并且 Eurorack 的魅力在于插拔线缆的直观操作。

• **简化与低成本设计（smj-edison, dylan604, JKCalhoun 部分观点）**：smj-edison 提出通过减少物理旋钮，用旋钮编码器和按钮组合来大幅降低成本，尽管操作体验不如专用旋钮。dylan604 则认为这种设计虽然昂贵，但对不同经济能力的用户有不同影响。JKCalhoun 认为很多音乐人追求的是简化而非复杂的模块化系统，更倾向于少量但高质量的旋钮设计。

• **技术与实践可行性（joemi, arnorhs, diggan）**：joemi 认为讨论的设计只是解决了表面问题，实际问题是模块设计者或用户过度追求小型化。arnorhs 进一步指出该设计虽然有趣，但实际应用可能受限，特别是与其他模块的兼容性问题。diggan 则关注实际操作手感，担心快速且精确的操作在这种设计中难以实现，并提出可配置阻力的想法。

• **创新与扩展（alnwlsn, csours, buescher）**：alnwlsn 提到可以加入加速度计、MCU等创新设计，提升功能性。csours 则激进地建议扩展到多维度控制器设计，甚至结合线性滑动器。buescher 对这种创新表示赞赏，但质疑其是否真正解决了实际问题，认为创新需要持续推进。

补充讨论：
• **移动端音频设计（m_kos）**：m_kos 提出了移动端软件合成器的设计挑战，特别是旋钮与滑块的用户体验问题，并寻求设计指南。

• **视觉与表达方式（jimbokun, d--b）**：jimbokun 赞赏视频中通过手势和视觉辅助解释设计，认为这种表达方式非常有效。d--b 则以幽默方式将模块化合成器设计与函数式编程概念联系起来。

争议焦点：
• 主要争议在于复杂性与简化设计的平衡，以及用户体验与成本之间的取舍。支持复杂设计的人强调功能性和操作直观性，而支持简化设计的人则关注成本与操作简便性。

data.title: A Love Letter to People Who Believe in People
data.author: NaOH
data.article_summary: 本文讲述了作者Tina对热情力量的深刻体会。从八岁时制作“粉丝俱乐部”海报，到成年后在生活和工作中遇到的几位关键人物，她意识到热情能改变人生。她的 eccentric 姨妈Hugi教会她勇敢、创意生活；她的首任老板Matthew Waldman让她明白工作环境可以充满关爱；女儿Ella的出生激励她创立自己的设计工作室；Jim Coudal让她相信自己也能实现创意想法。Tina受热情驱使，创立了Coworking空间Studiomates和晨间创意讲座CreativeMornings，通过这些社区活动，她与志同道合的人相互激励、共同成长。热情不仅改变了她自己，也影响了周围的人。

43788255.article_content:
Tina on the transformative power of enthusiasm
When I was eight, I made a big, hand-drawn poster that said, “Do you want to join my fan club?” and put it up in the small Swiss town where I grew up.
Neighbors would ask me, “What are we going to be fans of?” and I’d say, “It doesn’t matter—it’s just about being excited.” Eight year old Tina.
Decades later, I’m still convinced that being a fan is a state of mind.
Being a fan is all about bringing the enthusiasm. It’s being a champion of possibility. It’s believing in someone. And it’s contagious. When you’re around someone who is super excited about something, it washes over you. It feels good. You can’t help but want to bring the enthusiasm, too.
This, to me, is the real transformation. Confidence is impressive, but enthusiasm can change people’s lives.
If I trace all the defining moments of my life back to their beginnings, I can always find a person with this fan state of mind: someone who believed in me, opened a door, or illuminated a new path just by being who they are.
This is a love letter to all the people who believe in us and nudge us in new directions with their enthusiasm.
To the person who showed me you can live life your way—my beloved, eccentric Aunt Hugi
She was the most creative, unique, stubborn, wild Swiss woman I have ever known. I grew up in the Swiss countryside and visiting Hugi in Zurich was always an adventure. She was a fashion designer, artist, and a true original. As I got older, I really started to appreciate how she didn’t care what people thought. She lived a courageous, creative life and inspired me to be bold, forge my own path, and break rules.
To the person who opened up a different future—my first boss, Matthew Waldman
After I earned my graphic design degree, I convinced my parents that I wanted to go to New York to find a three-month internship. I arrived on a Monday night and had an interview lined up the next morning with Matthew Waldman—the CEO of a small, now defunct design studio. Within five minutes of talking to me, he offered me a job and predicted that I would never leave New York.
Not only was he right, but his instant belief in me taught me that your boss can be enthusiastic, kind, and caring. This set the tone going forward—I would not accept anything other than a loving work environment.
To the person who nudged me to ask myself, “What am I waiting for?”—my daughter Ella
While working as a Design Director at a digital agency and pregnant with my daughter Ella, I found myself inspired to think bigger. I always wanted to run my own design studio and an urgency suddenly hit me—I was making a human, and I wanted to be a role model to them, so what was I waiting for? I started my own design studio the day she was born.
To the person who helped me realise “I can do this too”—the inspiring Jim Coudal
My blog swissmiss became quite popular, but when I had other ideas, I’d second-guess them. I’d think, Who am I to do this thing? A real epiphany came when I was watching Jim Coudal at SXSW. As he was describing his fun side projects, including The Deck Network, Layer Tennis, and Field Notes, I realized I could put my ideas into the world, too. Seeing someone create the things they want to create can give us permission to do the same.
So I did it. I knew intuitively that the people you surround yourself with change what you dream about, which led me to start the coworking space Studiomates (now known as Friends Work Here). It has been magical to see what unfolds when you gather creative, kind, driven humans in a physical space. We often find ourselves in deep, engaging conversations over coffee or lunch, which in turn has led to the founding of multiple companies, magazines and conferences. We believe in each other, and we make each other brave.
To the person who encouraged the momentum of CreativeMornings—co-founder of Mailchimp, Ben Chestnut
After experiencing the power of my coworking community, I felt inspired to share the magic. I was in a city of eight million people, but the creative communities felt fragmented and disconnected. I knew there had to be more heart-centered, creative people looking to connect. So, I decided to invite people to the space for a free breakfast and a talk. I vividly remember being made fun of for inviting people to an event at 8:30 a.m., and assuming no one would show up. I am proud to say we had 50 attendees at the first ever CreativeMornings in October of 2008.
Just four months and four events later, I received an email from Ben Chestnut, co-founder of Mailchimp, saying he and his team were big fans and he wondered if they could sponsor future events. I had never dealt with sponsors before and clumsily invited them to pay for breakfast, which turned into the most supportive and encouraging 15-year corporate partnership and friendship.

data.title: Exploiting Undefined Behavior in C/C++ Programs: The Performance Impact [pdf]
data.author: luu
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于未定义行为（UB）对编译器优化和性能的影响，尤其是在链接时优化（LTO）场景下的表现和相关争议。

不同观点：
• **nikic的观点**：  
  - 禁用个别UB在无LTO时通常会降低性能，但在有LTO时却能提升性能，这一现象在基准测试结果中表现一致。  
  - 提到不同UB之间存在协同效应，单独禁用每个UB可能带来中性或正面效果，但同时禁用所有UB则会导致显著性能下降。  
  - 对论文未解释这一效应表示疑惑。

• **pcwalton的观点**：  
  - 指出论文并未声称消除所有与UB相关的优化，例如某些优化仍依赖于未定义行为（如对数组越界的利用）。  
  - 不同意论文中关于其语义提供“平坦内存模型”的说法，认为该模型仍保留了对象边界的概念，只是有所简化。  
  - 提出所谓的“不可防护UB”概念，并通过示例代码说明编译器如何依赖UB进行优化。

• **mwkaufma的观点**：  
  - 提到通过LTO可以恢复禁用UB导致的性能损失，但对“可以”（can）实现的优化表示担忧，认为很难保证优化“将会”（will）被应用。  
  - 暗示依赖LTO等间接效应来保证优化效果可能不太可靠，容易出问题。

• **gitroom的观点**：  
  - 提出团队可能因为构建过程的痛苦或对工具链的不信任而避免使用LTO等优化。  
  - 质疑开发者是否愿意为了最终产品的更高速度而忍受缓慢的构建过程。

• **jonstewart的观点**：  
  - 赞同论文结论，认为利用UB带来的性能提升在评估的案例中微乎其微，且通过小幅修改编译器或使用LTO可以恢复性能损失。

补充讨论：
- **争议焦点**：UB在不同场景下对性能的影响，以及是否应依赖LTO等复杂优化手段。  
- **nikic和pcwalton的分歧**：nikic对UB禁用效果与LTO协同效应的困惑，pcwalton则关注UB在特定优化中的不可或缺性及其对内存模型的影响。  
- **mwkaufma对LTO优化的怀疑**：担心LTO优化的可靠性，认为不能完全依赖其间接效果。  
- **gitroom对开发者行为的讨论**：提出构建过程中的实际问题和信任问题，可能影响优化手段的采用。
