data.title: Century-old genetics mystery of Mendel's peas solved
data.author: Brajeshwar
data.article_summary: 文章总结了科学家们如何解开格雷戈尔·孟德尔160多年前在豌豆实验中未解的三个遗传性状的基因谜题。孟德尔研究了豌豆的七种性状，但直到2023年，科学家仍未确定其中三种性状的相关基因。2019年豌豆基因组发布后，研究团队利用现代基因测序和计算工具，分析了近700个豌豆基因组，最终确定了控制豌豆荚颜色、形状以及花簇形态的基因。豌豆荚颜色由影响叶绿素合成的基因控制，荚形与细胞壁增厚相关基因有关，而花簇变化则由基因中的一个缺失导致。这项跨学科研究历时六年，标志着豌豆基因组学研究的新时代。

主要讨论点：关于"citizen scientist"（公民科学家）的定义和相关术语的争议，以及历史上科学与教育机构的关系。

不同观点：

Gregor Mendel cross-bred some 28,000 garden pea plants (
Pisum sativum
) and studied traits such as their flower colour to make discoveries about genetic inheritance.
Credit: imageBROKER/Alamy
The Augustinian friar Gregor Mendel completed his
groundbreaking work on genetic inheritance
more than 160 years ago, after carefully studying seven traits in peas, including the shape and colour of their seeds and pods. Yet until now, scientists still hadn’t worked out which genes drive three of those traits in the garden pea (
Pisum sativum
).
In a paper published on 23 April in
Nature
1
, researchers add a fresh chapter to
Mendel’s pivotal story
, perhaps in the process launching a new era in the genomic study of peas, which are a popular source of
plant-based protein
.
Scientists published a reference genome for
P. sativum
in 2019
2
. That digital sequence — a representation of the plant’s DNA — “was a huge breakthrough”, says Clare Coyne, an adjunct plant geneticist at Washington State University in Pullman. “But I would say [the latest study] is an even larger breakthrough. It’s really just an incredible effort.”
Modern tools meet age-old mystery
Mendel, a citizen scientist, famously performed a series of experiments in the mid-nineteenth century in which he cross-bred some 28,000 pea plants to understand how their traits were inherited by future generations. Although at that stage the concept of genes didn’t exist, Mendel concluded that plants were passing along hereditary ‘factors’ to offspring that determined whether they inherited what turned out to be ‘dominant’ or ‘recessive’ versions of genes known as alleles. Scientists continue to study such Mendelian traits today, and have identified thousands of them in humans. However, many of these traits
have yet to be linked
to a particular gene — and the same had been true of three of Mendel’s original seven pea traits.
Mendel, a friar, is recognized today as the founder of genetics.
Credit: Pictorial Press/Alamy
Noam Chayut, an applied crop geneticist at the John Innes Centre (JIC) in Norwich, UK, and a co-author of the current paper, says he and the other team members were intrigued by the enduring mystery and decided that “sequencing and computational tools had advanced enough to tackle the final three” genes. Using the JIC’s Germplasm Resource Unit — which houses more than 3,500 pea variants, alongside publicly available genomic data sets — the group amassed and deep sequenced nearly 700 pea genomes. These contained roughly 155 million single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) — single base-pair differences in the DNA sequences compared with the standard, or ‘reference’,
P. sativum
genome.
Using several methods, including selective breeding of pea plants and genome-wide association studies, which probe each genome for differences in the number and location of SNPs, the group identified the genes linked to the three remaining traits. Specifically, the researchers found that pea-pod colour is controlled by a gene that disrupts chlorophyll biosynthesis, leading to either green or yellow pods. They also identified two genes that probably help to control pod shape by inducing disruption of cell-wall thickening in the plant. And they determined that a deletion in the genetic code at a particular point in another gene can cause changes in the branching or clustering of flowers on the plants — a process known as fasciation.
A long road
Pulling together several methods meant that the work took six years to complete, and Chayut says it was possible only because of the interdisciplinary nature of the team, with each member bringing a necessary skill to the partnership. “The most important and beautiful part of this research is the collaboration,” he says.

43794081.article_summary: 文章总结了科学家们如何解开格雷戈尔·孟德尔160多年前在豌豆实验中未解的三个遗传性状的基因谜题。孟德尔研究了豌豆的七种性状，但直到2023年，科学家仍未确定其中三种性状的相关基因。2019年豌豆基因组发布后，研究团队利用现代基因测序和计算工具，分析了近700个豌豆基因组，最终确定了控制豌豆荚颜色、形状以及花簇形态的基因。豌豆荚颜色由影响叶绿素合成的基因控制，荚形与细胞壁增厚相关基因有关，而花簇变化则由基因中的一个缺失导致。这项跨学科研究历时六年，标志着豌豆基因组学研究的新时代。

data.title: Show HN: Logiquiz – Daily Self-Referential Puzzles
data.author: slig
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了如何玩和解决一种名为Logiquiz的逻辑谜题。玩法包括点击选项标记正确或错误答案，并通过旁边的进度条查看逻辑正确性。解题步骤包括通读所有问题、排除明显错误选项、优先解决简单问题、跟踪潜在答案并根据新信息调整答案，以及在解决更多问题后重新审视之前的问题。Logiquiz是一种自我指涉的谜题，问题通常涉及整个 quiz 的结构或答案的特性，需要通过逻辑和推理来解决，可能从简单到复杂不等。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对一个谜题游戏的反馈和功能建议

不同观点：
• [mdduar] 认为游戏非常有趣，特别提到撤销/重做按钮非常有用，帮助他们纠正错误而无需重头开始，提升了游戏体验。
• [smeej] 分享了他们的挫折经历，因为误操作导致所有答案被清空，建议增加答案锁定按钮和浮动的撤销/重做按钮，以便更好地推演谜题，而不必借助外部工具。
• [Recursing] 提到使用人工智能工具（如Gemini和Claude）可以轻松编写程序来解决谜题，认为这是一个不意外但仍令人愉悦的观察。
• [jweather] 表示游戏非常有趣，但遇到了选择正确答案后得到红条提示的奇怪现象，这让他们一时困惑。
• [satisfice] 指出游戏中一个问题格式像是有bug，特别是“what is the only answer with ${q}?”这样的表述。

补充讨论：
• 用户对撤销/重做功能有较强的需求，认为该功能能有效改善游戏体验。
• 游戏中存在意外刷新导致答案丢失的问题，用户对此感到不满。
• 部分用户遇到界面反馈不一致的问题，例如正确答案被标记为错误。
• 有用户提到利用外部工具解决谜题，显示出谜题设计可能存在被自动化解决的风险。
• 游戏中的一些表述被认为是bug或不清晰，需要开发者注意和改进。

data.title: Show HN: BugStalker - a modern Rust debugger
data.author: godzie
data.article_summary: BugStalker 是一个专为 Linux x86-64 平台上 Rust 程序调试而设计的现代调试器。它采用 Rust 编写，具备核心调试功能，如断点、步进执行、信号处理和观察点等。同时支持多线程应用、数据查询表达式和深度的 Rust 类型系统集成，包括集合和智能指针等。它还支持异步 Rust，包括 Tokio 运行时检查，并提供灵活的界面，可在控制台和 TUI 模式之间切换。BugStalker 具有可扩展架构和内置的 Tokio 扩展机制。该项目开源，采用 MIT 许可，欢迎社区贡献。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：BugStalker调试工具的功能、名称、平台支持以及机器接口模式

不同观点：
• [otherayden] 对项目名称表示赞赏，尽管他不是Rust开发者。
• [bobajeff] 关注是否具有类似gdb/lldb的机器接口模式，以便与其代码编辑器集成。
• [gitroom] 表示该工具对解决async错误非常有帮助，认为Rust调试一直比较困难。
• [meisel] 对该工具未获得更多关注表示惊讶，基于以往使用其他Rug调试工具的糟糕经验，希望BugStalker能表现更好，例如以前无法调用函数。
• [bfrog] 表示希望该工具能够支持jtag/swd调试探针，以便用于嵌入式目标。
• [giancarlostoro] 认为“BugStomper”也是一个很好的名字选择。
• [thurn] 询问该工具是否因依赖关系必须在Linux上运行，或者未来是否可能支持OSX。

补充讨论：
• [godzie] 详细介绍了BugStalker的功能，包括支持Async Rust、增强的变量检查、新的命令如`call`和`trigger`，并提供了项目网站链接和更新日志。
• [sixthDot] 询问是否计划支持类似GDB/MI的机器接口。

争议焦点：
• 目前没有明显争议，但用户对平台支持和机器接口模式有不同期望和疑问。

data.title: Mary MacLane, the Wild Woman from Butte
data.author: samclemens
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了1902年美国蒙大拿州巴特市19岁女孩玛丽·麦克莱恩（Mary MacLane）因出版一本惊世骇俗的日记而一夜成名的故事。她的作品《玛丽·麦克莱恩的故事》坦率地展现了其内心世界，充满对生活体验的渴望、对两性情感的挣扎以及对青春不公的愤怒。麦克莱恩自诩为天才，毫不掩饰地表达对自身欲望和双性恋倾向的看法，并对周围人群表现出蔑视。她的文字风格前卫、自恋且带有些许残酷，尽管描写的是日常生活琐事，但内心活动极为丰富。她的独特个性和直言不讳的态度使她成为当时文坛的“怪才”，其作品在一百年后仍显得现代且未经时。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对历史上年轻女性创作及其当代对比的看法

不同观点：
• Phanteaume 认为过去的人们本质上与现代人相同，只是环境不同。他质疑在当代即时通讯和无尽娱乐的影响下，是否还会有年轻女性写出类似的书，并担心这些技术正在让人们，尤其是孩子，变得更愚笨。他还提出是否应通过培养“卢德分子”来解决问题。

“I Am Making the World My Confessor”
Mary MacLane, the Wild Woman from Butte
By
Hunter Dukes
In 1902, a woman named Mary MacLane from Butte, Montana, became an international sensation after publishing a scandalous journal at the age of 19. Rereading this often-forgotten debut, Hunter Dukes finds a voice that hungers for worldly experience, brims with bisexual longing, and rages against the injustices of youth.
Published
April 23, 2025
Scroll through the whole page to download all images before printing.
1903 portrait of Mary MacLane —
Source
.
A century before publishers started marketing novels as “essential sad girl literature” and newspapers ran headlines about the “cult of the literary sad woman”, Mary MacLane confessed all, at the age of nineteen, and became the
enfant terrible
of American letters, seemingly overnight.
1
“This is not a diary. It is a Portrayal. It is my inner life shown in its nakedness. I am trying my utmost to show everything—to reveal every petty vanity and weakness, every phase of feeling, every desire
. . . .
These are the feelings of miserable, wretched youth.”
2
Born in 1881 in Winnipeg, Canada, MacLane moved with her family to Butte, Montana, when she was ten years old. Her father had died two years prior (“he is nothing to me”), and she spent her childhood with her siblings — “they are also nothing to me” — and her mother, Margaret, a woman some biographers identify as “Anglo-Métis”, of mixed British and Indigenous North American ancestry.
3
By Mary’s own account, she graduated high school with “very good Latin; good French and Greek;
. . .
an empty heart that has taken on a certain wooden quality; an excellent strong young woman’s-body; a pitiably starved soul”.
4
She was accepted to Stanford and anticipated that her family’s fortune would see to the costs of student life. (Her late father had built a steamship empire, transporting postal freight and commercial goods along Canada’s riverways.) In one version of the story, it was not until Mary was standing on the station platform, awaiting a train to California, that her stepfather admitted to mismanaging a colossal estate. She was curtly informed that there was little to nothing left.
5
Scroll through the whole page to download all images before printing.
Studio portrait of Mary MacLane (top) and her siblings James, Dorothy, and John (left), ca. 1900 —
Source
.
And so, Mary MacLane stayed at home and followed a singular ambition: “I wish to write, write, write!”
6
Her first book was drafted when she was just nineteen. Originally titled “I Await the Devil’s Coming”,
The Story of Mary MacLane
(1902) records four months in the life of its author. Nothing much happens in the outside world beyond study and maintenance: she makes breakfast, cleans the bathroom, tidies her bedroom, reads, and walks. But her inner life is full of action, as she desires, dreams, and rants against the injustices of youth and sex. “I am obscure; I am morbid; I am unhappy; my life is made up of Nothingness; I want everything and I have nothing.”
7
MacLane’s voice is effortlessly conversational — a mix of emotional observation, self-celebration, and autofictional anticipation, with no shortage of cruelty — and, a century on, sounds mostly unworn, modern. The narrator defines herself in many ways: as a “thief”, “vagabond”, “liar”, and “a philosopher of my own peripatetic school”. She tirelessly expresses pride in her mind and her “fine young body that is feminine in every fiber” and brims with a desire to experience all aspects of life, except, perhaps, modesty.
8
The word “genius” occurs eighty-nine times in this book, the phrase “I am a genius” thirteen times. She extensively (and often unkindly) describes the various ethnic groups living in Butte — Cornish, Jewish, Finnish, and so on — before declaring, wholesale, that “the souls of these people are dumb”. Her disdain for others fills a broad church; she must stand apart, in every way.
I am charmingly original. I am delightfully refreshing. I am startlingly Bohemian. I am quaintly interesting—[all] the while in my sleeve I may be smiling and smiling—and a villain. I can talk to a roomful of dull people and compel their interest, admiration, and astonishment. I do this sometimes for my own amusement. As I have said, I am a rather plain-featured, insignificant-looking genius, but I have a graceful personality. I have a pretty figure. I am well set up. And when I choose to talk in my charmingly original fashion, embellishing my conversation with many quaint lies, I have a certain very noticeable way with me, an “air”.
9
Throughout
The Story of Mary MacLane
, she writes unabashedly about her romantic interest in both women and men, and records at length her fantasies of marrying Napoleon and the Devil in passages of self-immolating lust: “Hurt me, burn me, consume me with hot love, shake me violently,

data.author: wizardforhire
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了人工智能（AI）快速发展对人类创造力的威胁。科技公司通过网络爬虫获取大量创意内容来训练AI模型，而这些模型生成的大量合成媒体内容可能淹没人类的创造力，导致文化同质化和创造性表达的平庸化。文章强调，人类创造力源自有限的生物特性及真实生活体验，与机器学习将文化视为无限资源进行“开采”形成对比。AI依赖人类作品，但其使用方式引发了关于版权和公平使用的争议，传统艺术家担心生计受到影响，呼吁明确边界和尊重创作。文章将版权比作生态管理，强调创造性资源的可持续性，警告若不保护人类创造力，长期可能损害 both AI发展和社会。

不同观点：

Ironically, our present AI age has shone a bright spotlight on the immense value of human creativity as breakthroughs in technology threaten to undermine it. As tech giants rush to build newer AI models, their web crawlers
vacuum up
creative content, and those same models
spew floods
of synthetic media, risking drowning out the human creative spark in an ocean of pablum.
Given this trajectory, AI-generated content may soon exceed the entire corpus of historical human creative works, making the preservation of the human creative ecosystem not just an ethical concern but an urgent imperative. The alternative is nothing less than a gradual homogenization of our cultural landscape, where machine learning flattens the richness of human expression into a mediocre statistical average.
A limited resource
By ingesting billions of creations, chatbots learn to talk, and image synthesizers learn to draw. Along the way, the AI companies behind them treat our shared culture like an inexhaustible resource to be strip-mined, with little thought for the consequences.
But human creativity isn't the product of an industrial process; it's inherently throttled precisely because we are finite biological beings who draw inspiration from real lived experiences while balancing creativity with the necessities of life—sleep, emotional recovery, and limited lifespans. Creativity comes from making connections, and it takes energy, time, and insight for those connections to be meaningful. Until recently, a human brain was a prerequisite for making those kinds of connections, and there's a reason why that is valuable.
Every human brain isn't just a store of data—it's a knowledge engine that thinks in a unique way, creating novel combinations of ideas. Instead of having one "connection machine" (an AI model) duplicated a million times, we have seven billion neural networks, each with a unique perspective. Relying on the cognitive diversity of human thought helps us escape the monolithic thinking that may emerge if everyone were to draw from the same AI-generated sources.
Today, the AI industry's business models unintentionally echo the ways in which early industrialists approached forests and fisheries—as free inputs to exploit
without considering
ecological limits.
Just as pollution from early factories unexpectedly damaged the environment, AI systems risk polluting the digital environment by flooding the Internet with synthetic content. Like a forest that needs careful management to thrive or a fishery vulnerable to collapse from overexploitation, the creative ecosystem can be degraded even if the potential for imagination remains.
Depleting our creative diversity may become one of the hidden costs of AI, but that diversity is worth preserving. If we let AI systems deplete or pollute the human outputs they depend on, what happens to AI models—and ultimately to human society—over the long term?
AI’s creative debt
Every AI chatbot or image generator exists only because of human works, and many traditional artists
argue strongly against
current AI training approaches, labeling them plagiarism. Tech companies tend to disagree, although their positions vary. For example, in 2023, imaging giant Adobe took an unusual step by training its
Firefly AI models
solely on licensed stock photos and public domain works, demonstrating that alternative approaches are possible.
Adobe's licensing model offers a contrast to companies like OpenAI, which rely heavily on scraping vast amounts of Internet content without always distinguishing between licensed and unlicensed works.
Credit:
drcooke via Getty Images
OpenAI has argued that this type of scraping constitutes "
fair use
" and effectively claims that competitive AI models at current performance levels
cannot be developed
without relying on unlicensed training data, despite Adobe's alternative approach.
The "fair use" argument often hinges on the legal concept of "transformative use," the idea that using works for a fundamentally different purpose from creative expression—such as identifying patterns for AI—does not violate copyright. Generative AI proponents often argue that their approach is how human artists learn from the world around them.
Meanwhile, artists are expressing growing concern about losing their livelihoods as corporations turn to cheap, instantaneously generated AI content. They also call for clear boundaries and consent-driven models rather than allowing developers to extract value from their creations without acknowledgment or remuneration.
Copyright as crop rotation
This tension between artists and AI reveals a deeper ecological perspective on creativity itself. Copyright's time-limited nature was designed as a form of resource management, like crop rotation or regulated fishing seasons that allow for regeneration. Copyright expiration isn't a

data.article_summary: 文章讨论了教皇权力的世俗与宗教平衡，特别是1870年意大利统一后教皇失去大部分领土的历史背景。教皇庇护九世在罗马被并入意大利时，自我封闭在梵蒂冈，拒绝承认罗马为意大利首都，直到1929年《拉特兰条约》重新赋予教皇对梵蒂冈城国的主权。尽管领土缩小，但这一变化实际上帮助教皇摆脱了世俗政治的纷扰，确保了教会的独立性。文章还追溯了早期基督教合法化后，教皇在罗马的地位提升及其世俗权力的增长，但也带来了新的责任和挑战，如罗马多次被侵略和教皇领地受到威胁。最终，失去大部分领土反而成为教皇权力的“礼物”，使其能专注于宗教事务。

43790625.article_content:
Feature
Curbing the Power of the Popes
The survival of the papacy has always been dependent on a precarious balancing act between the pope’s religious and secular powers.
Jessica Wärnberg
| Published in
History Today
Volume 75 Issue 3 March 2025
I
n September 1870 concerned and curious Romans gathered at St Peter’s Basilica. Beyond the walls of the Vatican, Pope Pius IX claimed to have been imprisoned in his own realm. For more than a millennium popes had governed territory across central Italy from their capital in Rome. When, in 1861, King Vittorio Emanuele II had united the Italian states to create the nation of Italy, the rump of the Papal States remained distinct. On 20 September 1870, however, the Italian king took the papal capital as his own. For those who questioned the popes’ right to hold worldly authority, it was a just and timely act. For others, the king violated an office sanctioned by God. As a champion of tradition, Pius IX made his feelings plain: it was the pope who had locked himself inside the Vatican Palace. He and his successors would remain ‘prisoners’ until 1929, refusing to recognise Rome as the Italian capital by taking a single step on its soil.
As Italian troops streamed into the city in 1870, Pius IX appeared humiliated. On the Capitoline Hill, papal guards stood behind a barricade of mattresses. One hawker sold straw apparently slept upon by the imprisoned pope. In 1929 the pontiffs would regain their status as temporal rulers of the Vatican City state, but even then the territory granted to them did not extend much further than their self-imposed jail. Nonetheless, the history of the Papal States suggests that losing extensive territories may have been a gift rather than a blow to the papacy. The purpose of the popes’ sovereign status had never been riches or renown – though some popes relished their worldly prestige. Rather, the pontiffs’ temporal power was a means of guaranteeing their independence, free from obligation to secular rulers. When popes were reinstated as sovereigns in 1929 they secured their ability to run the Church as subjects only to God. As rulers of the world’s smallest state, they were liberated from the politicking, scandals, and wars that had blighted their predecessors.
Hallowed ground
From the popes’ emergence in antiquity, their tie to territory was inextricable from their religious role. For most Romans visiting the Vatican Hill in the first and second centuries, however, it was far from an edifying spot. Remote from the pagan city’s religious, political, and commercial centre, Tacitus tells us, ‘promiscuity and degradation throve’. In the hearts and minds of Rome’s first Christians, though, the Vatican was already hallowed ground. In the first century, Saint Peter had died there. While most Romans would have seen him as an anonymous Galilean criminal, Christians saw a martyr whom Christ had elected to lead his Church on Earth. Peter’s death in Rome meant that the first leaders, or bishops, of Rome’s Christian community could call themselves his successors. Rome and the Vatican Hill became fundamental to the claim that the bishops of Rome – later known as popes – are the leaders of the entire Christian Church.
Pope Urban VI and the Anti-Pope Clement VII at the beginning of the Great Schism, 1378. Miniature from Jean Froissart’s Chronicles, 15th century, 1480-83. The J. Paul Getty Museum, Los Angeles. Public Domain.
After the emperor Constantine legalised and sponsored Christianity in 313, the link between Peter, his papal successors, and Rome was memorialised in marble and gold. Until then, popes had fulfilled their office in relative obscurity. Now they were installed in splendour at the Lateran, the first Western Christian basilica. On the Vatican, Constantine subsumed the humble shrine to Peter into a vast cathedral inscribed with the imperial name. He gave privileges to priests across the empire, while Rome’s popes enjoyed their own palaces. Soon the popes’ worldly status was so enviable that a pagan aristocrat joked: ‘Make me the Bishop of Rome and I will become a Christian immediately!’
The legalisation of Christianity meant that popes and bishops elsewhere could lead and expand the Church. However, the popes’ new status in Rome and the empire encumbered them with new civic responsibilities. By 324 concerns about territories in the Eastern Roman Empire shifted Constantine’s focus from Italy to Byzantium. From a new capital, Constantinople, he would rule the Eastern empire, leaving Rome and its environs under the emperors of the West, many of whom were weak and unscrupulous. For Germanic tribes seeking wealth and influence, Italy and Rome became tantalising, vulnerable targets. Rome was sacked time and again. Pelagius, a monk who fled in 410, claimed that the city, once ‘the mistress of the world’, now ‘shivered, crushed with fear’. While the Western emperors kept their courts in the relative safety of cities such as Ravenna and Milan, the pop
43790625.article_summary: 文章讨论了教皇权力的世俗与宗教平衡，特别是1870年意大利统一后教皇失去大部分领土的历史背景。教皇庇护九世在罗马被并入意大利时，自我封闭在梵蒂冈，拒绝承认罗马为意大利首都，直到1929年《拉特兰条约》重新赋予教皇对梵蒂冈城国的主权。尽管领土缩小，但这一变化实际上帮助教皇摆脱了世俗政治的纷扰，确保了教会的独立性。文章还追溯了早期基督教合法化后，教皇在罗马的地位提升及其世俗权力的增长，但也带来了新的责任和挑战，如罗马多次被侵略和教皇领地受到威胁。最终，失去大部分领土反而成为教皇权力的“礼物”，使其能专注于宗教事务。

不同观点：
• [shalmanese] 认为创业比赛与成功呈负相关，因为这些比赛偏向于容易验证的想法，而这些想法通常没有显著的成功先例。尤其是在旅游行业，由于客户获取成本高，大多数创业项目最终失败。成功的可能性较低，且面临诸多挑战。
• [cynusx] 强调创业者应花更多时间在问题空间上，而不是过早跳入解决方案空间。他认为理解客户如何解决问题的背景和行为非常重要，并建议在AI领域寻找机会，因为该领域吸引了大量早期投资。
• [danielpetrica] 分享了自己在创业比赛中获胜的经验，强调了实践和快速验证想法的重要性。
• [andrewstuart] 反驳了“创业必须解决一个问题”的观点，认为创业不一定需要解决问题，可以有其他动机和路径。
• [belter] 认为创业成功的关键在于执行，而不是想法本身。硅谷的成功正是因为有无限的资金支持，可以尝试所有可能的执行路径。

补充讨论：
• [oaththrowaway] 和 [gitroom] 分享了参加创业周末活动的个人经历，强调了这些活动带来的灵感和人际网络的价值。
• [lud_lite] 对danielpetrica的创业想法表示兴趣，并质疑其是否具有增长潜力，还是仅为生活方式业务。

争议焦点：
• 创业比赛的价值：shalmanese认为比赛偏向于容易验证的想法，而danielpetrica则通过个人经验证明比赛可以带来成功。
• 创业是否必须解决一个问题：andrewstuart和传统观点之间的对立。
• 创业成功的关键因素：shalmanese和belter分别强调了想法和执行的不同重要性。

data.title: On loyalty to your employer (2018)
data.author: Peroni
data.article_summary: Stevie Buckley讨论了对雇主的忠诚问题，对比了科技行业频繁跳槽的现象与父亲为同一雇主工作30年的忠诚。作者承认自己曾吹捧雇主以招聘人才，但强调透明和诚实的重要性。他提出选择雇主的四大标准：薪资合理、善待员工、财务稳健、愿意创新。同时警告员工，尽管公司可能提供良好工作环境，但本质上是交易关系，不应牺牲家庭、心理健康、尊严和价值观来迎合雇主。最后，呼吁不要被企业文化迷惑，保持清醒。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：公司与员工之间的忠诚度与雇佣关系的性质

不同观点：
• [rckt, lenerdenator, kinow, bsnnkv] 认为公司与员工之间不存在忠诚，雇佣关系纯粹是交易性的。员工不应期待公司会对他们忠诚，公司只会关注自身利益。因此，员工也不应付出额外的忠诚或努力。
  - 论据：公司会在不再需要员工时立即解雇，不带感情色彩；员工只需完成基本工作，不必投入额外的情感或努力。
  
• [jp57, II2II, samspot] 主张在雇佣关系中可以存在某种程度的忠诚，但这应基于双方的互惠互利。员工可以对同事或直接上级忠诚，但不一定对公司忠诚，且员工应根据自身利益决定是否留下。
  - 论据：员工可以在不“盲目忠诚”于公司的情况下，依然努力工作并感到自豪；雇佣关系是双向的，如果员工受到良好对待，回报以忠诚是合理的；但同时需要设置界限，避免过度投入。

• [hintymad] 提出只有在特定文化背景下（如日本），公司对员工的长期承诺可能换来员工的忠诚，而在美国等国家，这种忠诚没有基础。
  - 论据：在日本，公司与员工之间的关系更长久且收入差距较小，因此员工可能对公司忠诚；而在美国，公司更注重短期利益，忠诚没有实质回报。

• [trefoiled] 指出在某些行业（如游戏行业）中，高管与员工之间存在一种个人忠诚的关系，这种忠诚并非针对公司，而是针对个人。
  - 论据：某些高管拥有忠实的追随者，这些员工跟随高管在不同公司间流动，形成了一种个人忠诚的模式。

• [CharlieDigital, conductr] 强调工作不应成为生活的全部，生活的其他方面（如家庭、个人兴趣）同样重要。同时，经济利益可能短期内激励员工保持忠诚，但这种忠诚往往是暂时的。
  - 论据：工作与生活应保持平衡，过度投入工作可能牺牲个人生活；经济激励（如 retention bonus）可能在短期内留住员工，但长期来看，员工还是会根据自身利益做出选择。

补充讨论：
• 雇佣关系的交易性与情感投入之间的矛盾是争议的焦点。一部分人认为雇佣关系应完全交易化，避免情感投入；另一部分人则认为在某些情况下，情感和忠诚可以存在，但需要平衡和互惠。
• 不同文化和行业对忠诚的理解存在差异，某些行业或国家可能存在特殊的雇佣文化，使得忠诚更加普遍或被期待。
• 个人职业发展与生活质量之间的平衡是另一个讨论要点，部分人强调生活不应被工作完全占据，而应追求更广泛的人生体验。

On loyalty to your employer
Stevie Buckley
Follow

I’ve just returned to London having spent the past two weeks back home in Cork where I spent an awful lot of time with my father, a man who set up his first ever email account less than a year ago and a man who has spent the past 30 years working for the same employer. My Dad is the antithesis of the tech industry in every sense.
Considering the average ‘career’ with each employer in the tech industry is a touch under three years, the idea of spending 30 years working for the same employer is mind boggling. Despite this enormous disparity, I’m constantly witness to colleagues in the tech industry waxing lyrical about how great their employer is and why everyone should drop everything and come and work with them, only for them to announce a few short years later that they are moving on “to bigger and better things”.
I’m going to be the first to hold my hands up and admit to being extremely guilty of doing exactly that on a regular basis in the past. I work in recruitment. Employers pay me a lot of money to wax lyrical about how great they are. They pay
me
to convince
you
that the grass is not only greener, but their grass is more flexible and inclusive too. So how do I reconcile my apathy towards every employer claiming to be the best, and my ability to do a good job?
Transparency & Honesty
My criteria for vetting an employer worth working with is very straightforward. Anything beyond these four criteria is a bonus (and extremely subjective) but the four criteria below are my absolute zero compromise criteria.
Do you pay reasonable salaries?
Fortunately, due to my line of work, asking for specifics around salaries is par for the course and not something an employer can easily lie about. To put it simply, if your salaries aren’t at least competitive then we’re wasting each others time. Pay fairly or pay well and we’re off to a good start.
Do you treat your people well?
Glassdoor
is your friend. If there are a slew of negative comments, look for consistencies. Were they all posted around the same time? Are there consistent themes? Raise these points and ask for the employers perspective. A quality employer will be honest and highlight what steps they took to address those issues. Not every company has a helpful Glassdoor profile (a lot of startups have yet to be reviewed) so take to places like twitter and look up current and former employees to see if there are any red flags.
Are you financially secure?
This is
startup
101 folks. Do your due diligence. Companies House, Duedil, etc are a good start. Enquire about their runway (how long they can survive if their current income and expenses stay constant). If they aren’t willing to be open and honest about their finances, walk away immediately.
Are you open to trying new things?
This criteria is quite specific to the work I do and may not be universally applicable. If you’re asking me to team up with you to improve your ability to hire people then you categorically need to be open and willing to try new things. No amount of money will be enough to convince me to join your company and follow your same old tired recipe just because it worked well a couple of times in the past.
If you hit all of the above criteria then I can do the thing that enables me to convince great people to work for your company. I can be absolutely transparent and honest with people.
Delicious Kool-Aid
Ok, so you’ve landed a great job, the office is incredible, the people seem super friendly, the money is good, the work is challenging and life seems pretty great. Post pictures of your desk littered with company branded swag. Enjoy yourself but don’t delude yourself.
You are a transaction. Sure, your employer gives you the impression they care about you but as soon as you start costing the company money or pose a risk to the company’s image or breach any other element of your 300 page contract, then I can absolutely assure you that they
will
drop you in a heartbeat. You don’t even need to do anything wrong to be at risk. If the company is struggling financially, due to no fault of yours, you and all your colleagues are at risk. Suddenly the corporate line of “we’re all family here” sounds a bit ridiculous.
Your employer pays you to spend more time with them than you spend with your family and/or loved ones. Your employer is one of the biggest influencers on your mental well-being. Your employer can and will replace you in a heartbeat if absolutely necessary.
Let me be explicitly clear, your employer isn’t your family and they are not your friend. They pay you to do a job and your responsibility is to do that job well.
Do not sacrifice your relationship with family and friends to appease your employer.
Do not sacrifice your mental wellbeing to appease your employer.
Do not sacrifice your dignity, values and ethics to appease your employer.
Do not buy into the bullsh

data.title: Show HN: My from-scratch OS kernel that runs DOOM
data.author: UnmappedStack
data.article_summary: TacOS 是一个从零开始构建的类 UNIX 操作系统，拥有自己的内核，采用 C 语言和汇编语言编写。该系统具备虚拟文件系统（VFS）、调度器、TempFS、设备管理、上下文切换、虚拟内存管理和物理页帧分配等功能，甚至可以运行《DOOM》游戏。它能够在真实硬件和 QEMU 模拟器上运行。然而，TacOS 仍是一个业余项目，存在多个已知 bug，尚未达到实际使用的要求。要构建和运行 TacOS，需使用 Limine 启动引导器，并依赖 QEMU、NASM 和 Clang 等工具。项目代码基于 MPL-2.0 许可证发布。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕自制操作系统TacOS及其运行DOOM的技术讨论

不同观点：
• [planck_tonne] 对如何在笔记本上运行该操作系统提出了实际操作问题，关注具体步骤及学习资源的推荐。该评论者对操作系统开发有基础了解，但希望获得更具体的实践指导。
• [worldsavior] 对使用不安全语言（如C）开发操作系统提出质疑，认为应使用内存安全的低级语言来避免安全漏洞。该评论者承认项目是业余爱好，但仍主张淘汰不安全语言。
• [the_hoffa] 对项目的动机提出好奇，询问TacOS是否专为运行DOOM设计，还是作为一个通用操作系统并以DOOM为概念验证。该评论者分享了自己多年前类似的操作系统开发经验。
• [xhrpost] 提出是否有人尝试让现代PC硬件直接启动游戏，类似于旧世代游戏主机。该评论者认为虽然复杂驱动难以实现，但基本输入设备应该可行。
• [OSDeveloper] 对具体实现细节提出技术性问题，询问使用的DOOM版本、存储方式及引擎相关资源文件。

补充讨论：
• [tamat] 赞赏项目并表达对阅读大量规范文档的困难，特别对构建GPU驱动及相关文档的难度提出疑问。
• [waschl] 分享了自己类似的项目经验，强调作为业余项目的满足感，并提供了一个相关链接。
• [badmonster] 和 [NoScopeNinja] 都对TacOS如何处理进程隔离、调度及多程序运行提出技术性问题，关注操作系统的多任务能力。
• [throwawaymaths] 对PotatOS提出疑问，询问其具体含义，显示出对项目背景信息的需求。
• [finalhacker] 关注操作系统内核与CPU型号的关系，以及是否能在KVM中启动该内核，显示出对虚拟化支持的兴趣。
• [NoOn3] 对mmap实现方式提出调侃性评论，暗示可能存在取巧。
• [andrewmcwatters] 表达了对项目的高度赞赏，认为从零开始实现内核并运行DOOM是高水平的技术成就。
• [pkoird] 仅对项目名称表示喜爱，未提出技术性问题。
• [thewileyone] 对项目表示印象深刻，提出一个将OS默认设置为直接运行DOOM的创意，并建议通过USB启动加载器实现多游戏支持。

争议焦点：
• [worldsavior] 对使用不安全语言开发操作系统表示反对，主张采用内存安全的低级语言，与其他评论者对项目成就的赞赏形成对比。

总体来看，讨论涵盖了从技术细节到项目动机的多个方面，体现了社区对操作系统开发的浓厚兴趣及多样化观点。

TacOS
My from-scratch OS with it's own kernel written in C and assembly
TacOS is a UNIX-like kernel which is able to run DOOM, among various other smaller userspace programs. It has things like a VFS, scheduler, TempFS, devices, context switching, virtual memory management, physical page frame allocation, and a port of Doom. It runs both on real hardware (tested on my laptop) and in the Qemu emulator.
Please note that TacOS is a hobby toy OS and is not complete enough for real usage. It has multiple known bugs.
I have a Discord server for TacOS where I will share most updates, and you can also get help with your own OSDev project or just have a chat. You can join
here
.
Quickstart
To build and run TacOS, simply run in your shell:
git clone https://github.com/UnmappedStack/TacOS
cd TacOS
git clone https://github.com/limine-bootloader/limine
cd limine
git checkout v9.x-binary
cd ..
make
You'll need to have Qemu, NASM, and Clang installed. It will automatically run in the Qemu emulator.

43778081.article_summary: TacOS 是一个从零开始构建的类 UNIX 操作系统，拥有自己的内核，采用 C 语言和汇编语言编写。该系统具备虚拟文件系统（VFS）、调度器、TempFS、设备管理、上下文切换、虚拟内存管理和物理页帧分配等功能，甚至可以运行《DOOM》游戏。它能够在真实硬件和 QEMU 模拟器上运行。然而，TacOS 仍是一个业余项目，存在多个已知 bug，尚未达到实际使用的要求。要构建和运行 TacOS，需使用 Limine 启动引导器，并依赖 QEMU、NASM 和 Clang 等工具。项目代码基于 MPL-2.0 许可证发布。

data.author: rbanffy
data.article_summary: 文章主要讲述了作者Christian Quest重启1986年底运行的COMPUTEL视频文本BBS服务的过程。他使用Apple IIe和Apple Tell卡（集成了Minitel功能）搭建了一个Minitel服务器，通过直接拨号实现低成本连接。作者开发了Cristel软件，扩展了Apple II的BASIC语言，添加了视频文本功能，如&PRINT、&INPUT等指令，创建了自己的BBS系统。1985年，作者还编写了Rembrant软件用于制作视频文本页面，并与其他朋友建立了微型服务器网络，成立了AMISERV协会，形成了一个小型服务器社区。如今，这个BBS服务重新上线，可以通过特定电话号码访问。

43744635.article_content:
Get your Minitel back, the COMPUTEL videotex BBS is back!
Christian Quest
Follow
11 min read
·
Sep 15, 2017
--
2
Listen
Share
For the impatient… the server can be reached at
+33 1 8421 8116
(
original french version
)
After sleeping more than 30 years and 5 years after the “official” shutdown of the Minitel (actually the shutdown of the “Télétel kiosk”, the famous 3615 and others) here is how I restarted my COMPUTEL videotex BBS on Apple IIe as it was running at the end of 1986…
Retour en 1984…
My very first Minitel (in fact it was officially my grand mother’s one)
The first Minitels are beginning to be distributed free of charge in Paris area as a replacement for the printed phonebook. I remember going to France Telecom local boutique get a Minitel thanks to my grandmother’s phone subscription… it was a Matra Minitel 1 that I still have!
I also had an Apple IIe since I was able to save money to replace my TRS-80 that I had for 3 years. My next investment is an Apple Tell card.
Very expensive stuff at that time, more than 6000 Francs (half the price of the Apple II itself), because it actually integrates most of the electronics of a Minitel to fit inside an Apple II.
Of course, we have the V23 modem (1200/75 baud) and also the whole video generator part allowing to have an output on SCART (color included) and composite video jack with a true image, identical to what we have on a real Minitel.
Very expensive Apple Tell card… that will be (very well) cloned. At the radio-club where I tinker almost every week I buy a “copper”, that is to say the bare printed circuit board, with the list of components to weld myself… components that we find in the Parisian electronics stores (to my knowledge all have closed since then). I solder all this patiently and here’s my Apple II that can act as Minitel.
What interests me most is the possibility of transforming my Apple to a
server
, i. e. to be called by Minitels because it was not mandatory to go through the famous “361x” like 3615* to connect with your Minitel to a server. With direct calls, the cost of connection was just the cost of telephone communication, which at the time was a flat rate of 0.73F for local call regardless of the duration. Of course it didn’t last long, France Telecom passed to a tax every 20mn then 10mn… around that time if I remember well.
PDF available at
http://apple-iigs.info/doc/fichiers/pubappletell.pdf
Hello Informatique
, the company that marketed this card designed by
Roland Moreno
(the father of the smart card) documented the entry points of its ROM to enable software developments. Some softwares such as Fakir, Télébasic, Télépom were available.
I can’t remember why I decide to write my own, probably because I wasn’t satisfied with the ones available… and here I am programming my own software to write videotex servers based on the documentation of these famous entry points.
Cristel
Christian + Minitel, here is Cristel!
The idea is simple: add new instructions to the Apple II Applesoft BASIC and make them easy to use… and this is possible because Apple has provided a mechanism to extend its language with the “&”.
Cristel therefore adds an &PRINT that does the same thing as a PRINT, but on the connected Minitel. More than twenty instructions are added to write in BASIC language you own videotex server: &PRINT, &INPUT, &COLOR, &HOME, etc…
Sample code from Cristel printed manual
Cristel, on the other hand, is written in 6502 assembly language. Its code is very optimised (I remember nights well filled to save a few bytes) the first versions was around 700 bytes and the source code of the most recent versions is barely more than 1000 lines and less than 2Kb of 6502 binary code.
COMPUTEL
I therefore write the logic of my own server in BASIC… waiting for a call (&WAIT), displaying the home page (&DRAW), then a menu to choose between different “services”: the site of the local computer club that I had created (BASICLUB), a few games, a local mail service(not, not pink), etc…
My server is therefore an Apple IIe, switched on 24 hours a day and as there are many calls, I subscribe to a second dedicated phone line.
Here is the general menu of COMPUTEL as it was looking in May 1985…
In 1985 I didn’t have any software to create videotex pages (too expensive), so I wrote mine “Rembrant” which, as you can see, didn’t handle colors and grayscale or semi-graphic characters at all!
It was closer to BBS than videotex, but you have to start somewhere…
micro-servers… and the AMISERV
On this main menu, the 5th choice “Minitel Servers” made it possible to access a list of other servers that others had set up. Many of them were running on Apple II, then came those on Telestrat (an Oric Atmos with a builtin modem), PC, Atari… a small network of friends, also on Apple II, started using my Cristel software.
We had in the end created the “Association des MIcro-SERVeurs”, the AMISERV and the directory of these micro-servers was gradually filling up and could be found

• [marcodiego] 则从语言角度出发，认为如果观众懂法语，观看会更容易。这暗示视频可能以法语为主，或者法语知识对理解视频内容有帮助。这个观点关注的是语言对内容理解的影响。

- [marcodiego] 的评论指出语言障碍可能影响观众对视频的理解，提示语言能力在观看此类视频时的作用。
- 争议焦点可能在于视频的理解难度：历史背景和设备技术细节 vs. 语言障碍对内容理解的影响。

data.title: The effect of deactivating Facebook and Instagram on users' emotional state
data.author: imakwana
data.article_summary: 这篇文章通过两个大型随机实验，研究了在2020年美国大选前六周，停用Facebook和Instagram对用户情绪状态的影响。结果显示，停用Facebook的用户幸福感、抑郁和焦虑指数提高了0.060个标准差，而停用Instagram的用户提高了0.041个标准差。进一步分析表明，Facebook的影响主要体现在35岁以上人群，而Instagram的影响主要体现在25岁以下的女性。文章还披露了多位作者与Meta（Facebook母公司）之间的财务和研究关联。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：社交媒体对个人生活、心理健康以及社交互动的影响

不同观点：
• **支持减少或消除社交媒体使用**：
   - [8s2ngy] 认为通过取消社交媒体的“信息流”并只展示现实生活中认识的人的动态，可以解决当前社交媒体的许多问题。他希望有一个更小、更私人化的社交网络。
   - [donatj] 经历了Twitter等平台的衰落后，感觉社交媒体已死，现在的互动变得很少，这让他感到非常消极。
   - [flkiwi] 认为退出Facebook和Twitter后，生活变得更加轻松。虽然与一些亲属的联系减少，但整体上生活质量有所提升。
   - [submeta] 删除Facebook和Instagram后，感受到内心的平静和积极的变化。
   - [ElijahLynn] 成为“无信息流”用户两年多，感觉生活质量显著提升，并指出信息流对多巴胺的影响。

• **对社交媒体的矛盾态度**：
   - [kleiba] 认为社交媒体的弊端大于益处，但由于孩子和家庭的社交活动越来越依赖于WhatsApp等平台，个人保持不使用社交媒体变得越来越困难。
   - [rimeice] 认为在选举等情绪高涨的时期，六周的社交媒体停用期可能不足以观察到长期效果。

• **质疑社交媒体对幸福感的影响程度**：
   - [nomilk] 引用研究结果，认为Facebook和Instagram对幸福感的影响非常小，并怀疑研究结果的可靠性。
   - [perching_aix] 同样对研究结果表示怀疑，认为个人体验与研究数据不符。

• **社交媒体对心理压力的影响**：
   - [countWSS] 提到停止在Reddit上评论后，情绪压力显著减少，指出社交媒体上的讨论容易变得对立和紧张。
   - [Kozmik1] 描述了妻子沉迷于Facebook对家庭生活和关系的负面影响。

• **对特定平台的特定体验**：
   - [Arisaka1] 指出LinkedIn上的“高光时刻效应”让他感到压力和抑郁，关闭账户后心理状态有所改善。

补充讨论：
• **技术与社交媒体的关系**：
   - [notepad0x90] 分享了仅将智能手机用于基本功能（如电话、短信和打车服务）的经验，并指出这种限制使用的方式让生活更加高效和愉快。

• **对未来社交媒体的反思**：
   - [ryandrake] 预测未来社会将把社交媒体和智能手机成瘾视为当今吸烟一样的危害，并认为这种反思是必然的。

争议焦点：
• **社交媒体对幸福感的影响程度**：一些用户质疑研究结果的真实性和适用性，认为个人体验与研究结果不符。
• **社交媒体在现代社交中的必要性**：虽然有些用户认为可以完全退出社交媒体，但也有用户认为在现代社会中完全脱离社交媒体可能导致不便和社交孤立。

We estimate the effect of social media deactivation on users’ emotional state in two large randomized experiments before the 2020 U.S. election. People who deactivated Facebook for the six weeks before the election reported a 0.060 standard deviation improvement in an index of happiness, depression, and anxiety, relative to controls who deactivated for just the first of those six weeks. People who deactivated Instagram for those six weeks reported a 0.041 standard deviation improvement relative to controls. Exploratory analysis suggests the Facebook effect is driven by people over 35, while the Instagram effect is driven by women under 25.

data.title: Show HN: Rowboat – Open-source IDE for multi-agent systems
data.author: segmenta
data.article_summary: Rowboat 是一个由 OpenAI 代理 SDK 驱动的多代理工作流构建工具，允许用户通过简单描述快速创建多代理系统。用户可以通过 HTTP API 或 Python SDK 与代理进行交互，并能集成 MCP 服务器。使用步骤包括设置 OpenAI API 密钥、克隆仓库并启动 Docker、通过 API 或 SDK 进行交互。Rowboat 提供快速入门指南、文档和示例代码，便于开发者构建自定义代理。该项目在 GitHub 上获得 976 个星标，主要代码语言为 TypeScript 和 Python。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：多代理协作系统的有效性及其实际应用

不同观点：
• simonw：对“多代理协作优于单代理全包”的观点持怀疑态度。他认为，虽然在某些复杂系统中多代理可能有用，但对大多数应用来说，这种模式可能会让LLM（大语言模型）代码更难获得可靠结果，类似于微服务架构在很多情况下并不比单体架构优越。
• victorbjorklund：引用Open Hands项目的经验，指出在软件工程中，单代理因为拥有所有必要上下文，能完成大部分任务，表现优于多代理协作。他强调，多代理模式并非“显而易见”的最佳选择，需要更多基准和 reasoning 来支持。
• NitpickLawyer：对通过自然语言链接过多逻辑表示关注，询问是否测试过不同模型，并建议使用更多代码逻辑而非依赖模型处理链式提示。

补充讨论：
• asnyder 和 flynumber：对该系统表示兴奋和期待，认为其满足了使用自然语言而非节点结构来构建代理的需求。
• esafak：关注对Google A2A协议和无状态聊天的支持。
• justanotheratom 和 sirjaz：分别建议在着陆页添加演示视频和考虑原生应用支持。
• zcror 和 asasidh：对 mascot 和产品的视觉设计表示赞赏。
• owebmaster 和 andsoitis：讨论了该工具是否算作一个完整的IDE及其命名。
• ic_fly2 和 whall6：以幽默和哲学角度评论产品命名和潜在悖论。

争议焦点：
多代理协作系统是否在大多数应用中优于单代理系统。支持者认为多代理能提高灵活性和扩展性，反对者则认为单代理因其上下文完整性可能更有效。

• owebmaster 和 andsoitis：讨论了该工具是否算作一个完整的IDE及其命名。

争议焦点：
多代理协作系统是否在大多数应用中优于单代理系统。支持者认为多代理能提高灵活性和扩展性，反对者则认为单代理因其上下文完整性可能更有效。

data.title: Large language models, small labor market effects [pdf]
data.author: luu
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI在企业中的应用及其经济价值和影响

不同观点：
• [mediaman] 认为AI在企业中的有效应用非常困难，仅仅部署简单的聊天机器人效果不佳。他指出，AI的成功应用需要与现有系统集成，并深入了解具体的工作流程。他还提到，很多所谓的“AI解决方案”实际上是通过替代糟糕的旧流程创造价值，而非纯粹依赖AI能力。
• [Legend2440] 认为现在评估AI的经济影响为时过早，类似于1985年时评估互联网的影响。他指出，大型语言模型（LLM）目前更像是技术演示，而非成熟产品，其全面影响可能需要多年才能显现。
• [credit_guy] 通过历史类比指出，在计算机早期，许多科学家仍然使用计算尺，暗示新技术的普及和有效应用需要时间。
• [jaxtracks] 认为目前处于AI采用的早期阶段，过早得出结论并不合适。他提到丹麦的商业文化相对较少受到炒作影响，并指出在美国看到的一些AI相关招聘冻结可能会在管理层对AI能力有更现实的认识后逆转。
• [kazinator] 以幽默的方式指出，借助AI帮助撰写LaTeX文档的经济学家仍然令人敬畏，暗示AI在某些专业领域的影响可能有限。
• [trod1234] 对研究的方法论提出质疑，认为研究未能充分考虑多种因素，如客户在与失败的聊天机器人互动后产生的负面情绪，以及GDPR对数据隐私的影响。他指出，研究推导出的结论缺乏严谨性，可能误导非专业读者。
• [meta_ai_x] 认为复杂非线性系统难以建模，当前的研究数据点对未来决策没有实际价值。他指出，chatGPT之前聊天机器人效果不佳，而之后一切发生了变化，暗示劳动力市场可能会出现临界点事件，而单变量数据分析无法预测这一事件及其影响。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于AI在企业中应用的实际效果和经济价值。一些评论者（如[mediaman]和[jaxtracks]）认为目前AI的应用仍处于早期阶段，效果有限，而另一些评论者（如[Legend2440]和[meta_ai_x]）则认为现在评估AI的影响为时过早，未来可能会有重大变化。
• [trod1234] 对研究的方法论和结论提出严厉批评，认为研究未能充分考虑多种变量，可能存在误导性。
• 讨论中多次提到聊天机器人的局限性和客户互动的复杂性，指出这些因素可能导致负面情绪和更高的劳动力需求。

总结：评论者对AI在企业中应用的实际效果和经济价值存在不同看法，主要争议点在于当前研究的结论是否可靠，以及AI未来可能产生的影响是否可以预测。

data.title: Tumor-derived erythropoietin acts as immunosuppressive switch in cancer immunity
data.author: bookofjoe
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于癌症免疫疗法中促红细胞生成素（EPO）作用的研究及其潜在影响

不同观点：
• **[biotechbio]** 认为该研究具有有趣的发现，展示了EPO通过影响肿瘤相关巨噬细胞，改变其状态，从而减少杀伤性T细胞进入肿瘤微环境，导致免疫抑制。这一发现与临床观察到接受EPO治疗的癌症患者肿瘤进展的现象一致。该评论者还表示有兴趣重新分析旧数据集以验证这一发现。
  
• **[hinkley]** 提出肿瘤通过分泌化学物质来防止自身被破坏，可能是一种进化机制，而非DNA损伤。评论者强调了一些癌症与病毒的关系，并提出应该开始对癌症进行培养和DNA测试，以探索其微生物起源，类似于我们发现胃溃疡由细菌引起的过程。

• **[w10-1]** 对研究表示乐观，认为该研究识别了一种固体肿瘤逃避免疫攻击的方式，并提出了潜在的治疗靶点。EPO不仅刺激红细胞生成，还可将肿瘤局部巨噬细胞从攻击性转变为免疫抑制性。尽管实验模型是小鼠肝癌，但高EPO水平与多种固体肿瘤的不良预后相关。评论者还指出，目前没有批准的药物能够阻断EPO受体或减少EPO。

补充讨论：
• **[SimplyUnknown]** 提供了一个链接，指向该研究的完整论文，供有兴趣的读者查阅。

• **[mariusor]** 以讽刺语气猜测该研究是否由Lance Armstrong赞助，暗示对研究可能存在的商业动机或偏见持怀疑态度。

争议焦点：
• 研究中EPO对肿瘤免疫逃逸的影响是否具有广泛的临床意义，以及是否可以通过阻断EPO或其受体来改善肿瘤治疗效果，仍需进一步验证。
• 评论者对肿瘤的微生物起源和化学分泌机制存在不同看法，表明对肿瘤免疫逃逸机制的理解尚有争议。

总结：讨论围绕EPO在肿瘤免疫逃逸中的作用、其临床相关性以及肿瘤进化和微生物起源的可能性展开，涉及研究发现的意义、现有治疗手段的局限性和潜在新靶点。

主要讨论点：对一个特定网站及其相关事件的评价与讨论，涉及网站的功能、高校录取问题、API保护以及大学教育价值。

不同观点：
• 一位用户认为该网站有趣，类似于早期的互联网，具有学术幽默和实用性，并提供了历史链接作为例子。（正面评价）

• 用户"giarc"对Brock University上榜表示惊讶，并引用当地谚语暗示该校入学门槛低。（对具体大学的不满）

• 用户"bombcar"建议增加付费功能以增加收入，指出人们可能会因为对学校的复杂情感而愿意付费。（商业化建议）

• 用户"loeg"以幽默方式回应自己也被CMU和MIT拒绝，暗示对高校录取结果的无奈。（自我调侃）

• 用户"ericmcer"认为作者应对API未保护负责，而非责怪滥用者，认为被攻击是体验的一部分。（技术责任讨论）

• 用户"gaws"质疑作者在高峰期发布应用却没有预见高流量的可能性，指出发布时机不当。（对发布策略的批评）

• 用户"cultofmetatron"认为大学教育对于多数课程是骗局，除医学和法律外，自学和购买设备更具成本效益。（对大学教育价值的否定）

补充讨论：
• 用户讨论中涉及高校录取的挫折感，尤其是在Ivy Day发布应用所带来的反应。（心理和社会现象）

• 技术层面上，API保护和网络应用的发布策略成为争议焦点，强调了安全性与预期管理的重要性。（技术与管理问题）

• 教育价值的讨论扩展到自学与传统大学教育的比较，提出了自学与导师辅导的成本效益分析。（教育经济学）

争议焦点：
• 大学教育的价值以及自学替代大学教育的可行性是讨论中的一个主要争议点。

data.title: Show HN: Magnitude – open-source, AI-native test framework for web apps
data.author: anerli
data.article_summary: Magnitude 是一个开源的、专为 web 应用设计的人工智能原生测试框架，利用视觉 AI 代理进行端到端测试。其特点包括：通过自然语言构建测试用例，利用强大的推理代理规划和调整测试，使用快速视觉代理执行测试，并能在本地或 CI/CD 管道中运行。设置 Magnitude 需要配置两个大型语言模型（LLM）：一个用于规划的多模态 LLM（如 Gemini 2.5 Pro）和一个用于精确视觉交互的快速视觉模型（目前仅支持 Moondream）。配置完成后，使用 `npx magnitude` 命令运行测试。该框架支持与 CI/CD 集成，并允许并行运行多个测试。通过自然语言描述测试步骤、数据和检查条件，简化了测试用例的编写。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕使用LLM（大型语言模型）和VLM（视觉语言模型）进行自动化测试的方案及其优缺点，特别是与传统测试工具（如Playwright、Cypress）的比较，以及对Magnitude测试工具的具体功能和实现细节的讨论。

不同观点：
• NitpickLawyer提出将LLM和VLM用于首次测试，之后由传统库（如Playwright、Puppeteer）执行廉价、可重复的测试，只有在两者都失败时才最终失败。该方案旨在结合AI和传统测试，提高测试的效率和一致性。

• retreatguru询问了使用AI生成测试用例的具体建议，特别是从应用使用视频转化为测试用例的可行性，认为AI应该能有效支持这一过程。

• o1o1o1认为Magnitude并没有明显优于Cypress测试，尤其是在处理复杂企业应用时，通过容器化整个应用可以解决OAuth和复杂构建流水线的问题，质疑Magnitude在实际场景中的优势。

• chrisweekly提到Netflix的SafeTest方案，建议Magnitude开发者可以参考其思路，将其整合到自己的工具中，以增强功能。

• arendtio指出Playwright在处理音频输入方面的不足，建议Magnitude加入对语音输入的支持，以适应现代AI应用的测试需求。

• SparkyMcUnicorn认为Magnitude缺少一些功能，如提取数据（截图、页面内容）的能力，并建议增加非AI执行模式以减少成本和提高速度，同时对文档中未提及这些功能表示担忧。

• tobr担心这种测试方法可能存在非确定性问题，质疑其在实际应用中的稳定性和可靠性。

• grbsh基于自身经验，对Moondream模型的可靠性提出质疑，认为只有大型LLM才能有效支持某些复杂测试场景。

• dimal提出不应放弃页面可访问性测试，建议测试两种路径（视觉和无障碍访问），并设想AI代理模拟不同类型的残疾用户进行测试。

• aoeusnth1质疑是否能用强模型编译出非AI驱动的测试执行计划，并对Moondream的能力表示好奇。

• badmonster关心Magnitude中规划器和执行器的角色区分以及这些组件在特定测试流程中的可定制性。

Magnitude: The open source, AI-native testing framework for web apps
End-to-end testing framework powered by visual AI agents that see your interface and adapt to any changes in it.
How it works
✍️ Build test cases easily with natural language
🧠 Strong reasoning agent to plan and adjust tests
👁️ Fast visual agent to reliably execute runs
📄 Plan is saved to execute runs the same way
🛠 Reasoning agent steps in if there is a problem
🏃‍♂️ Run tests locally or in CI/CD pipelines
↕️
Magnitude test case in action!
↕️
test
(
'can add and complete todos'
,
{
url
:
'https://magnitodo.com'
}
)
.
step
(
'create 3 todos'
)
.
data
(
'Take out the trash, Buy groceries, Build more test cases with Magnitude'
)
.
check
(
'should see all 3 todos'
)
.
step
(
'mark each todo complete'
)
.
check
(
'says 0 items left'
)
Setup
Install Magnitude
1. Install our test runner
in the node project you want to test (or see our
demo repo
if you don't have a project to try it on)
npm install --save-dev magnitude-test
2. Setup Magnitude
in your project by running:
npx magnitude init
This will create a basic tests directory
tests/magnitude
with:
magnitude.config.ts
: Magnitude test configuration file
example.mag.ts
: An example test file
Configure LLMs
Magnitude requires setting up two LLM clients:
A strong general multi-modal LLM (the
"planner"
)
A fast vision LLM with pixel-precision (the
"executor"
)
For the
planner
, you can use any multi-modal LLM, but we recommend Gemini 2.5 pro. You can use Gemini via Google AI Studio or Vertex AI. If you don't have either set up, you can create an API key in
Google AI Studio
(requires billing) and export to
GOOGLE_API_KEY
.
If no
GOOGLE_API_KEY
is found, Magnitude will fallback to other common providers (
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
/
OPENAI_API_KEY
).
To explicitly select a specific provider and model, see
configuration docs
. Currently we support Google AI Studio, Google Vertex AI, Anthropic, AWS Bedrock, OpenAI, and OpenAI-compatible providers.
Configure Moondream
Currently for the
executor
model, we only support
Moondream
, which is a fast vision model that Magnitude uses for precise UI interactions.
To configure Moondream, sign up and create an API with Moondream
here
, then add to your environment as
MOONDREAM_API_KEY
. This will use the cloud version, which includes 5,000 free requests per day (roughly a few hundred test cases in Magnitude). Moondream is fully open source and self-hostable as well.
🚀 Once you've got your LLMs set up, you're ready to run tests!
Running tests
Run your Magnitude tests with:
npx magnitude
This will run all Magnitude test files discovered with the
*.mag.ts
pattern. If the agent finds a problem with your app, it will tell you what happened and describe the bug!
To run many tests in parallel, add
-w <workers>
Building test cases
Now that you've got Magnitude set up, you can create real test cases for your app. Here's an example for a general idea:
import
{
test
}
from
'magnitude-test'
;
test
(
'can log in and create company'
)
.
step
(
'Log in to the app'
)
.
data
(
{
username
:
'test-user@magnitude.run'
,
password
:
'test'
}
)
// any key/values
.
check
(
'Can see dashboard'
)
// natural language assertion
.
step
(
'Create a new company'
)
.
data
(
'Make up the first 2 values and use defaults for the rest'
)
.
check
(
'Company added successfully'
)
;
Steps, checks, and data are all natural language. Think of it like you're describing how to test a particular flow to a co-worker - what steps they need to take, what they should check for, and what test data to use.
For more information on how to build test cases see
our docs.
Integrating with CI/CD
You can run Magnitude tests in CI anywhere that you could run Playwright tests, just include LLM client credentials. For instructions on running tests cases on GitHub actions, see
here
.
FAQ
Why not OpenAI Operator / Claude Computer Use?
We use separate planning / execution models in order to plan effective tests while executing them quickly and reliably. OpenAI or Anthropic's Computer Use APIs are better suited to general purpose desktop/web tasks but lack the speed, reliability, and cost-effectiveness for running test cases. Magnitude's agent is designed from the ground up to plan and execut

data.title: UIT – performant, modular, low-memory file processing at scale, in the Cloud
data.author: janwilmake
data.article_summary: UIT 是一个用于大规模云端文件处理的库，具有高性能、模块化和低内存的特点。它通过四步过程来处理文件层次结构：收集、过滤/转换、合并和输出。UIT 强调性能和低内存使用，通过流处理和并行化实现在云端低内存环境下的运行。其模块化设计使各个模块可以独立运行和组合，例如 `uithub.ingestzip`、`uithub.merge`、`uithub.outputmd` 等，每个模块执行特定步骤。UIT 还支持在不同云环境（如 Cloudflare workers）中托管模块，但并不限于此，只要符合 UIT 协议即可。该库目前处于早期预发布阶段，旨在通过开源鼓励开发者添加所需模块。

UIT - Universal Information Terminal
X Thread
Hackernews Thread
UIT is a library for
performant, modular, low-memory
file processing at scale, in the Cloud. It works by offering a 4-step process to gather a file hierarchy from any desired modality, apply filters and transformations, and output it in any desired modality.
performance
: speed is of essence when navigating and searching through large amounts of data
low-memory
by applying streaming and parallelization we can run this in low-memory environments such as Cloudflare workers
modular
: modularity is beneficial because by making it composable we get a clear high-level overview of all building blocks. also, not all building blocks can be ran in the same runtime or location.
Important
This is an early pre-release. See
TODO
for current challenges. Try the demo at
https://uuithub.com
UIT has come about after many iterations of the platform of
uithub
, which started as a simple node-based parser of zipfiles. While building more and more features and add-ons, I found myself limited by the memory a lot as I was not streaming enough, and going back to JSON too early (because using the Streams API is tricky!). Thus, as features and complexity grew the need was born to create a more modular extensible architecture with good serverless practices in mind.
FormData
has a long history [
RFC 1867 (1995)
] [
RFC 2388 (1998)
] [
RFC 7578 (2015)
] and is deeply embedded into the web. It offers an excellent way to serve multiple files, binary and textual, over a single request. Although
FormData
does not support stream-reading directly from
Request
and other Web Standards yet, UIT leverages the fact that intermediate results can be read using the
Streams API
using
multipart-formdata-stream-js
.
UIT cleverly modularizes filters and transformations on file hierarchies by providing an elegant way to combine multiple UIT 'modules' together to get to a final result. Every UIT 'module' can apply path filters, content filters, and content transformations, to change the files in the file hierarchy, all while streaming, and even merge multiple file hierarchies together in the blink of an eye.
UIT Modules
So far, UIT provides the following modules that can be combined to create powerful file processing pipelines:
uithub.ingestzip
- Ingests and processes ZIP files into normalized formdata format
uithub.merge
- Combines multiple formdata streams into a single unified stream
uithub.outputmd
- Transforms and outputs data as markdown files
uithub.outputzip
- Packages processed data into downloadable ZIP archives
uithub.search
- Provides search capabilities across file hierarchies
uithub.ziptree
- Highly performant zip file-hierarchy extractor
uithub.otp
- Source proxy that generates an OTP to minimize secret exposure to other modules.
uithub
- Brings several modules together, pipes through them, and shows in authenticated HTML interface.
Each module is designed to perform a specific step in the UIT 4-step process (ingest, filter/transform, merge, output) while maintaining performance and low memory usage.
It is important to note that each of these modules can be independently hosted as a cloudflare worker, but the spec doesn't require it to be hosted on Cloudflare per se, you can also host UIT modules in other runtimes, as long as it's compliant with the
UIT Protocol
Please also note that above diagrams showcase many modules that haven't don't exist yet, but could be beneficial to exist. By Open Sourcing UIT, I hope to empower developers to add the modules they need.
UIT Protocol
The UIT Protocol is the convention that characterizes any UIT module. As can be seen in the diagrams

data.title: The VTech Socratic Method
data.author: zdw
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了作者对VTech公司1988年推出的混合型视频游戏机兼电脑Socrates的拆解和修复过程。文章提到，Socrates因作为“教育”设备生产过剩，导致其在eBay上价格低廉且数量众多。作者购买的设备到手时脏污且包装破损，经过清理后发现其外观和结构特点，包括一个用于扩展设备的插槽和两个RF接口。拆解过程中，作者发现内部使用了大量螺丝、热熔胶和 masking tape，主板由Toshiba提供的主要部件组成，包括Z80 CPU和Toshiba的集成电路。扩展接口简单，主要用于I/O设备。此外，作者还对机器进行了AV修改，增加视频放大功能，并解决了电源问题。最终，通过复杂的修改实现了更高质量的视频输出。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对老式教育玩具的看法及其技术特点

不同观点：
• v64认为这种老式教育玩具的图形加载缓慢可以被视为一种美学，类似于填色书的效果，特别适合作为孩子的加载屏幕。他还引用了Wikipedia中关于系统逐行填充颜色的描述，不确定这是否是为了孩子的乐趣有意为之，还是因为系统处理速度慢。

• mthiim指出，这种玩具在1988年算是相当先进，相比之下，自己在90年代初得到的VTech SmartStart只有14段显示线，主要配合纸质书使用，功能相对简单。

• eru观察到，近期市场上的一些VTech电脑与90年代中期的产品相比，技术上似乎没有太大进步，并认为这可能是厂家故意为之。

• nubinetwork抱怨这种玩具速度很慢，但作为孩子时并不在意，并认为随着个人电脑和互联网的普及，教育娱乐类产品逐渐减少。

• pixelatedindex分享了个人经历，表示这种玩具对他有深远影响，由于无法负担游戏机，这种玩具占据了他很多时间。他还提到父亲拥有的Tatung Einstein，并计划将其芯片逻辑翻译到FPGA上以复习数字信号知识。

补充讨论：
• MrsPeaches对PCB的铜线布线感到好奇，质疑是否是手工绘制的，涉及对老式电子产品制造工艺的讨论。

争议焦点：
• v64和mthiim对老式教育玩具技术水平的评价不同，前者欣赏其美学效果，后者强调其在当时技术上的先进性。
• nubinetwork认为教育娱乐产品因个人电脑和互联网的普及而减少，这一观点引发了对技术进步与市场变化关系的讨论。

43779398.article_content:
We’ve had a lot of fun with VTech’s computers in the past on this blog. Usually, they’re relatively spartan computers with limited functionality, but they did make something very interesting in the late 80s. The Socrates is their hybrid video game console/computer design from 1988, and today we’ll start tearing into it.
Checking it out
These machines are oddly inexpensive and plentiful on eBay. I suspect that, like most “educational” computers, they made way too many of these, selling them very cheaply in anticipation of big sales of cartridges to make a constant influx of cash over time. The classic razor-and-blades model. As a result, retail stores were allowed to slash the prices on seasonal sales, which flooded the market. Most of the boxes I see on eBay have two or three price tags stuck on top of each other, indicating they were certainly not bought at full MSRP.
As you might expect for an eBay transaction, my Socrates showed up late, completely filthy, and in a heavily-damaged, too-big box. Luckily, the Socrates is built of some pretty thick plastic. I spent a lot of time rubbing it down with wet wipes and paper towels soaked in Windex. I was not hopeful that the keyboard worked, as the sticker on top was wavy, which indicated water damage to me.
In photos, I thought the big blue thing was a power button. It turns out to be a window looking into an expansion bay with a male edge connector inside it:
This is apparently where you put expansion devices, such as the voice module. We’ll talk about that in a bit.
The back of the system has
two
coaxial RF jacks. One is for “Antenna In,” and the other is for “RF Out.” I guess they decided this would be simpler for the end user than putting the switcher/tap outside the computer like most systems do. This isn’t going to last long.
Disassembly
“Educational,” eh? The way I learn best is by taking things apart. That’s how I got kicked out of the military museum. And the grocery store.
This thing is held together by an insane number of screws! The top of the case has a crudely cut hole hidden under a sticker, just like the Precomputer did.
Lots of hot glue and masking tape, too. I’d like to say this is the first computer I’ve taken apart that had masking tape in it, but
the NEC Bungo word processor had a bunch of it inside
, holding the broken plastics of the printer together. Let’s call this the first
factory
masking tape.
There’s a weird rusty spot under the tape for this keyboard-IR-receiver cap.
I don’t think these capacitors leaked, not at this angle, but boy is that rusty spot ever suspicious. Am I going to ESR-test these caps? Absolutely not. We got stuff to do.
The motherboard is removed, showing that there really are not that many parts, which helps explain the low cost. Toshiba dominates as supplier, as they did with the VTech Precomputer when I looked into that a few years ago. You can see
a much better scan of the Socrates motherboard on Wikimedia
.
Key parts, from left to right:
VTech mask ROM. 32-pin, so likely 1Mbit;
Zilog Z84C0004PSC or Toshiba TMPZ84C00AP CPU (CMOS Z80);
Dense QFP gate array VTEL 27-0769, a Toshiba TC17G032AF;
Multiple Toshiba TMM41464AP-12 64K x 4 DRAMs;
Toshiba TMP42C40P1844 4-bit microcontroller, probably for IR decoding because of where it’s placed;
A huge number of passives, some of which are probably a DAC for generating colour video and audio.
It’s a shame that so much is integrated into that gate array, but this was an inexpensive machine and large-scale integration keeps costs way down.
Judging from the “24” on the edge connector, I expected the expansion port to be 24-pins. It’s 12 pins on the top of the console… and then a big blob of ground on the bottom. The motherboard PCB reveals that this connector goes “TO VOICE CARTRIDGE.” With so few pins, this is probably for simple I/O devices and unlikely to be useful as a full general-purpose expansion port, but you never know.
AV Mod
Blog superfriend
Johnny Blanchard of Re-Enthused
had already designed an AV mod for this machine in the past, so I asked him about it. He assured me that it was a very simple design, and so I decided to make it much more complicated.
One of the admitted flaws in Mr. Blanchard’s design was that the video output was pretty dim. A little bit of amplification never hurt anyone, and for that, I went to my standby: the TI THS7374 video amp.
To power that video amp, I added a 5-volt surface-mount LDO after discovering the RF module usually receives unregulated 12V from the rest of the system. The THS7374 really wants 3.3 - 5V, and feeding it twelve volts will blow it up. I know this from experience.
Since I wanted to show off a little bit, I initially used an extremely tiny, inexpensive LDO. After sobering up, I realized it would be extremely annoying to hand-solder. A SOT223 LDO was chosen to replace it – it’s not like I don’t have the board room – and I did a test print for alignment in the case. Everything fit well, so I proceeded to fabrication.

data.title: Reproducibility project fails to validate dozens of biomedical studies
data.author: rntn
data.article_summary: 巴西一项由50多个研究团队参与的大规模复现研究发现，只有不到一半的生物医学实验结果能够被成功复现。该研究聚焦于巴西常用的三种生物医学研究方法，并在疫情期间克服了诸多挑战。结果显示，复现实验的成功率仅为21%，且原研究常高估干预效果。研究人员呼吁通过公共政策和学术机构内部改革来加强科学可重复性。该研究已发布在bioRxiv上，但尚未经过同行评审。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：科学领域的可重复性危机及系统性问题

不同观点：
• **系统激励机制的问题**：[drgo] 认为科学危机的根源在于系统内的激励机制不当，过度强调发表论文数量和获取资助，导致低质量科学泛滥。必须通过改革来解决这些问题，尤其是随着AI技术的发展，传统的以论文数量衡量生产力和质量的模式已经过时。

• **可重复性失败的影响**：[jl6] 提出应评估不可重复研究的影响力，区分重要研究和边缘研究。关键论文应有额外验证步骤，以避免依赖有缺陷的结果。

• **样本量和实验设计问题**：[jpeloquin] 指出很多研究样本量过小（n=5），导致不可靠的结果，特别是在生物机械实验中。低成本实验限制了样本量，影响了结果的可重复性。

• **科学停滞和低质量研究**：[acscott314] 强调科学停滞的风险，指出大多数已发表研究的不可靠性，呼吁提高研究标准，否则科学将停滞不前。

• **出版压力和职业需求**：[addoo] 分享了在计算机科学领域遇到的不可重复问题，认为出版压力和职业需求导致低质量工作被发表。出版不再是出于真正的发现或创新，而是为了满足职业需求。

• **不可发表的重复结果**：[jkh1] 提到在其实验室中，重复实验结果通常只在内部讨论，无法发表，因为确认结果不被视为新发现，而否定结果也不被期刊接受。

• **公众对科学的信心**：[WhitneyLand] 担忧可重复性危机对公众科学信心的影响，特别是在后真相时代，这可能会加剧科学信任危机。

• **根本原因分析**：[gitroom] 质疑不可重复性的根本原因，是出版压力还是长期积累的草率科学所致。

• **系统性解决方案**：[N_A_T_E] 询问如何系统性地解决可重复性危机，认为个体努力不足以解决如此大规模的问题，需要对论文验证和出版过程进行系统性改革。

• **对权威的批判性思考**：[mrguyorama] 强调不应盲目相信权威期刊如《Nature》或《Science》上的论文，科学是自我纠正的过程，失败的实验和错误的论文都是科学进步的一部分。

补充讨论：
• **跨学科的不可重复性问题**：[hahaxdxd123] 指出计算机科学领域也存在不可重复性问题，特别是在机器学习和机器人学中，实验条件和数据集的限制使得结果难以验证。

• **历史案例的反思**：[ein0p] 提到历史上的错误研究（如治疗溃疡的方法）在多年后才被纠正，表明即使有明确证据，科学进展也可能缓慢。

• **对未来分析的关注**：[chmorgan_] 提到通过关注Vinay Prasad的分析，可以预见哪些研究结论可能在未来发生变化，从而更好地理解当前研究的局限性。

争议焦点：
• **不可重复是否等于 fraud**：部分评论者如[mrguyorama] 强调不可重复的实验不一定代表欺诈或劣质科学，而是科学研究固有的困难和不确定性。其他评论者则更关注如何区分重要研究和边缘研究，以减少不可重复性的影响。

A replication drive focused on results that lean on three methods commonly used in biomedical research in Brazil.
Credit: Mauro Pimentel/AFP/Getty
In an unprecedented effort,
a coalition of more than 50 research teams
has surveyed a swathe of Brazilian biomedical studies to double-check their findings — with dismaying results.
The teams were able to replicate the results of less than half of the tested experiments
1
. That rate is in keeping with
that found by other large-scale attempts to reproduce scientific findings
. But the latest work is unique in focusing on papers that use specific methods and in examining the research output of a specific country, according to the research teams.
The results provide an impetus to strengthen the country’s science, the study’s authors say. “We now have the material to start making changes from within — whether through public policies or within universities,” says Mariana Boechat de Abreu, a metascience researcher at the Federal University of Rio de Janeiro (UFRJ) in Brazil and one of the coordinators of the project.
The work was posted on 8 April to the bioRxiv preprint server and has not yet been peer reviewed.
Ambitious undertaking
The massive experiment was coordinated by the Brazilian Reproducibility Initiative, a collaborative effort launched in 2019 by researchers at the UFRJ. The scientists wanted to assess publications “based on methods, rather than research area, perceived importance or citation counts”, de Abreu says. And they wanted to do so on a large scale. Ultimately, 213 scientists at 56 laboratories in Brazil were involved in the work.
The project unfolded during the COVID-19 pandemic, which brought numerous logistical challenges. And teams disagreed about how closely to follow the tested protocols. “It was like trying to turn dozens of garage bands, each with its own way of playing, into an orchestra,” says project coordinator Olavo Bohrer Amaral, a physician at the UFRJ.
Reproducibility trial: 246 biologists get different results from same data sets
The authors began by reviewing a random sample of life-sciences articles to determine the most common biomedical research methods used in Brazil, ensuring that any biomedical lab interested in joining the project would be capable of reproducing the experiments.
They ended up selecting three of these methods: an assay of cell metabolism, a technique for amplifying genetic material and a type of maze test for rodents. Then the authors randomly selected biomedical papers that relied on those methods and were published from 1998 to 2017 by research teams in which at least half the contributors had a Brazilian affiliation.
The collaborators initially chose a subset of 60 papers for replication, guided by factors such as whether a paper included certain statistical information. Three labs tested each experiment, and an independent committee judged which of those tests was a valid replication. The coalition performed 97 valid replication attempts of 47 experiments.
Falling short
The authors judged a paper’s replicability by five criteria, including whether at least half of the replication attempts had statistically significant results in the same direction as the original paper. Only 21% of the experiments were replicable using at least half of the applicable criteria.
The authors also found that the effect size — the magnitude of the observed impact in the experiments — was, on average, 60% larger in the original papers than in the experimental follow-ups, indicating that published results tend to overestimate the effects of the interventions tested.

data.title: "Poetry City": Iowa City, Iowa
data.author: samclemens
data.article_summary: Iowa City, home to the renowned Iowa Writers’ Workshop, is a hub for contemporary English literature, boasting numerous literary events, famous authors, and a UNESCO City of Literature title. However, alongside this literary identity, the city also harbors a rich countercultural history. Venues like Dave’s Fox Head Tavern, linked to figures such as Hunter Thompson and Kurt Vonnegut, bridge past and present countercultural movements. The city's avant-garde legacy includes artists like Denis Johnson and Ana Mendieta, and persists in modern writers such as Anaïs Duplan and Andrea Lawlor. Despite some loss of countercultural spaces due to development, Iowa City's alternative scene continues to thrive, encouraging artistic experimentation and maintaining its dynamic, "weird" community.
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点： Iowa City的生活体验及优缺点

不同观点：
• **[yesfitz]**：完全支持住在Iowa City。列举了其优点，如活跃、友好、社区导向、步行可达、安全、有反叛精神、价格合理。承认冬季寒冷和缺乏自然美景，但认为可以适应和欣赏小规模的自然美。
• **[shishy]**：将Iowa City比作“中西部的巴黎”，强调其艺术文化，特别是对艺术家的吸引力。同时幽默指出在有主场比赛时例外。
• **[_dark_matter_]**：基于养育孩子的经验，赞扬Iowa City的友好、餐饮、活动、学校和低生活成本。认为孩子们在那里成长很幸运。
• **[100k]**：引用歌曲歌词来表达对Iowa City的印象，强调其单纯和干净的特点，并与其他城市如芝加哥、纽约进行对比。
• **[billjive]**：对Iowa City有情感，提到一些老酒吧如The Sanctuary关闭的遗憾。
• **[BSOhealth]**：认为Iowa City有优点如新先锋合作社，但整体感觉小，冬天冷，缺乏自然美景， downtown变得越来越乏味，非学生或教授可能会遇到经济限制。

补充讨论：
• **自然美景**：yesfitz和BSOhealth提到Iowa City缺乏壮观的自然美景，但yesfitz认为小规模的自然美仍然值得欣赏。
• **生活成本与经济**：_dark_matter_强调低生活成本，而BSOhealth指出非学生或教授可能会遇到小城镇经济限制。
• **冬季寒冷**：yesfitz和BSOhealth都提到Iowa City冬季寒冷的问题，但yesfitz认为可以适应。
• **文化活动**：shishy强调艺术文化，而BSOhealth则认为与其他大城市相比，Iowa City的文化活动显得有限。
• **地方特色活动**：Boogie_Man提到附近Amana Iowa的Bratwurst节和独特的活动如矮脚狗比赛，增加了Iowa City的地方特色。

43790603.article_content:
Iowa City is the place where contemporary English literature matters more than anywhere else on earth.
By
Harry Stecopoulos
O
n Iowa City’s Market Street stands a low-slung, trailer-like red building. This is Dave’s Fox Head Tavern, one of the sites where the official culture and the counterculture of this most literary town overlap. Often used for student gatherings of the prestigious Iowa Writers’ Workshop—and memorialized in season 4 of
Girls
—the bar boasts such past regulars as poet John Berryman, novelist Denis Johnson, and poet Dean Young. Yet, for all its past sex, drugs, and literary high jinks, today’s Fox Head can’t quite match the volatile seediness of the original Vine, a bar important to Johnson’s
Jesus’ Son
. “Some of the most terrible things that had happened to me … had happened in [the Vine],” remembers the narrator of Johnson’s short story “Out on Bail”—“But like the others I kept coming back.” Nonetheless, the Fox Head still bridges across time to the vanished counterculture of the long sixties. Hunter Thompson was thrown out of the Fox Head when visiting Iowa City in 1978, and Kurt Vonnegut drank there when he taught at the Writers’ Workshop from 1965 to 1967. Vonnegut’s house, still standing at 800 North Van Buren Street., is only about a half mile from the legendary bar.
Is there a more literary town than Iowa City, Iowa? Iowa City is the place where contemporary English literature matters more than anywhere else on earth. The home of arguably the world’s most famous MFA program, Iowa City has authors’ plaques embedded in the sidewalk (yes, our streets are paved in literary gold), over 100 literary readings per year, and roughly 1,000 writers—young and old, town and gown—in a community of 75,000. No surprise, then, that in 2008 Iowa City was named a UNESCO City of Literature.
Yet as the Fox Head shows, there also exists another Iowa City alongside this broadly accepted and well marketed literary identity. Like a smaller Ann Arbor or Berkeley, Iowa City has long been a countercultural burg, more elusive and more incoherent than the City of Literature brand might suggest. During the late 1960s and early 1970s, Iowa City was where antiwar activism coexisted with a fervent dedication to the literary and artistic avant-garde. This era witnessed the innovations of such figures as Denis Johnson, but also artist Vito Acconci (a Workshop poet before he created celebrated art pieces like
Seedbed
), publisher Alan Kornblum (founder of
Coffee House Press
), artist Rosemary Mayer (a poet before she revolutionized feminist art), artist Ana Mendieta (celebrated for her earth-body works), writer and Actualist provocateur David Morice (a.k.a. Dr. Alphabet), and poet Alice Notley (a second generation member of the New York School), among others. And this legacy persists, not only in the material traces of that bygone era—the Fox Head, George’s Buffet, and the rock club Gabe’s—but also in the revolutionary 21st-century writing of trans poet and artist
Anaïs Duplan
and queer novelist
Andrea Lawlor
. Most importantly, perhaps, the vestiges of an avant-garde survive in the fandom of those students, faculty, and townspeople who seek a countercultural aesthetic that doesn’t always completely jibe with the more mainstream literary identity. The bookstores, headshops, bars, and clubs that Morice described as “Poetry City”—a place of artistic experimentation where a writer could, as Morice once did,
wrap an entire city block in a poem
—have largely disappeared thanks to urban renewal and real estate development.
Still, some sites remain. And, more excitingly still, new countercultural institutions have emerged.
If we want to keep college town communities dynamic, we should work hard to keep them weird.
If one were to take a tour of an alternative Iowa City, past and present, one could begin at the Black Angel (1913), the eight-and-a-half-foot tall memorial created by Mario Korbel that stands in Oakland Cemetery on the northside of town. This Beaux Art sculpture inspired Mendieta’s 1975 Super 8 film of the same name, in which the Cuban American artist ritualistically creates a silhouette of her body on the tombstone that extends from the base of the statue. In the film, Mendieta first uses dark dirt or paint to outline her body; then she traces it again in red pigment before adding a red “heart.” Mendieta completes the silhouette with a large black X also composed of dirt or paint before standing on the stone and swinging her leg, brushing away the figure with her foot. Short and intense,
Black Angel
provides a powerful reminder of how a radical artist can make a local landmark troubling and new.
Mendieta’s innovative use of the Black Angel statue looks ahead to Lawlor’s equally bold appropriation of the memorial in the novel
Paul Takes the Form of a Mortal Girl
(2017). In this celebrated trans text, Paul Polydoris, the protean protagonist, attempts to seduce a visiting writer in the shadow of the vampire-winged
43790603.article_summary: Iowa City, home to the renowned Iowa Writers’ Workshop, is a hub for contemporary English literature, boasting numerous literary events, famous authors, and a UNESCO City of Literature title. However, alongside this literary identity, the city also harbors a rich countercultural history. Venues like Dave’s Fox Head Tavern, linked to figures such as Hunter Thompson and Kurt Vonnegut, bridge past and present countercultural movements. The city's avant-garde legacy includes artists like Denis Johnson and Ana Mendieta, and persists in modern writers such as Anaïs Duplan and Andrea Lawlor. Despite some loss of countercultural spaces due to development, Iowa City's alternative scene continues to thrive, encouraging artistic experimentation and maintaining its dynamic, "weird" community.

data.author: mifydev
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了美国政府为减少国家债务所做的削减开支举措，并通过将庞大数字按比例缩小来帮助理解。目前，美国国债已达36万亿美元，每年政府支出超过收入，导致债务不断增加。文章指出，尽管某些部门的项目削减听起来节省了可观资金，如国际援助、教育和环境项目，但实际上这些节省相对于联邦总支出微乎其微，每年的国债利息就高达5000亿美元。文章批评这些削减更多是象征性的，对减少国债效果有限，却对社会服务和弱势群体造成重大影响。因此，文章呼吁关注实际有效的解决方案，而非象征性的削减。

A Scaled Down Look at Spending, Revenue, and What's Being Cut
The national debt is being used to justify spending cuts - but do these cuts actually reduce it?
Current US National Debt
$
36,000,000,000,000
Source:
U.S. Treasury Debt to the Penny
(updated daily)
Scroll to continue
The Problem of Scale
Our brains aren't wired to intuitively understand the difference between millions, billions, and trillions.
When we hear about the national debt reaching $36 trillion, or annual spending of $4.1 trillion, these numbers are so large they become almost meaningless. The human mind simply wasn't designed to comprehend quantities of this magnitude.
To put it in perspective:
1 Million Seconds
11.5 days
The time between two pay periods
1 Billion Seconds
31 years
The length of a typical career
1 Trillion Seconds
31,700 years
Longer than all of recorded human history
So how do we make sense of these astronomical figures? By scaling them down to numbers we can relate to.
Understanding the Scale of Government Finances
The national debt—currently at $36 trillion—is a number so large it's difficult to comprehend. Throughout this site, we've scaled down all government finances by a factor of
36 million
to bring these enormous numbers into a range that's easier to grasp.
Scaled Values
Actual Values
👆

🏦
National Debt
The total outstanding debt of the federal government
💰
Annual Revenue
(2024)

💸
Annual Spending
(2024)

📉
Annual Deficit
(2024)
The shortfall between revenue and spending each year
Each year, the government spends more than it collects in revenue, creating an annual deficit. This deficit is added to the national debt, which continues to grow year after year.
To put this in perspective: The cost just to service the debt—the interest payments alone—is
$500 billion
per year. This is money that doesn't fund any government services or investments—it's simply the cost of carrying the debt. These interest payments are now one of the fastest growing parts of the federal budget.
Data sources:
U.S. Treasury Debt to the Penny
,
Revenue
, and
Spending
data from U.S. Treasury (FY 2024).
The DOGE Cuts in Context
Recently, the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE) announced cuts to various government grants and contracts. But how significant are these cuts in the context of overall government finances?
The federal government spends about
$186,417
a year in our scaled perspective. Let's examine these cancelled grants across different sectors, each designed to address important social needs.

The Scale Perspective
These examples illustrate the scale challenge: while the savings from each cancelled grant might sound substantial in isolation, they represent an incredibly small fraction of the federal budget—typically less than one ten-millionth of annual spending.
These are just a few of thousands of grants and contracts that have been cancelled in the name of reducing the national debt. While their fiscal impact is minimal—collectively representing a tiny fraction of federal spending—the social impact of these cancellations is substantial. Communities lose vital services, research projects are abandoned, and vulnerable populations lose critical support, all for savings that make virtually no difference to the national debt.

data.title: Exercise before bed is linked with disrupted sleep
data.author: PaulHoule
data.article_summary: 一项由蒙纳士大学主导的研究发现，睡前四小时内进行剧烈运动可能导致入睡时间延迟、睡眠时间缩短、睡眠质量下降以及夜间心率升高和心率变异性降低。该研究发表于《Nature Communications》，是迄今为止规模最大的相关研究，涉及14,689名参与者，收集了四百万个夜晚的数据。研究使用生物传感器设备记录运动、睡眠和心血管数据，结果显示，高强度运动如HIIT、足球或长跑，尤其在接近就寝时间进行时，会对睡眠和夜间心脏活动造成更大干扰。研究建议，若想改善睡眠健康，最好在睡前四小时结束运动；若不得不在这段时间锻炼，选择低强度活动以减少对睡眠的影响。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：运动时间（尤其是睡前运动）对睡眠的影响

不同观点：
• **睡前运动与白天运动的对比**：levocardia指出，讨论的比较是"睡前运动与在当天早些时候进行同等量和强度的运动"，而不是"睡前运动与不运动对比"。levocardia引用的研究表明，运动相比不运动确实对睡眠有积极影响。

• **个人时间安排的挑战**：reedf1和Fire-Dragon-DoL提到，晚间是他们唯一可以运动的时间窗口，调整到早晨运动需要大幅改变生活安排，因此不太可行。

• **运动强度与时间的影响**：
  - jll29和loufe对"剧烈的晚间运动"具体指什么提出疑问，并分享了自己因晚间运动导致睡眠问题的经历。
  - anthomtb和parliament32表示，剧烈运动如果在睡前几小时内进行，确实会影响他们的睡眠，尤其是未预料到的运动（如爬楼梯）。
  - helge9210提到，只有最大强度的运动显著影响睡眠，并指出研究中对力量训练的测量可能不够准确。

• **个体差异与例外**：
  - ktm5j和sakopov表示，他们在睡前运动后反而睡得很好，显示出个体差异。
  - srameshc认为，听从身体的反应很重要，他的睡眠质量取决于是否进行了适当的运动。
  - clpm4j分享了自己晚间运动后顺利入睡的经验，显示出规律和习惯可能也有影响。

补充讨论：
• **科学与建议的争议**：wonder_er对很多人过分关注睡眠表示不解，并分享了自己对睡眠和饮食的不同态度。他还提到了一篇文章，对Matthew Walker的《Why We Sleep》一书中的科学错误进行了批评，引发了对睡眠科学的讨论。

• **情感与亲密关系的影响**：wonder_er进一步提到，睡前的亲密关系如果情感连接良好，对睡眠有积极影响，并希望人们不要追求情感上不连贯的亲密关系。这一观点引发了一些不适，并建议版主可能需要干预。

争议焦点：
• **睡前运动对睡眠的具体影响**：不同用户的经验和科学研究结果存在不一致，尤其是关于运动强度和时间对睡眠的影响程度。个体差异和生活方式的差异也是争议的重要方面。
