data.title: Parallel ./configure
data.author: brooke2k
data.article_summary: 本文记录了在2025年运行`./configure`命令进行软件配置的过程，详细输出了各种系统和编译器的检查结果。主要包括确认GNU工具（如`gcc`、`gawk`等）的可用性、头文件的存在性、系统特性支持（如大文件支持、时间戳等）、以及库函数的存在性检查。最终，该配置过程确认了构建环境的基本配置，为后续的编译和安装步骤做好了准备。文章还带有些许调侃，认为在2025年仍在使用这种配置方式显得有些过时。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕软件项目中`configure`脚本的效率、设计及替代方案的讨论。

不同观点：
• iforgotpassword：认为许多开发者直接复制`configure`或autotools脚本，导致不必要的检查。即使是现代代码库，仍然会进行一些多余的检测，如int大小、printf所需的头文件等，且在整个代码库中不集中检查生成的宏。
• codys：分享了自己将"configure”步骤部分整合进"make"的经验，并提出可以通过生成头文件的方式，减少对`config.h`的依赖，从而实现配置与构建的交错执行。
• epistasis：表示自己多年来使用autotools的体验不佳，认为这是对时间的浪费。尽管C语言还会继续使用，但自己不会再用C语言开始新项目，不过乐见对legacy项目的改进。
• rbanffy：指出`configure`不仅是顺序执行，还可能是增量执行，先前结果会影响后续测试。并认为不应该每次运行make时都运行`./configure`。
• fmajid：提到在macOS上，由于公证检查，`configure`生成的conftest二进制文件增加了延迟，且苹果取消了原先提供的 opt-out 选项。

data.title: Show HN: GS-Calc – A modern spreadsheet with Python integration
data.author: jpiech
data.article_summary:
GS-Calc是一款现代电子表格软件，专为处理大数据集而设计。它支持编辑大型CSV文件（包含数百万行）和自动拆分、合并的XLSX文件，能够处理复杂的数百万查找公式的数据模型，并快速打开和更新。其最大规格为3200万行和16384列，支持无限量工作表和子文件夹，无文件大小限制。对于超大文件，GS-Calc可自动拆分并保存为多个工作表于一个zip文件中。它还支持树状结构组织工作表和3D数组单元格引用，性能优于其他电子表格软件。

GS-Calc具备高效的数据处理能力，如快速加载文本文件、复制/粘贴大范围数据、执行VLOOKUP和MATCH操作，速度显著快于其他软件。它提供更强大的数据透视表功能（25个函数）、蒙特卡洛模拟、正则表达式支持、以及无限制的条件格式和超链接使用。此外，支持多核处理和Python集成，用户可自定义函数并处理多种数据格式。GS-Calc还提供两种文件格式：开放文档*.ods和高效的二进制格式。

GS-Calc is a modern spreadsheet with unique capabilities for processing big data sets.
You can edit large CSV files with millions of rows, XLSX files that are automatically split and merged,
build complex data models e.g. with millions of look-up formulas that are opened/updated almost
instantly and clean, transform, publish multi-gigabyte data sets.
32 million rows x 16,384 columns.
The number of worksheets and subfolders is unlimited. No limit for the file size.
Large text, CSV files exceeding the 32M/16K limits are automatically split into multiple sheets
and saved together in one zip.
Organizing worksheets in a tree form and creating 3D array cell references for
worksheets in a given subfolder (by specifying only the folder path in the reference).
Optimized to process large files. GS-Calc easily outperforms other existing spreadsheet solutions
and redefines what the term "large data set" means for desktop software.
→ Performance examples
.
GS-Calc vs other spreadsheets (for consistency, using the "industry standard" 1M row limit):
Loading text files is several times faster in GS-Calc.
Copying/pasting/filling large data ranges should be on average several times faster (and more, especially for blocks containing formulas) in GS-Calc.
Performing VLOOKUP and MATCH for newly pasted/entered data in large data sets can be executed at least several times faster in GS-Calc.
GS-Calc workbooks saved in its binary file format are a few times (and up for specific data sets) times smaller and are accordingly faster to load/save.
Pivot table data functions in GS-Calc: 25 functions (vs 11 functions in Excel), chi2 tests, 32 million rows, full regex filtering.

No limitations for using cell references to external closed workbooks in all functions
including the INDIRECT() function and functions written and added by users.
Closed workbooks are automatically opened in the background when updating formulas

.
The

conditional formatting

Python integration with UDF() functions. Create your own functions in Python that can return numbers, matrices, strings, CSV data blocks for parsing and images to be displayed in sheets.

• [sunray2] 从非专业用户的角度出发，指出该工具能够快速加载和处理大型数据，并且可以在视觉上进行编辑，而不仅仅是通过编程方式。他还提到，该工具可能吸引那些希望提高数据检查准确性的人，并以怀旧的态度评价了该工具的网站设计。
• [tianqi] 提到自己一直在应对Office Excel无法打开大文件的问题，习惯使用Python处理csv文件。他认为这款新工具可以解决这一痛点，但对“使用旧电脑”的宣传语感到幽默。
• [conductr] 对该工具表示赞赏，但质疑是否存在隐藏的缺陷，并提到以往许多试图取代Excel的工具都失败了。他还分享了自己在Excel中处理较大数据集时遇到的问题。
• [akdor1154] 对该工具是否仅支持Windows平台提出疑问，显示出对跨平台兼容性的关注。
• [Yiling-J] 提到另一个工具（RowZero）可以处理超过10亿行数据，并提供原生Python支持，兼容Excel和Google Sheets，但指出其私有云托管仅对企业用户开放。

补充讨论：
• 该工具与Excel的比较及其在处理大型数据集方面的优势。
• 对工具跨平台支持的关注，尤其是Windows独占的可能性。
• 其他类似工具（如RowZero）的功能对比，特别是云服务和企业级支持。
• 用户对工具取代Excel的潜在接受度及以往类似工具失败的例子。

data.author: anticorporate
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对《纽约时报》关于政府监控和数据驱动政策的评论及其引发的观点分歧

不同观点：
• **对《纽约时报》动机的怀疑态度**（potato3732842）：该评论者对《纽约时报》发表此类批评政府监控的文章持怀疑态度。他们认为时报的立场转变并非基于原则，而是出于对当前政治现实的反映。评论者个人有些天真地希望这代表着时报及其读者在观点上的真正转变，期待未来对数据驱动政策的态度会像对优生学运动一样被摒弃。

• **对左派支持监控的质疑**（rpgwaiter）：该评论者反对“左派支持政府监控因为便于提供社会服务”的观点。他们以自身经验为例，指出左派更倾向于直接发钱给民众（如全民基本收入UBI），而非通过繁琐的验证和行政成本进行管控。他们批评了食品券制度，认为这是政府自以为知道什么对贫困人群最好的表现。

• **历史案例的引用**（csdvrx）：该评论者通过提供历史链接，指出过去滥用数据的案例，例如二战时期美国政府利用人口普查数据对日裔美国人进行强制迁移。这个例子强调了对政府监控和数据使用的潜在风险的担忧。

补充讨论：
• **对文章标题的修正**（JKCalhoun）：该评论者仅指出文章标题中缺失的数字，未深入讨论内容，属于技术性补充。

• **提供外部资料支持讨论**（OsrsNeedsf2P）：该评论者提供了一个链接，可能用于支持或补充相关讨论，但未详细阐述自身观点。

争议焦点：
• **《纽约时报》立场转变的真实原因**：potato3732842认为《纽约时报》的转变是出于政治现实考虑，而非原则性改变，这一观点引发了对其真实动机的讨论。
• **左派对政府监控和数据使用的真实态度**：rpgwaiter对“左派支持监控便于社会服务”的说法提出质疑，并以UBI和食品券为例进行反驳，引发了对左派真实态度的讨论。

data.title: Fun with IP Address Parsing
data.author: marbu
data.article_summary:
本文讨论了编写IPv4和IPv6地址解析器的复杂性，特别是处理各种“诡异”的表示形式。作者首先介绍了IPv4和IPv6的标准格式：IPv4采用点分十进制，而IPv6采用冒号分隔的十六进制表示。然而，IPv6允许使用`::`来省略连续的零块，导致多种可能的形式，例如`1:2::3:4`实际代表`1:2:0:0:0:0:3:4`。

更复杂的是，IPv6还可以在末尾使用点分十进制的IPv4地址，例如`1:2:3:4:5:6:77.77.88.88`。此外，IPv4地址有多种历史遗留的表示方式，例如将地址视为一个32位整数（如`3232271615`代表`192.168.140.255`），或使用八进制和十六进制表示。

最后，作者提到处理IPv4和IPv6地址时，需要面对前导零和不同解析方式带来的不确定性，这使得编写一个完全正确的解析器变得相当复杂。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：IP地址解析及其相关API和标准的复杂性，尤其是在处理IPv6和IPv4转换时遇到的问题。

不同观点：
• **nly** 认为现代应用程序开发者面对地址解析的复杂性时，选择使用现有的API（如inet_pton）是合理的。但他建议inet_pton应该被弃用，取而代之的是一个更合理的API（如inet_pton2），以处理更合理的子集。他还提到HTTP的RFC标准对URI格式有明确限制，但现代浏览器仍较为宽松。此外，他提到IPv6在处理IP和端口对时需要使用括号，这在默认端口缺失时尤为麻烦。

• **orangeboats** 指出，带有IPv4后缀的IPv6地址在NAT64（以及XLAT464）技术中仍然具有相关性，特别是在移动网络中。这种地址转换技术允许IPv6网络中的设备通过特定前缀（如64:ff9b::/96）访问IPv4地址，这在IPv6过渡阶段非常重要。

• **ryan-c** 提到自己可能间接引发了这个讨论，并提供了一个链接，但没有进一步阐述具体观点。

• **o11c** 强调，仍然存在支持八进制解析的解析器是一个安全漏洞，因为以0为前缀的地址如果被解释为八进制数，将产生不同的有效值。他认为其他问题相对安全，因为最多导致失败，但建议在处理地址时应格外严格。

43798311.article_content:
Written by
David Anderson
on
December 25, 2020
Fun with IP address parsing
In my quest to write a fast IPv4+6 parser, I wrote a
slow-but-I-think-correct parser, to use as a base of comparison. In
doing so, I discovered more cursed IP address representations that I
was previously unaware of. Let’s explore together!
We start out simple, with IPv4 and IPv6 in what I’ll call their
“canonical form”:
192.168.0.1
and
1:2:3:4:5:6:7:8
. Various specs
call these “dotted quad” (more specifically, “dotted decimal”),
dot-separated fields each representing 1 byte; and “colon-hex”,
colon-separated fields each representing 2 bytes.
The first bits of complexity come from IPv6. In canonical form, common
addresses would end up with long runs of zeros in the middle. So,
::
allows you to elide 1 or more 16-bit blocks of zeros:
1:2::3:4
means
1:2:0:0:0:0:3:4
Next up, for cursed historical reasons, IPv6 permits you to write the
final 32 bits of the address in dotted quad form. Effectively, you can
splat an IPv4 address onto the end of IPv6 addresses!
1:2:3:4:5:6:77.77.88.88
means
1:2:3:4:5:6:4d4d:5858
.
And of course, you can combine the two!
fe80::1.2.3.4
means
fe80:0:0:0:0:0:102:304
The existence of
::
introduces an annoying edge case in parsing: the
::
can be at the start or end of the address, and the “empty” side
of the address is not one of the 16-bit fields.
::1
means
0:0:0:0:0:0:0:1
,
1::
means
1:0:0:0:0:0:0:0
, and
::
means
0:0:0:0:0:0:0:0
. This is a natural consequence of the
::
rule, but
it makes the parser slightly more annoying to write.
One final rule for IPv6: technically, each colon-hex field is 4 hex
digits, but you can elide leading zeros, as I’ve been doing so
far. Fully canonically,
::
is
0000:0000:0000:0000:0000:0000:0000:0000
. My apologies to trypophobic
readers.
That’s it for IPv6, mostly. Now, on to IPv4!
Fun fact, the textual representation of IPv4 was never standardized in
any document before IPv6 needed a grammar for its weirdo “trailing
dotted quad” notation. So, it’s a de-facto standard that boils down to
mostly “what did 4.2BSD understand?”, and “what did other OSes keep
when they copied 4.2BSD?”
And hoo boy, strap yourselves in, because 4.2BSD sure had some whacky
opinions! Let’s use
192.168.140.255
as an example. That’s an IPv4
address that people would look at and go “yes, that sure is an IPv4
address.” How else can we write that exact same address?
This is the same IP address:
3232271615
. You get that by
interpreting the 4 bytes of the IP address as a big-endian unsigned
32-bit integer, and print that. This leads to a classic parlor trick:
if you try to visit
http://3232271615
, Chrome will load
http://192.168.140.255
.
Okay, but that’s sort-of sensible, right? An IPv4 address is 4 bytes,
so printing it as a single number is a bit human-unfriendly, but
broadly plausible, right?
How about
0300.0250.0214.0377
? That’s still the same
address. Dotted quad, except each field is written out in octal.
And if octal is supported, you might be wondering about hex. And you’d
be right!
192.168.140.255
is also
0xc0.0xa8.0x8c.0xff
, according
to 4.2BSD.
Now, remember before we had CIDR (Classless Inter-Domain Routing) ?
IPv4 addresses were Class A, Class B or Class C. It was a weird time.
And that weird time made it into IP addresses! The familiar
192.168.140.255
notation is technically the “Class C” notation. You
can also write that address in “class B” notation as
192.168.36095
,
or in “Class A” notation as
192.11046143
. What we’re doing is
coalescing the final bytes of the address into either a 16-bit or a
24-bit integer field.
This, by the way, is why utilities like
ping
will accept weird
looking addresses like
127.1
for
127.0.0.1
. Unlike IPv6, it’s not
doing some kind of “missing fields are zero” expansion.
127.1
is the
Class A notation for “host 1 of network 127”, where the 1 is a 24-bit
number.
And finally, we come to one last bit of unspecified behavior: do IPv4
addresses permit an unlimited number of leading zeros in each quad? Or
is there a maximum of 3 digits?
001.002.003.004
is universally
recognized as valid. What about
0000000001.0000000002.0000000003.000000004
?
You might also be wondering if either of these numbers should be read
in as octal, since we said earlier that a leading zero might be
interpreted as octal. It depends! There are implementations that do
both, but
most
modern implementations have abandoned the octal and
hex notation, and treat leading 0s as decimal.
The leading zero debate also infects IPv6, to some extent. Is
000001::00001.00002.00003.00004
is a valid IPv6 address (“common”
form
1::1.2.3.4
, or
1::102:304
)? Most modern parsers seem to allow
an unlimited amount of leading zeros in their representations,
probably because they’re leaning on some “parse integer” library that
implements that behavior.
And so, we reach the bitter end. If you want to
truly
parse IP
addresses, this is the bullshit you have to put up with.

本文讨论了编写IPv4和IPv6地址解析器的复杂性，特别是处理各种“诡异”的表示形式。作者首先介绍了IPv4和IPv6的标准格式：IPv4采用点分十进制，而IPv6采用冒号分隔的十六进制表示。然而，IPv6允许使用`::`来省略连续的零块，导致多种可能的形式，例如`1:2::3:4`实际代表`1:2:0:0:0:0:3:4`。

更复杂的是，IPv6还可以在末尾使用点分十进制的IPv4地址，例如`1:2:3:4:5:6:77.77.88.88`。此外，IPv4地址有多种历史遗留的表示方式，例如将地址视为一个32位整数（如`3232271615`代表`192.168.140.255`），或使用八进制和十六进制表示。

最后，作者提到处理IPv4和IPv6地址时，需要面对前导零和不同解析方式带来的不确定性，这使得编写一个完全正确的解析器变得相当复杂。

data.title: Things I learned about software and startups by playing video games
data.author: mprast
data.article_summary: 本文主要讲述了作者从史蒂夫·乔布斯的斯坦福演讲中得到的启发，特别是关于“连接点滴”的经验。乔布斯提到，他大学时学的书法课程为他后来开发Macintosh的数字字体奠定了基础，强调人生经历的点滴会在未来不知不觉中连接起来。作者认同这一观点，并通过视频游戏中的体验进一步阐述，尤其是在平台游戏如《超级马里奥兄弟》中学习到的经验。这些游戏通过实践教授玩家新技巧和框架，因为玩家必须学会才能赢得游戏。作者鼓励大家通过尝试视频游戏来学习，不必成为专家，只需动手体验即可。文章还简要介绍了早期游戏设计的效率和沟通技巧，以《超级马里奥兄弟》为例，展示了如何通过游戏设计在无文字情况下传达信息。

43796746.article_content:
In 2005, Steve Jobs told the graduating class of Stanford a now-famous story about
connecting the dots
- a story about the calligraphy courses he took in his college years, which later influenced the industry-leading digital fonts that shipped with the Macintosh. He said:
Again, you can’t connect the dots looking forward; you can only connect them looking backward. So you have to trust that the dots will somehow connect in your future. You have to trust in something — your gut, destiny, life, karma, whatever. This approach has never let me down, and it has made all the difference in my life.
I’m a firm believer in this idea. I think every experience - even ones that seem frivolous - can teach you something valuable if you’re willing to pay attention.
In the spirit of connecting the dots, I’m writing a series of articles about useful truths I’ve picked up in unlikely places. I hope they not only entertain you, but perhaps compel you to consider what you could learn from your own adventures!
I’m a gamer. I wouldn’t call myself a capital-G Gamer, but I do enjoy playing and talking about video games when I have time, and as I've progressed into adulthood I've found I also really like
thinking
about them as well.
At some point I realized I often rely on mental models that I first developed playing a video game (I'm sure someone's written a thinkpiece in
The Atlantic
about what this means for my generation.) Something that I think is special about the medium is that when you're learning, you almost always are learning by
doing
. You pick up new techniques and frameworks because you have to in order to win the game (which is usually something you really want to do), and in my experience, putting ideas into practice in high-stakes situations is a great way to understand them on a more visceral level.
So, I urge you - if you too want to learn from video games, try them out!  Get your hands dirty. You don’t have to be an expert!
Learning from platformers
I don't need to tell you what a platformer is. It's probably the first thing that popped into your head when you read "video game": Mario running around, grabbing mushrooms, and stompin' on Goombas. Platformers are one of the most popular genres of game, and for good reason - they're casual, accessible fun, easy to pick up and understand. They're also a hallmark of the earliest era of home gaming, when video games went from being a weird pinball-machine thing you could play at the bar to being a weird toy computer you could plug into your TV.
It can be really instructive to play some older games. The more popular ones have been ported to newer consoles, but you can also play them on an emulator (IF you own a legitimate physical copy of the game of course and far be it from me to ever suggest you use an emulator in any other capacity.) Back in the day, if you wanted to market a successful video game, you had to be an incredibly efficient communicator, as well as making something really fun. Your customers were usually children - not known for their powers of attention - and you needed to make sure they understood what the controls were, understood what the point of the game was
and
were excited and engaged within the first ten seconds of picking up the controler. There simply wasn't enough memory available to include a drawn-out tutorial with lots of writing, and you couldn't count on the manual either - no kid is going to sit down and read a booklet about the amazing new game they got for Christmas. The only option is to somehow incept knowledge into the users's brain as they play.
The poster child for this kind of approach is, of course, Mario. You may be familiar with
this video
, or others like it, which showcases all the different ways the game communicates with the player without resorting to text.
Before we go any further, I need to clear up something very important.
Mario Bros. - the very first one - was an early Nintendo release about two plumber brothers who had to rid the sewers of turtles and crabs and weird moths. You wouldn't recognize it unless you're big into old arcade games. It was
not
originally developed for Nintendo's famous home console, the Family Computer (Famicom for short, and known stateside as the NES), which debuted almost simultaneously in July 1983 (it would soon be ported over, however.)
In 1985, after a few years of experience making games for the Famicom, Nintendo felt ready to begin work on a platformer that would push the bounds of the genre. The Famicom port of Mario Bros. was selling pretty well, so the development team decided to reuse the IP for their new game. It had little in common with the first Mario Bros. besides the name and the characters, so instead of calling it Mario Bros. 2, they named it Super Mario Bros. Every mainline Mario game thereafter has carried the same epithet, for reasons unknown; perhaps it just has a certain ring to it.
In any case - it's Super (Mario Bros.), not (Super Mario) Bros. His name's not Super

data.title: Simons Foundation Launches Collaboration on Ecological Neuroscience
data.author: domofutu
data.article_summary: 文章报道了新启动的“西蒙斯生态神经科学合作组织”（SCENE），该项目汇集了神经科学和机器学习领域的顶尖科学家，旨在研究大脑如何处理感知与运动（即感觉和运动）之间的交互。该合作基于生态心理学原理，重点研究大脑如何编码环境中的行动机会（可供性），从而将感知与行动紧密结合。SCENE项目每年提供超过800万美元资金，支持六个研究团队，涵盖从啮齿动物、蝙蝠到人类的多物种大脑模型研究。该项目为期10年，旨在通过跨学科方法揭示认知的基本原则，推动神经科学领域的发展。

Neuroscience
Home
Neuroscience
By
Jane Beaufore
April 24, 2025
Credit: Jun Cen for Simons Foundation
We are constantly perceiving the world around us. As we do, we make decisions on how to move our bodies. The brain’s ability to process all the required sensory and motor information for this is no small feat. And one of neuroscience’s most significant questions is how exactly our brains integrate these two information sources as efficiently as they do.
The newly launched
Simons Collaboration on Ecological Neuroscience (SCENE)
will unite leading scientists across neuroscience and machine learning to discover how the brain represents ‘sensorimotor’ (that is, sensory and motor) interactions.
“We are excited to enable a collaborative research program that uses the framework of ecological neuroscience to understand brain function,” says
Kelsey Martin
, executive vice president of autism and neuroscience at the Simons Foundation. “With an interdisciplinary approach, we hope to discover fundamental principles of cognition applicable across species.”
SCENE builds on principles from ecological psychology, which posit that one of the brain’s core functions is to encode affordances. An affordance is an opportunity for action available in an environment — for example, a chair affords the opportunity to sit. By encoding affordances, the brain closely links perception with action. Identifying how the brain encodes and uses this information will bridge gaps in our understanding of cognition.
The collaboration, which will officially begin July 1, will provide over $8M per year across six teams of researchers. These teams will include scientists dedicated to theory and data science as well as brain modeling in species ranging from rodents and bats to humans.
Simons Neuroscience Collaborations
are designed to span 10 years, enabling scientists to conduct large-scale longitudinal studies that typically aren’t feasible under conventional grants. These collaborations bring together groups of outstanding scientists to address fundamental questions about brain function, focusing on fields in which significant developments have created novel opportunities for exploration. Current neuroscience programs include the
Simons Collaboration on the Global Brain
and the
Simons Collaboration on Plasticity and the Aging Brain
.
“We received hundreds of intriguing proposals and are truly excited by the many outstanding scientific directions put forward by our community,” says
Alyssa Picchini Schaffer
, vice president and senior scientist of the Simons Collaborations in Neuroscience. “It was a rigorous evaluation process, and we are confident that SCENE will push the entire field forward by reshaping our understanding of cognition and behavior.”

data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了关税对美国消费者行为的影响。尽管汽车和一些iPhone的购买有所增加，但其他类别的消费则被推迟。宝洁公司首席财务官表示，关税导致消费者更加谨慎。根据美联储报告，除汽车外，消费者支出整体下降。汽车销售因关税引发的涨价预期而增长，但其他非必需品消费则显得犹豫。调查显示，约35%的消费者计划因关税推迟大额采购。关税导致的不确定性使消费者更倾向于控制家庭开支，而非加速消费。汽车行业受关税影响显著，预计进口车价格将大幅上涨，消费者 rush 购买以节省开支。零售商和制造商正密切关注消费者行为以预测需求。

Key Points
Tariffs have fueled car purchases across the country and some iPhone upgrades, too.
Yet in other categories, U.S. consumers have delayed rather than sped up purchases, according to surveys by market research firms and a recent Federal Reserve report.
Procter & Gamble CFO Andre Schulten said Thursday that tariffs have contributed to "a more nervous consumer" who pulled back in the last two months of the quarter.
In an aerial view, Ford Broncos are seen for sale on a lot at a dealership on April 18, 2025 in Austin, Texas.
Brandon Bell | Getty Images
At car dealerships across the country, consumers are rushing to buy new vehicles ahead of
tariff-related price hikes
. Some shoppers have also replaced iPhones early.
Yet when it comes to other items, retailers aren't seeing widespread stock-ups or huge waves of early purchases due to tariffs — or at least not yet. Instead,
U.S. shoppers seem hesitant to spend and inclined to delay purchases rather than speed them up, according to consumer surveys by market researchers and early reads from the Federal Reserve.
Consumer spending, excluding autos, was lower overall across the country, according to the Federal Reserve's latest
Beige Book report
on economic conditions released on Wednesday. Five of the Fed's districts saw slight growth in economic activity, four districts had slight to modest declines and three reported relatively unchanged trends since the central bank's previous release in early March.
Most districts saw moderate to robust sales of vehicles and some nondurable items, which the report attributed to "a rush to purchase ahead of tariff-related price increases." Yet both leisure and business travel were down, and the report noted that "uncertainty around international trade policy was pervasive across [district] reports."
Beyond some of the pricier purchases that stand to cost a lot more even under a 10% tariff on imports, early data suggests the duties have intensified consumers' desire to watch their wallets closely as they wait to see how Trump's trade policy unfolds. Companies from
Chipotle
to
PepsiCo
and
American Airlines
said this week that
they're seeing pockets of slower spending
.
U.S. shoppers have adopted "a conservation mentality" for their cash as they follow fast-changing headlines and see wild swings in the stock market — and their savings and retirement accounts, said Steve Zurek, vice president of thought leadership at NielsenIQ.
"There's so much uncertainty right now that shoppers just don't know what to do," he said. "There's nowhere to hide here — all they can do is control the household economics they have."
Some survey results have backed up a theory that shoppers are kicking the can rather than accelerating purchases: about 35% of U.S. consumers said they planned to put off a major purchase, such as a home, car, appliance or furniture because of tariffs, according to a NielsenIQ survey. That compares with just 7% who said they anticipated making a major purchase now to avoid the possibility of a higher price later. The market researcher conducted the survey in late March, days before Trump unveiled steep tariffs on dozens of countries, almost all of which
he later lowered
for 90 days.
In another reflection of consumer caution, along with higher mortgage rates, home sales in March
fell to the slowest pace since 2009
, according to the National Association of Realtors.
Retailers, airlines, car manufacturers and more will be watching consumer behavior closely as they try to predict demand and buy inventory. Some of those companies have
accelerated their own orders
of longer-lasting and pricier durable goods, such as equipment, to beat tariff-related price hikes.
Here's a look at what we know so far about consumers' early response to tariffs.
Early buying
In tariff fear-buying, one category stands out: cars.
The auto sector outperformed the rest of the retail market in March, as sales excluding motor vehicles and parts increased 0.5%, while sales in the auto sector jumped 5.3%, the
Commerce Department
reported last week.
While Trump eased additional tariffs on many countries that export goods to the U.S., he has kept a 25% levy on all imported vehicles.
Consumers are rushing to showrooms to try to save thousands of dollars on a new vehicle.
Cox Automotive estimates the 25% tariff on non-U.S. assembled vehicles will increase the average cost of imported vehicles by $6,000, while the cost of vehicles assembled in the U.S. will rise by $3,600 due to upcoming 25% tariffs on automotive parts. Those are in addition to $300 to $500 hikes as a result of previously announced tariffs on steel and aluminum.
Automotive executives and dealers reported significant gains in showroom traffic and sales once Trump confirmed the tariffs late last month and into April.

data.author: domofutu
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了2025年美国政府大幅削减国家科学基金会（NSF）、国立卫生研究院（NIH）和NASA科学部门预算的情况，以及这对科学界的潜在影响。作者埃里克·霍尔表达了对学术界被视为腐败并因此不值得拯救的虚无主义观点的担忧。文章指出，有人建议将科学研究从传统学术机构转移到更商业化的环境，如硅谷。现任总统科学顾问迈克尔·克拉齐奥斯与硅谷有深厚联系，但缺乏科学背景，这引发了对科学研究未来方向的讨论。作者质疑这种转变是否可行及有益。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对科学研究的价值以及学术体系的批评

不同观点：
• [riehwvfbk] 认为并非所有的科学研究都在产生有价值的结果。其指出，大多数大学并不像哈佛那样具有高水平的研究能力，很多实验室从事的是非常明显且 incremental（渐进的、小步伐的）工作。这些实验室通常为了获取科研经费和发表更多论文，追随当前热门的研究方向。此外，研究生大多是移民，他们从事科学研究的主要动机并不是出于对科学的热爱，而是为了最终获得在美国工作的许可。

• [BLKNSLVR] 则将话题引向了对特朗普时期美国政策的担忧，暗示科学研究的价值和学术体系的问题可能是更广泛政治背景下的一个表现。这种观点没有直接回应前者的具体论点，而是将讨论与更大的政治环境联系起来。

补充讨论：
• [riehwvfbk] 强调了学术体系中的功利性问题，尤其是科研资金和论文发表的压力如何影响了研究的质量和原创性。
• [BLKNSLVR] 的回应则将讨论引向了一个更广泛的政治层面，表明科学研究的问题可能与政府政策和更广泛的社会背景有关。
• 两者之间的讨论焦点在于科学研究的价值以及学术体系中的动机问题，其中[riehwvfbk] 关注微观的学术动机和研究质量，而[BLKNSLVR] 则从宏观的政治角度看待这一问题。

Art for
The Intrinsic Perspective
is by
Alexander Naughton
New directives from on high, shouted from a governmental megaphone at scientists, might not be so bad if they were clear. But since they are very much unclear, there is a new mood among my fellow scientists:
paranoia.
I don’t remember this ever happening before.
The director of the National Science Foundation—which, for all major scientific fields, except biology/medicine, is the main federal funder of basic research—resigned
yesterday
after the NSF was ordered to be cut by 55%. Meanwhile, the NIH (biology/medicine) is proposed to be
cut by 40%
, and NASA’s science division
by 50%
. These numbers will likely change to some degree in Congress, but the proposals are already having tangible effects everywhere. Science has, in terms of inflows of funding, been slowed to a trickle in 2025.
source
To litigate all that led to this, politically, would take a book. The stated reason for the cuts to science is obvious, best seen in the fight between the
Trump administration and Harvard
around the role of DEI requirements in admissions, hiring, and grants. But let’s just be honest: that doesn’t explain cutting 55% of the NSF budget.
Subscribe
Thus, the unstated reason is worth examining. If you criticize academia as a sclerotic and ailing institution, then you are a doctor, and should be seeking cures. If you view ideological creep within science as cancer, then the goal is to kill the cancer and keep the patient. Yet, there’s a new nihilism based on the idea that academia is entirely corrupt. And things entirely corrupt are not worth saving.
It’s a view only possible if an alternative is available. Academia houses the crown jewel of science. If academia is not to be saved, where does science go?
A possible hint comes from the current Science Advisor to the President:
Michael Kratsios
. As far as I can tell, he is the first confirmed in that position, created 49 years ago, to not actually be a scientist. There’s not one scientific citation to his name. But he does have deep ties to Silicon Valley, and was even Peter Thiel’s former chief of staff.
Of course, I don’t know what Trump or Kratsios personally believes. But I do think that the nihilistic view of academia, at least more nebulously at a cultural level, is fed by a whisper: Why not just do a little swap? Why not trade all those pompous ivy-covered campuses for something slicker and less janky? Why not take the crown jewel of science and box it up in a package white and molded, like an Apple product?

data.title: Netflix introduces a new kind of subtitles for the non-hearing impaired
data.author: furcyd
data.article_summary: 约一半的美国家庭在观看电视和电影时使用字幕，尽管其中只有少数家庭有听力障碍成员。许多人感到在现代观看环境中难以听清对话，因此Netflix引入了一种新的字幕选项，仅显示对话文字，不包括角色名称、音乐提示和音效描述，以减少干扰。这种新格式将在新的Netflix原创节目中提供，并逐步扩展至旧节目。传统的隐藏字幕仍然可用，标记为"English CC"，而新选项仅标记为"English"。这一变化是针对当前影视作品中更自然的表演风格和流媒体音频压缩导致的对话清晰度问题的一个解决方案。各类硬件制造商和音频工程师仍在寻求更好的解决办法。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕影视作品中的对话音轨和音效/音乐提示的争议，以及字幕和音频处理的体验和改进建议。

不同观点：
• **WalterGR**：认为音效和音乐提示不会对观赏体验造成阻碍，开启字幕只是个人习惯。但对于阅读速度较慢的人或认为提示打破“第四面墙”的观众，可能会觉得提示令人分心。

• **mrandish**：指出音频混合问题应由专业音频工程师在制作阶段解决，而不是由观众在家通过自动化插件解决。认为现代音频技术已经足够先进，音频工程师有责任确保对话音轨的清晰度，动态范围过大和不正确的声音混合是问题的根源。

• **monetus**：认为对话音轨功能很有必要，但仍需通过音频混合器进一步优化体验。这一功能并不能完全取代其他音频处理工具。

• **solardev**：质疑该功能是否真的是新事物，指出流媒体服务和视频游戏早已提供类似选项（如SDH字幕）。同时指出Netflix等平台可能早已提供此类功能。

• **pulvinar**：批评当前影视表演风格过于自然化，导致对话声音过小，影响观赏体验。认为选择“经典”音频轨道是更好的解决方案，而不是依赖字幕。

• **conartist6**：对该功能的出现表示欢迎，暗示等待此功能已久。

• **stevage**：讨论了在多语言字幕处理上的困扰，指出在打开字幕时所有对话都被字幕化，而不是仅针对外语部分，认为这一问题亟待解决。

• **satellite2**：对比YouTube的字幕显示方式，批评其逐字显示影响观赏体验。对Netflix在此方面的改进表示赞赏。

• **raphael_l**：提到字幕有时会提前透露角色身份信息，而不是仅描述对话特征（如“沙哑的声音”），认为这可能是外包字幕制作中对剧情暴露不够重视所致。

• **instagib**：建议通过增强对话音量和调整播放速度来改善观赏体验。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**：音频混合和对话清晰度问题是否应由制作方解决，还是可以通过观众端的工具（如音频插件或字幕）解决。部分观众认为音频工程师在制作过程中应更注重音频平衡，而不是依赖观众自行调整。

• **字幕的使用体验**：不同观众对字幕的需求和偏好存在差异，部分观众认为字幕会分散注意力，而其他人则认为字幕是必要的辅助工具。

• **现有功能的新颖性**：部分评论者认为对话音轨和字幕选项并非新功能，早已在其他平台上存在。

Multiple studies and investigations have found that about half of American households watch TV and movies with subtitles on, but only a relatively small portion of those include someone with a hearing disability. That's because of the trouble many people have understanding dialogue in modern viewing situations, and Netflix has now
introduced
a subtitles option to help.
The closed captioning we've all been using for years includes not only the words the people on-screen are saying, but additional information needed by the hard of hearing, including character names, music cues ("dramatic music intensifies") and sound effects ("loud explosion").
For those who just wanted to make sure they didn't miss a word here and there, the frequent descriptions of sound effects and music could be distracting. This new format omits those extras, just including the spoken words and nothing else—even in the same language as the spoken dialogue.
The feature will be available in new Netflix original programming, starting with the new season of
You
in multiple languages. Netflix says it's looking at bringing the option to older titles in the library (including those not produced by Netflix) in the future.
Traditional closed captions are still available, of course. Those are labeled "English CC" whereas this new option is simply labeled "English" (or whatever your preferred language is).
This is just the latest answer to a long-standing problem. Streamers and device makers have been including speech or dialogue boost
audio modes
to help users better understand dialogue, too. There's no single reason this is now a problem that needs solving—rather, it's a confluence of things.
The performance style of actors in current TV shows and movies is more naturalistic and less elocutive than it once was, so characters are more likely to speak softly. Streaming services compress the audio more vigorously than is common in physical media, which can cause problems with intelligibility. The range of home audio hardware is far wider than ever before, so engineers and editors mastering shows and films face the near-impossible task of providing strong dynamic range and quality for those with high-end systems, but still making it sound good on cheap TV speakers.
It's a relatively new problem, and everyone from hardware makers to audio engineers is seeking the ideal solution. Netflix's new subtitles don't really fix it, of course, but they make the viewing experience a little nicer for the millions of people who've resorted to reading subtitles all the time.
Samuel Axon
Senior Editor
Samuel Axon
Senior Editor
Samuel Axon is a senior editor at Ars Technica, where he is the editorial director for tech and gaming coverage. He covers AI, software development, gaming, entertainment, and mixed reality. He has been writing about gaming and technology for nearly two decades at Engadget, PC World, Mashable, Vice, Polygon, Wired, and others. He previously ran a marketing and PR agency in the gaming industry, led editorial for the TV network CBS, and worked on social media marketing strategy for Samsung Mobile at the creative agency SPCSHP. He also is an independent software and game developer for iOS, Windows, and other platforms, and he is a graduate of DePaul University, where he studied interactive media and software development.

data.title: Breitspurbahn
data.author: zeristor
data.article_summary: **Breitspurbahn**是纳粹德国计划建造的超宽轨距铁路系统，轨距为3000毫米（9英尺10又1/8英寸），远超西欧使用的1435毫米（4英尺8又1/2英寸）标准轨距。该铁路最初计划连接大德意志帝国及其邻国的主要城市。由于一战后赔款导致的资金短缺，德国铁路公司Deutsche Reichsbahn难以扩展和维护其铁路网。随着纳粹党崛起和经济复苏，铁路交通量增加，政府开始计划现代化铁路网并提升运输能力。希特勒认为斯蒂芬森标准轨距过时，不足以支撑铁路的全面发展，因此采纳了弗里茨·托特的建议，计划建造新高容量铁路Reichsspurbahn，采用超宽轨距。尽管铁路专家反对，希特勒仍下令建设，初期规划线路包括汉堡、柏林、纽伦堡、慕尼黑和林茨。该项目得到了多家公司的参与，但最终仅停留在线路规划阶段，未实际建设。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：纳粹德国3米宽轨铁路的利弊及其设计目的

不同观点：
• **stevage 的观点**：
  - 最初计划的4米宽轨被缩减到3米，设计中去掉了枕木和道砟，以便在战争时期可以让车辆直接在铁路上行驶。
  - 提出宽轨铁路的一个缺点：需要非常宽的弯道，这在实际应用中可能存在问题。
  - 认为文章没有对选择宽轨铁路的理由进行充分解释，缺乏对该设计决策的合理论证。

• **zeristor 的观点**：
  - 简短评论，提到纳粹德国的3米宽轨铁路，但没有深入展开利弊分析或提供额外背景。

补充讨论：
- 宽轨铁路的设计初衷可能是为了提高运输效率，尤其是在战争时期，能够让车辆直接在铁路上行驶是一个显著优势。
- **争议焦点**在于宽轨铁路的实用性和实际操作中的技术难题，特别是宽轨所需的宽弯道是否会对铁路建设造成重大限制。
- **未解答的问题**包括：为什么选择3米宽轨而不是其他尺寸，以及这种设计在现代是否仍然具有实际意义。

The
Breitspurbahn
(
German pronunciation:
[ˈbʁaɪtʃpuːɐ̯baːn]
,
transl.
broad-gauge railway
) was a railway system planned and partly surveyed by
Nazi Germany
. Its
track gauge
– the distance between the two running rails – was to be
3000 mm
(
9 ft
10
+
1
⁄
8
in
), more than twice that of the
1435 mm
(
4 ft
8
+
1
⁄
2
in
) standard gauge used in western Europe. The railway was intended initially to run between major cities of the
Greater Germanic Reich
(the regime's expanded Germany)
[
1
]
and neighbouring states.
History
[
edit
]
Since
reparations
due after World War I had to be paid, the German railway company
Deutsche Reichsbahn
lacked money for appropriate expansion and sufficient maintenance of their track network and rolling stock.
[
2
]
Commercial and civilian traffic increased due to economic stimulation after the rise of the
NSDAP
and Hitler's
seizure of power
. Deutsche Reichsbahn was now faced with a serious capacity problem. As a result, in part driven by its military objectives, the government began to prepare plans to modernize the railway network and increase transport capacity. Hitler believed that the standard
Stephenson gauge
was obsolete and was too narrow for the full development of railways.
[
1
]
Also, as Hitler envisioned the future German empire as essentially a land-based Empire, the new German railways were imagined as a land-based equivalent of the
ocean liners
and freighters connecting the maritime
British Empire
.
[
1
]
Hitler embraced a suggestion from
Fritz Todt
to build a new high-capacity
Reichsspurbahn
(imperial gauge railway) with notably increased gauge. Objections from railway experts – who foresaw difficulties in introducing a new, incompatible gauge (and proposed
quadruple track
standard gauge lines instead), and who could not imagine any use for the vast transport capacity of such a railway – were ignored, and Hitler ordered the
Breitspurbahn
to be built with initial lines between Hamburg, Berlin, Nuremberg, Munich and Linz.
The project engaged commercial partners
Krauss-Maffei
;
Henschel
;
Borsig
;
Brown, Boveri & Cie
and
Krupp
, but did not develop beyond line planning

  - 提出宽轨铁路的一个缺点：需要非常宽的弯道，这在实际应用中可能存在问题。

• **zeristor 的观点**：
  - 简短评论，提到纳粹德国的3米宽轨铁路，但没有深入展开利弊分析或提供额外背景。

补充讨论：
- 宽轨铁路的设计初衷可能是为了提高运输效率，尤其是在战争时期，能够让车辆直接在铁路上行驶是一个显著优势。
- **争议焦点**在于宽轨铁路的实用性和实际操作中的技术难题，特别是宽轨所需的宽弯道是否会对铁路建设造成重大限制。

data.article_summary:
这篇文章讨论了汽车无钥匙进入系统（RKS）的安全性问题。无钥匙进入系统使用遥控钥匙（key fob），允许车主无需物理钥匙即可开锁和启动汽车。然而，这些系统并非总是安全，低成本硬件可能被用于破解系统，从而导致汽车被盗。

文章详细介绍了钥匙fob的工作原理，包括其使用的频率（如美国为315 MHz）以及如何通过软件定义无线电（SDR）检测信号。钥匙fob使用滚动码生成唯一信号，汽车和钥匙保持同步以验证下个代码。若按键过多而不同步，汽车将无法识别钥匙。

攻击方法包括录制钥匙信号以重放开锁，或逆向工程滚动码序列。某些情况下，由于系统设计缺陷，破解变得相对容易。最终，文章提醒用户这些系统并非绝对安全，依赖于汽车厂商的安全设计和实施。

不同观点：

补充讨论：
• **厂商与车主责任的争议**：[madphilosopher]建议厂商为存在漏洞的车型承担保险费用，以此激励厂商修复问题。[neogodless]分享了其Polestar应用与车钥匙配对失败的经历，显示出技术实现中的实际问题。

• **用户对安全措施的无奈**：[1970-01-01]半开玩笑地提出“输入密码解锁汽车”的建议，反映出对现有“持有物”认证方式安全性的不信任。

争议焦点：汽车厂商是否应为钥匙系统漏洞承担更多责任，以及现有技术能否有效且经济地解决无钥匙系统安全性问题。

Assignment 5: Cars and Key Fobs
Overview
Almost all cars currently come with a key fob, which allows you to open the doors, and start the car.  When you buy a car, the convenience is the compelling feature.  You can leave the key fob in your pocket, and never again worry about having a physical key. It sounds great.
The implicit assumption you make is that the key fob system is secure, and that some random person with $50 of hardware can't drive off with your car.  You have no real way to tell whether the car company did a reasonable job with their system, so you have to trust them.  Unfortunately, that trust is not always warranted.  And it isn't until people try to hack these systems that the problems come out.  Problems that less scrupulous people may have already been exploiting.
Your Car's Key Fob
There are lots of different key fob systems.  We'll start by looking at the key fob for my 2006 Prius. Key fobs use something called a Remote Keyless System (RKS).  In the U.S. these operate at 315 MHz, +/- 2.5 MHz.  My Prius key turned out to be at 312.590 MHz.The keyfobs are all listed in the FCC database.  Watching for new entries is one of the ways people can tell when new car models are coming out. These will appear long before the official announcement.
You can figure out what frequency your key fob transmits on using your SDR and use GQRX or SDR# to monitor the spectrum.  When you push a button on the fob, you should see a brief jump in the spectrum.  You may need to shift the frequency band up or down by a couple of MHz to find the signal, mine was almost 2.5 MHz low.
One word of caution.  Don't get too carried away pushing the button!  The RKS system uses a rolling pseudo-randomly generated code.  Both the key fob and the car keep in sync, so that the car recognizes the next code.  However, if the key fob gets too far ahead in the sequence (100s of button pushes) the car won't recognize it.  That makes the key (and the car) considerably less useful!
If we capture the signal the result is shown below
The total width of the plot is 10 seconds, so you can see there is one key press shortly after 2 seconds, and another shortly after 5 seconds.
If we plot 100 ms starting at 2 seconds, we can see the digital signal we are looking for:
Zooming in to the first couple of bits, we get
The bits are easy to identify.  A decision threshold of 15 will give almost perfect detection. If we do this, and then plot first part of the digital data for the two key presses, we get this
Although the two start the same, they rapidly diverge.  This is fortunate, because if the signal was the same every time, you'd have enough information to steal my car now!
The data is again on-off keying (OOK).  It is also almost certainly split phase  (or Manchester) encoding. Instead of a “1” being high, and a “0” being low, the information is  encoding in the transition from high to low or low to high. That means that a “0” bit is a rising transition, and a “1” bit is a falling transition.  A good way to recognize split phase encoding is that you can only have one or two low or high segments in a row.  The nice thing about Manchester encoding is that every symbol has a transition, and these are easier to find then when the signal has been high or low for several intervals.
This example is OOK, which is the most common for car remotes.  Some use frequency-shift keying (FSK), where each bit is transmitted as a different frequency, and the envelope is constant.
Attacks on Car Remotes
There are lots of different attacks that can be used against car remotes, depending on how they work, and what sort of access you are looking for.  The simplest just let you open the car up.  More thorough attacks give you complete control by basically cloning the remote.
Most key fobs use a rolling key. This produces a new waveform that depends on the ID of the key fob, a random seed, and how many times the key has been pressed.  The car keeps track of the last code it received, and knows what the next several hundred codes might be.  If it detects one of the expected future codes it opens the car.  If it gets a previously used code, it stops responding to the key fob.  For the Prius you have to do the
“Chicken Dance”
to get it to work again, provided you have another working key fob.  Otherwise, you have to have the dealer rekey the car, for many hundreds of dollars. I have had to do this a couple times, now (for other reasons).
There are several lines of attack.  One is simply recording the key fob output for a couple of button presses when it is away from the car, or the car is being jammed.  With recorded unused codes, you can open the car.
Another is to reverse engineer the RKS sequence.  In general this should be extremely hard.  However, there have been several situations where this is very easy.

data.author: geox
data.article_summary: 美国司法部长帕姆·邦迪警告称，威斯康星州法官汉娜·杜根的被捕只是特朗普政府对司法系统执法打击的开始。杜根因涉嫌帮助一名移民逃避逮捕而被捕，她被控两项联邦妨碍罪。特朗普的移民政策坚定捍卫者邦迪表示，任何庇护逃犯或帮助非法移民的人都将被追责。杜根的律师则称，逮捕不符合公共安全利益。与此同时，特朗普政府在全美范围内对移民法官展开攻击，已有八名法官被解雇或停职。民主党和相关人士对此事件表示震惊和强烈关注。

Attorney General Pam Bondi
warned
Friday that the arrest of a judge in Wisconsin was only the beginning of Donald Trump’s law enforcement crackdown on the judiciary.
Judge Hannah Dugan was
arrested
earlier in the day on charges of obstruction for supposedly misdirecting Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents away from Eduardo Flores-Ruiz, an immigrant attending a pretrial hearing at the Milwaukee County Courthouse last week.
While discussing the case during an
appearance
on Fox News, Bondi said that judges attempting to help immigrants evade arrest were “deranged.”
“I think some of these judges think they are beyond and above the law, and they are not,” Bondi said. “And we are sending a very strong message today: If you are harboring a fugitive, we don’t care who you are, if you are helping hide one, if you are giving a TdA member guns, anyone who is illegally in this country, we will come after you and we will prosecute you. We will find you.”
Crucially, Dugan is not accused of supplying a member of Tren de Aragua with guns. She is charged with two federal counts of obstruction, one for concealing a person from discovery and arrest, and another for obstruction of federal government proceedings.
According to the Department of Justice’s
filing
, Dugan allegedly let Florez-Ruiz enter the courtroom through a side door typically reserved for a jury. He then used a public hallway in the courthouse to get into an elevator and exit the building before ICE officers could stop him. If Dugan is convicted, the charges may result in a maximum penalty of six years in prison.
During an appearance in federal court Friday, Dugan’s lawyer Craig Mastantuono
said
that his client “wholeheartedly protests the arrest and believes it was not made in the interests of public safety.”
Bondi, who has been a fierce defender of the president’s immigration agenda—including its
wrongful deportation
of immigrants—has now taken up the mantle of antagonizing state and federal judges on behalf of the increasingly hostile executive branch.
Last week, Trump’s director of counterterrorism
argued
that anyone opposed to Trump’s immigration agenda was “aiding and abetting” terrorists.
Dugan’s arrest comes as Trump continues his widespread attack on immigration judges, eight of whom have been
fired
or put on leave in the last week across California, Massachusetts, and Louisiana.

Democrats Erupt After Trump’s FBI Arrests Sitting Judge

• tlogan指出，AI无法解决用户不清楚自己目标的问题，很多用户在使用AI增强的UI时，无法清晰表达自己的目标。AI可能放大这种模糊性，且可能阻碍用户对工具的深度学习和掌握。他认为当前很多AI功能只是为了添加而添加，缺乏深思熟虑。

• mNovak批评了一些过度宣传的AI功能，例如Gmail的"总结此邮件"按钮，认为这些功能并不实用。他还指出，许多有用的AI功能是用户不易察觉的，比如自动化过滤垃圾邮件，这些功能虽然提供了实际价值，但不够吸引眼球。

• oceanplexian讨论了AI生成内容的风格问题，提出AI生成的内容可以通过提示和微调来变得更像人类写作。他还猜测大公司可能故意让AI生成一些让人感到不安的内容，以避免用户对AI的能力感到过于惊讶。

• pmarreck提出了一种完全自动化的邮件草稿生成系统，认为可以通过AI分析用户的发件风格来自动生成邮件，用户只需审核批准。但他质疑这种趋势是否会导致人们仅仅成为“工作审核者”而非“工作执行者”。

• throwaway2037用一种讽刺的方式将使用Gemini帮助写邮件比作管理一个表现不佳的员工，认为这种体验浪费时间且效果不佳。

• kristjank对使用AI代理来增强或替代个人消息表达持谨慎态度，认为AI生成的消息缺乏个性化的表达，且可能导致信息传递的失真。

• benterris不理解为何人们希望AI代写消息，尤其是对于亲密的交流，认为这种做法剥夺了交流的个人性。

• kkoncevicius担心AI应用的极限会完全消除人类之间的互动，例如在邮件回复和视频生成等领域，AI可能最终取代人类的创造性和互动性。

• dvt呼吁新的UX/UI范式和更智能的AI产品，认为当前的聊天界面和提示写作方式不理想，且AI工具应更智能地调用其他工具来弥补其在逻辑和数据处理方面的不足。

• kfajdsl对比了大公司与个人开发者在AI集成方面的表现，认为个人开发者能更快速有效地实现有用的AI功能，而大公司常常推出不完善的产品。

• minimaxir批评了AI生成的预填充回复功能，尤其是在社交媒体和邮件中，认为这种功能不仅效果差，还可能被公司利用来增加用户参与度以提升财报数据。

• darth_avocado认为Google等公司不推出AI阅读和分类邮件功能的原因是这会影响其广告收入，因为用户不再亲自阅读邮件意味着广告商无法通过吸引用户注意来获利。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于AI功能是否真正提升了用户体验，还是仅仅为了追赶AI热潮而添加。许多评论者认为当前的AI功能多为噱头，缺乏实用性，且可能阻碍用户的深度学习和创造性。
• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是AI对人类互动的影响，有评论者担心AI可能完全取代人类之间的互动，从而削弱交流的个人性和真实性。
• 关于AI在邮件和其他个人信息处理方面的应用，评论者普遍认为AI缺乏个性化和深度理解，可能导致信息传递的失真。

data.title: Berkeley Humanoid Lite – Open-source robot
data.author: ratsbane
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一款由加州大学伯克利分校开发的开源、可定制且价格可负担的3D打印人形机器人——Berkeley Humanoid Lite。该机器人设计强调模块化和易于制造，所有组件均可通过电商平台获取，并使用桌面3D打印机制造，总成本控制在5000美元以内。为了解决3D打印齿轮箱强度和耐用性不足的问题，研究团队采用了摆线齿轮设计。实验验证了3D打印执行器的耐用性，并通过强化学习开发了运动控制器，成功展示了从模拟到实际硬件的零样本策略转移。该平台旨在促进人形机器人技术的民主化，所有硬件设计、嵌入式代码及训练部署框架均开源，便于全球研究人员使用。平台在成本效益对比中表现出色，提供了高性能且低成本的解决方案。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：机器人技术的可行性、成本、开放性以及在家庭环境中的应用潜力

不同观点：
• lifeisstillgood认为制造人形机器人非常困难，尤其是在家庭环境中，直接改造环境比制造一个灵活的机器人更实际。不过，每天清洁一小时的机器人是有可能实现的。
• RetroTeche认为3D打印并不是降低成本的唯一途径，批量生产的机械部件加上可编程的“大脑”才是更有效的解决方案。最坏的情况是替换控制电子元件，如电机驱动等。
• bjackman对开放平台的概念表示支持，认为当前的核心硬件问题已经基本解决，接下来的重点应是降低成本、扩大硬件设计空间，并解决软件方面的巨大挑战。

补充讨论：
• larodi提到Berkeley Humanoid被标记为“闭源”的疑问，并质疑相关文献是否经过同行评审。
• frainfreeze对机器人性能指标（如扭矩和自由度）与可访问性和可定制性之间的关系表示困惑，认为这些指标可能具有误导性。
• em0sh以专业机械工程师的身份批评了性能因素与扭矩、自由度之间的对比，认为这种比较毫无意义。
• gitroom表示对开放源码机器人技术的兴趣，认为这种趋势激发了DIY和实验的热情。
• DonHopkins通过分享视频链接，展示机器人服务的不同场景，如侍者机器人、情感机器人等，从实际案例出发讨论机器人应用。
• bk496和demaga对开放源码机器人技术表示支持和期待，认为这是未来的重要方向，且具有很大的潜力。

争议焦点：
1. 机器人技术在家用环境中的实际应用价值和实现难度。
2. 降低机器人成本的最佳途径，包括3D打印与批量生产机械部件的对比。
3. 机器人性能指标的合理性和可理解性，尤其是与可定制性的关系。

总体来看，讨论围绕机器人技术的可行性、成本、开放性和在家庭中的应用潜力展开，参与者提供了不同的技术路径和观点。

Berkeley Humanoid Lite: An Open-source, Accessible, and Customizable 3D-printed Humanoid Robot
Robotics: Science and Systems (RSS) 2025
Yufeng Chi
,
Qiayuan Liao
,
Junfeng Long
,
Xiaoyu Huang
,
Sophia Shao
,
Borivoje Nikolic
,
Zhongyu Li
,
Koushil Sreenath
University of California, Berkeley
Paper
arXiv
Video
Code
Documentation
Abstract
Despite significant interest and advancements in humanoid robotics, most existing commercially available hardware remains high-cost, closed-source, and non-transparent within the robotics community. This lack of accessibility and customization hinders the growth of the field and the broader development of humanoid technologies. To address these challenges and promote democratization in humanoid robotics, we demonstrate
Berkeley Humanoid Lite
, an open-source humanoid robot designed to be accessible, customizable, and beneficial for the entire community.
The core of this design is a modular 3D-printed gearbox for the actuators and robot body. All components can be sourced from widely available e-commerce platforms and fabricated using standard desktop 3D printers, keeping the total hardware cost under $5,000 (based on U.S. market prices). The design emphasizes modularity and ease of fabrication. To address the inherent limitations of 3D-printed gearboxes, such as reduced strength and durability compared to metal alternatives, we adopted a cycloidal gear design, which provides an optimal form factor in this context. Extensive testing was conducted on the 3D-printed actuators to validate their durability and alleviate concerns about the reliability of plastic components. To demonstrate the capabilities of Berkeley Humanoid Lite, we conducted a series of experiments, including the development of a locomotion controller using reinforcement learning. These experiments successfully showcased zero-shot policy transfer from simulation to hardware, highlighting the platform's suitability for research validation.
By making the hardware design, embedded code, and training and deployment frameworks fully open-source and globally accessible, we aim for Berkeley Humanoid Lite to serve as a pivotal step toward democratizing the development of humanoid robotics.
Demonstrations
Playing with a Rubik's Cube
Writing its name with a marker
Playing with blocks
Locomotion in bipedal configuration
Comparision
To be able to benchmark against other robots and illustrate our focus on accessibility and customizability while maintaining sufficient performance, we introduce a quantitative metric that captures cost-effectiveness. Specifically, we define the performance factor as the average peak torque of all actuated DoFs, normalized by the robot's size:
\begin{equation}
\hat{p} = \frac{1}{N h mg} \sum_{i=1}^N |\tau_i^{\max}|.
\end{equation}
$N$ denotes the number of actuated DoFs, $h$ and $mg$ represent the height and weight of the robot, and $|\tau_i^{\max}|$ represents the maximum torque of the i-th joint motor. The performance factor per dollar is then defined as the performance factor divided by the cost or selling price of the robot:
\begin{equation}
\varphi = \frac{\hat{p}}{\text{cost}}.
\end{equation}
As shown in the figure below, our platform achieves high performance factor with a cost lower than
$5000
.

data.title: I wrote a book called "Crap Towns". It seemed funny at the time
data.author: url
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对《Crap Towns》类书籍及其幽默在当下是否仍合适的分析

不同观点：
• jdietrich认为，二十年前人们还能一起自嘲小镇的无聊和平庸，但现在这种集体身份感已消失。他指出，不同城镇的命运已发生巨大分化，过去那些共同的平庸符号（如Woolworths等连锁店）已不复存在，取而代之的是精品店或慈善商店等。他还提到，上层中产阶级变得更加严肃和清教徒式，而工人阶级则充满愤怒，不再愿意被嘲笑。

• svat赞赏文章没有陷入“政治正确”的简单争论，而是深入探讨为什么过去那些自嘲的玩笑现在不再好笑。他认为，这不仅仅是幽默变化的问题，而是社会希望和集体情绪的变化。

• amiga386提到一个类似《Crap Towns》的网站“ChavTowns”，并指出该网站因缺乏访问量，其所有者已放弃维护。他还提到该网站被媒体盗用内容以获取流量。

• Centigonal引用了原文，指出《Crap Towns》式的幽默现在看起来“肮脏”且可能残酷，不再适合当下。他还反思了这种变化是否一定是坏事。

• Yossarrian22认为，那些被书称为“垃圾”的城镇在书籍出版时并不被认为是如此，而现在记得那个时代的人已老去。

• fallous认为，幽默应关注人类普遍经验，而非仅仅一时流行。他指出，不同年龄段的人对幽默的理解不同，并质疑“一代人认为自己发现了新事物”的自负。

• smelendez认为，类似的幽默仍存在于年轻人中，但可能不再适合作为书籍出版，尤其是幽默类咖啡桌书籍已不再流行。

• thomassmith65赞赏作者的写作能力，指出读者容易忘记“现在无法出版《Crap Towns》”是假设。

• ChrisMarshallNY回忆了一个早期网站“sheppeyscum.com”，指出因死亡威胁该网站已消失，反映出某些幽默的极端反应。

• PaulRobinson认为，关键在于幽默是“向上打”还是“向下打”。如果《Crap Towns》是为了批评政治失败，则是好的讽刺；如果是嘲笑工人阶级，则是欺负。

• econ指出，缺乏对“垃圾城镇”的明确定义使得讨论难以进行。

• zeroq分享了一个关于描绘城镇丑陋面的书籍的例子，认为这种幽默带有怀旧和历史意义。

• Sparkyte支持这种类型的书籍，认为能给人提供新的视角。

• mmaunder批评当下对思想和幽默的审查和压迫，认为青年应质疑规则而不是盲目执行。

• bryanrasmussen认为，在美国只有少数城市的居民会对被列入“垃圾城镇”书籍感到 insulted，并质疑哪些人群过去会买这类书而现在不会。

补充讨论：
• 幽默的时代性和社会背景：不同年代的幽默反映了当时的社会情绪和集体身份。
• 政治正确与幽默：文章探讨了幽默和政治正确之间的复杂关系，以及幽默在不同社会背景下的接受度。

data.title: Reading RSS content is a skilled activity
data.author: d0liver
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了互联网从早期有趣和利他性质演变为如今充满负面影响的现状，尤其是广告商通过算法操控用户注意力，导致用户体验受损。作者提出通过RSS技术重新掌控注意力的可能性。与社交媒体不同，RSS阅读器让用户自主决定观看内容，初始时内容未经过滤，用户需通过信任链逐步筛选和订阅值得注意的信息源。这一过程需要像打理花园一样，定期修剪和去除杂草，最终形成多样化且无干扰的内容集合。使用RSS不仅是信息聚合，更是一种技能和习惯，使用户拥有对自己注意力的控制权。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：RSS阅读的价值、使用方式及其潜在问题

不同观点：
• [kgwxd] 认为RSS的优点在于不需要重新查看已经决定不读的内容，偶尔提到RSS能让他重新使用RSS阅读器。
• [bsnnkv] 强调与内容互动并决定其价值的过程让RSS阅读体验更好，主张"现在读或永远不读"的策略，避免积压未读内容。
• [bitbasher] 认为RSS阅读器有助于控制内容消费，避免陷入社交媒体的"兔子洞"。
• [soapdog] 提出可以通过使用具有更平静用户体验的RSS阅读器来减少信息过载，例如其开发的BlogCat阅读器，允许用户自定义查看帖子的频率和数量。
• [rambambram] 分享自建RSS阅读器的经验，通过随机选择订阅源来减少信息过载，并指出适应这种信息控制方式需要时间。
• [simonw] 认为RSS不仅仅是为了逃避算法控制，还应通过信任链来筛选信息源，找到具有良好判断力和品味的人进行订阅。
• [mnls] 指出RSS虽然摆脱了社交媒体平台的控制，但仍受制于发布者的控制，可能导致信息过载，最终成为数字负担。
• [mbanerjeepalmer] 将RSS用户分为两类：一类是精心修剪订阅源的人，另一类是认识到RSS也是一种"专制"的人，并提出可以使用LLM或嵌入模型来过滤低相关性内容。
• [nexo-v1] 认为RSS阅读的维护需要精力，但值得，因为最好的系统往往是通过小而定期的维护来维持的。
• [AstroBen] 分享了一些有用的RSS资源，如HN RSS和RSSHub。
• [1dom] 强调自我策划的重要性，认为如果将信息策划外包给他人，可能会导致信息消费状态偏离自己的期望。
• [lexoj] 通过自建工具生成每日摘要来减少压力，只关注当天的内容。
• [tducasse] 选择付费托管的RSS服务Miniflux，通过少量订阅和快速标记不感兴趣的内容来管理信息。
• [nickdothutton] 通过引入与现有订阅源观点相反的信息源来避免回声室效应。

补充讨论：
- RSS阅读的价值在于自我控制和信息筛选，但需要投入精力进行维护。
- 不同用户有不同的RSS使用策略，如"现在读或永远不读"、随机选择订阅源、信任链筛选等。
- 信息过载和数字负担是RSS用户面临的主要问题，一些用户通过技术工具和策略来缓解这些问题。
- 自我策划和避免回声室效应是RSS用户关注的重要方面。

43799697.article_content:
Shit's gotten weird out there. The internet has devolved from something that was mostly quirky and altruistic to something that, in many ways, is straight-up evil. Companies have commoditized user attention through an economic framework that is completely divorced from the user's experience: Advertisers go to some ad platform, set up a few tags, and third parties shill for them without knowing anything about advertiser or user. The user's experience is determined by some algorithm whose sole purpose is to increase engagement, so the effects on the user are harmful and unknown, and advertisers don't care.
Enter RSS: An opportunity to reclaim your attention through simple and open tech. Unfortunately, I've bailed on all of my attempts at using RSS readers up to this point because there's simply too much content to sift through. But, I'm finally realizing what was right in front of my face: The experience of using an RSS reader
is
and
should be
characteristically different than using other forms of social media. With an RSS reader, you decide what you see; in order to
decide
you must start with something
undecided
meaning
unfiltered
.
So, how do we decide and filter for ourselves? My favored approach is fairly old fashioned: Chains of trust. We start by finding someone whose
judgement
we trust and subscribing to their feed, and then we find out who they trust and subscribe to their feed, and so on. Part of the
judgement
that we're looking for in these trustees is not simply whether or not content is
accurate
but whether or not it is worth our
attention
. Over time, we can curate our little garden of content, make it diverse, and eliminate unnecessary noise. But, much like a real garden, pruning and weeding is essential and intentional. So, using an RSS reader is more than having a nice aggregator: It's a skill and a routine. And that's also where the magic lies because it's that very process of engaging with content and deciding whether or not it has value to you that makes using an RSS reader a better experience and one where you own your attention.

data.title: Mathematicians just solved a 125-year-old problem, uniting 3 theories in physics
data.author: mikhael
data.article_summary: 数学家于2025年宣布，他们可能解决了希尔伯特第六问题中的一个关键目标，即统一解释流体运动的三种物理理论。希尔伯特于1900年提出这一问题，旨在通过数学公理化物理学理论。具体而言，这涉及微观层面的牛顿运动定律、介观层面的玻尔兹曼方程以及宏观层面的欧拉和纳维-斯托克斯方程。这些理论分别描述了流体在不同尺度下的行为，但一直缺乏严格的数学证明来统一它们。芝加哥大学的于登云和密歇根大学的扎赫尔·哈尼、肖马通过最新研究，提供了数学上的严谨证明，弥合了这些理论间的 gap。这一突破不仅增强了对流体运动方程的信心，还可能推动其他物理领域的类似进展。

Mathematicians Crack 125-Year-Old Problem, Unite Three Physics Theories
A breakthrough in Hilbert’s sixth problem is a major step in grounding physics in math
By
Jack Murtagh
edited by
Jeanna Bryner
Mathematicians suggest they have figured out how to unify three physical theories that explain the motion of fluids.
Floriana/Getty Images
When the greatest mathematician alive unveils a vision for the next century of research, the math world takes note. That’s exactly what happened in 1900 at the International Congress of Mathematicians at Sorbonne University in Paris. Legendary mathematician
David Hilbert
presented
10 unsolved problems
as ambitious guideposts for the 20th century. He later expanded his list to include
23 problems
, and their influence on mathematical thought over the past 125 years cannot be overstated.
Hilbert’s sixth problem was one of the loftiest. He called for “axiomatizing” physics, or determining the bare minimum of mathematical assumptions behind all its theories. Broadly construed, it’s not clear that
mathematical physicists
could ever know if they had resolved this challenge. Hilbert mentioned some specific subgoals, however, and researchers have since refined his vision into concrete steps toward its solution.
In March mathematicians Yu Deng of the University of Chicago and Zaher Hani and Xiao Ma of the University of Michigan posted a new paper to the preprint server arXiv.org that
claims to have cracked one of these goals
. If their work withstands scrutiny, it will mark a major stride toward grounding physics in math and may open the door to analogous
breakthroughs in other areas of physics
.
On supporting science journalism
If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by
subscribing
. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
In the paper, the researchers suggest they have figured out how to unify three physical theories that explain the motion of fluids. These theories govern a range of engineering applications from aircraft design to weather prediction—but until now, they rested on assumptions that hadn’t been rigorously proven. This breakthrough won’t change the theories themselves, but it mathematically justifies them and strengthens our confidence that the equations work in the way we think they do.
Each theory differs in how much it zooms in on a flowing liquid or gas. At the microscopic level, fluids are composed of particles—little billiard balls bopping around and occasionally colliding—and
Newton’s laws of motion
work well to describe their trajectories.
But when you zoom out to consider the collective behavior of vast numbers of particles, the so-called mesoscopic level, it’s no longer convenient to model each one individually. In 1872 Austrian theoretical physicist Ludwig Boltzmann
addressed this when he developed what became known as the Boltzmann equation
. Instead of tracking the behavior of every particle, the equation considers the
likely
behavior of a
typical
particle. This statistical perspective smooths over the low-level details in favor of higher-level trends. The equation allows physicists to calculate how quantities such as momentum and thermal conductivity in the fluid evolve without painstakingly considering every microscopic collision.
Zoom out further, and you find yourself in the macroscopic world. Here we view fluids not as a collection of discrete particles but as a single continuous substance. At this level of analysis, a different suite of equations—the
Euler and Navier-Stokes equations
—accurately describe how fluids move and how their physical properties interrelate without recourse to particles at all.
The three levels of analysis each describe the same underlying reality—how fluids flow. In principle, each theory should build on the theory below it in the hierarchy: the Euler and Navier-Stokes equations at the macroscopic level should follow logically from the Boltzmann equation at the mesoscopic level, which in turn should follow logically from Newton’s laws of motion at the microscopic level. This is the kind of “axiomatization” that Hilbert called for in his sixth problem, and he explicitly referenced Boltzmann’s work on gases in his
write-up of the problem
. We expect complete theories of physics to follow mathematical rules that explain the phenomenon from the microscopic to the macroscopic levels. If scientists fail to bridge that gap, then it might suggest a misunderstanding in our existing theories.
Unifying the three perspectives on fluid dynamics has posed a stubborn challenge for the field, but Deng, Hani and Ma may have just done it. Their achievement builds on decades of incremental progress. • [dako2117] 提供了一个存档链接，暗示原始科学文章链接可能在未来不可用，因此使用存档链接可以确保信息的长期可访问性。这反映了对信息持久性和可访问性的关注。

• [paulpauper] 认为许多重要论文首先发表在arXiv上，质疑同行评审的作用，并提出arXiv上的快速发布有助于确立研究成果的优先权，像是一种时间戳，防止他人同期推导出相同结果并抢先发表获得认可。这涉及到对学术发表速度和优先权确立的重视。

• [SpaceManNabs] 赞赏文章对证明背景的清晰描述，特别是对三个尺度的解释，表明该文章在教育和传达复杂数学概念方面做得很好。这强调了科学文章在解释和背景提供上的重要性。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：[paulpauper] 的观点引发了对同行评审作用的质疑，传统上同行评审被视为确保学术质量的关键步骤，但快速在arXiv上发布以确立优先权的做法可能削弱这一过程的价值。

• 不同平台的角色：讨论中提到了Reddit、arXiv和存档网站等不同平台，它们在提供背景信息、快速发布研究成果以及确保信息持久性方面各有作用。

• 信息可访问性：[dako2117] 强调了使用存档链接的重要性，这反映了对学术信息长期可访问性的关注，尤其是在原始链接可能失效的情况下。

43799306.article_content:
Submit articles for inclusion in CACM’s new Practice section, dedicated to enhancing practitioners’ understanding of computing and improving job performance.
Communications of the ACM (CACM)
is the ACM’s flagship magazine. It is sent to all ACM members and its articles are available open access. Although
CACM
has long had a strong academic and research focus, it also regularly publishes articles of interest to practitioners.
CACM
is promoting its Practice section to be co-equal with its long-standing Research section. The new Practice section will accept submissions and publish articles of lasting interest to computing practitioners. We are seeking articles that enhance practitioners’ understanding of computing and enhance their job performance. If you could see your colleagues enthusiastically recommending an article to their friends and coworkers, we would love to publish it!
We are soliciting articles for CACM’s new Practice section!
What We’re Looking for
The scope of this section includes technical advances, development practices, organizational structures, examples of successful systems, and other topics of interest to computing practitioners. Articles need not be tied to academic or industrial research. However, they should be of interest to a significant number of practitioners. Highly specialized articles or articles demanding a deep technical background are unlikely to pass this test.
Specs
An article is limited to 10 pages, roughly equivalent to 6,000 words. A submission may have previously been posted on a blog or online but not published elsewhere. Authors retain copyright, and it is published with a CC-BY license.
Submission details and guidelines for authors are available
online.
View Author Guidelines
Potential authors are encouraged, but not required, to contact the Practice section’s co-chairs before submission to discuss their article:
Co-Chair
s:
Nachi Nagappan
Terence Kelly
Unlike most journals, we expect many of our authors do not publish regularly, so we are willing to advise and work with authors before an article is submitted. All articles will be reviewed by the Practice section’s editorial board and outside reviewers, meet ACM editorial standards, and be professionally edited by the CACM staff.
The Practice section will not publish vocational or tutorial articles on technologies. Numerous excellent websites and blogs provide detailed descriptions of specific software packages, applications, and programming languages. We seek articles that offer in-depth and lasting insights into ideas, tools, techniques, and practices that enable practitioners to stay current and advance in a rapidly evolving profession.
We also will not publish opinion pieces.
CACM
has an active Opinion section for commentary on issues of broad interest to the computing community.
For further questions, please contact the
CACM Editor-in-Chief
at section co-chairs
Nachi Nagappan
and
Terence Kelly
.

submissions

XATSHOME
For hosting ATS3 and developing CodeDepot
Project Description
ATS3 refers to the third edition of ATS, which is currently
being developed at
ATS-Xanadu
.
XATSHOME is a place for one to learn ATS3 and also contribute to ATS3.
A Quick Method for Trying ATS3
There is a directory of the name 'contrib'. For now, there is
'contrib/githwxi'. You should set up a directory for your own use by
following the example or from scratch. There will be other examples
in this directory that you can follow in the future.
The currently released ATS3-to-JS compiler is stored in the following
BIG file:
xassets/JS/xats2js/xats2js_jsemit01_dats_opt0.js
which is bootstrapped from the source of compiler.
Please set the envionment variable XATSHOME to the directory what
XATSHOME is located. For instance, I set it to '~/Research/XATSHOME'
on one of my computers (running bash):
export XATSHOME=${HOME}/Research/XATSHOME
In the directory 'contrib/githwxi', the compiler can be invoked
as follows:
node --stack-size=8000 \
./../../xassets/JS/xats2js/xats2js_jsemit01_dats_opt1.js mycode.dats
where mycode.dats contains some ATS3 code to be compiled. The output
of the compiler is JS code. However, the generated JS code needs some
code in the following directory in order to run:
./../../xassets/JS/xats2js/runtime/xats2js_js1emit.js
./../../xassets/JS/xats2js/runtime/xats2js_prelude.js
Please see the following Makefile for a complete example of compiling
ATS3 to JS:
contrib/githwxi/pground/proj001@250424/misc001/Makefile

data.title: Your phone isn't secretly listening to you, but the truth is more disturbing
data.author: zeech
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了关于手机是否通过麦克风秘密监听用户对话的争议。尽管许多人曾感受到看到相关广告的诡异巧合，但并无确凿证据表明手机在持续监听对话。2024年，媒体曝光了Cox Media Group的“主动聆听”系统，该系统通过语音助手激活后上传的小量语音数据来投放精准广告，但该系统并非持续监听。2019年，网络安全公司Wandera的实验也表明手机并未持续监听。尽管Facebook曾承认对外包的Messenger音频进行人工转录以改进算法，但声称用户知情。文章指出，广告精准投放更多依赖复杂的数据分析，而非简单的麦克风监听，这一真相比想象中更复杂和令人不安。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：手机是否秘密监听用户，以及相关隐私问题和技术滥用问题

不同观点：
• **ThinkBeat**：认为手机可能会被监听，尤其是通过恶意软件或间谍软件（如NSO集团的Pegasus软件）。虽然一般公司可能不会监听，但不能排除情报机构拥有更先进的工具进行监听。
• **benlivengood**：认为广告技术非常先进，可以通过用户行为数据和机器学习模型推断用户兴趣，甚至不需要直接监听。广告推荐系统可能通过其他数据源进行高度相关的广告投放。
• **NemoNobody**：认为手机并不会一直进行录音或跟踪，但在某些特定情况下可能会记录信息。跟踪用户行为并不是一直进行的，但在某些场景下是可能的。
• **fmajid**：提到曾有公司尝试使用音频识别技术来追踪用户暴露于广告的情况，尽管他们拒绝了合作，但市场上确实存在一些不道德的公司。
• **alganet**：认为技术滥用是不可避免的，用户可以保持适度的 paranoid（多疑）态度，但不必完全孤立自己或放弃技术。接受并适应技术的同时保持警觉。

补充讨论：
• **diggernet**：提到Android应用会截屏并发送给第三方，质疑如何检测并阻止这种行为。
• **wrs**：指出智能电视也会发送截图，链接了一个学术文章作为证据。
• **polskibus**：询问iOS应用是否也会截屏其他应用的活动，并讨论如何阻止这种行为。
• **washadjeffmad**：回顾了9/11后的元数据讨论以及TIA项目，质疑当前媒体对类似事件的报道能力。
• **nonameiguess**：分享了YouTube推荐系统的奇怪行为，即使关闭历史记录，系统仍基于同一IP的其他账户活动进行推荐。
• **simonw**：澄清了CMG系统并未通过手机麦克风24/7监听，而是使用激活语音助手后的短语音数据，并讨论了Apple和Facebook的相关隐私问题。
• **anenefan**：通过其兄弟的经历说明应用权限滥用问题，认为Android应用权限管理需要改进。
• **ivape**：质疑Siri如何在不持续监听的情况下捕捉唤醒词，并暗示大公司可能出于自身利益或政府要求进行监控。
• **Am4TIfIsER0ppos**：认为设备可能会发送所有数据回家，包括每个按键、触摸屏操作、加速度计样本和音频样本，并担心5G带宽可能使这种情况变得更严重。

争议焦点：
• 手机是否通过麦克风进行持续监听以投放相关广告。
• 如何有效检测和阻止应用截屏和发送数据的行为。
• 广告技术是否已经先进到可以通过其他数据源实现高度个性化的广告推荐，而不需要直接监听用户。
• 用户应如何在技术便利和隐私保护之间取得平衡。

How does Facebook occasionally deliver such disconcertingly timed advertisements? Is it really listening to users through their smartphone microphones? Or is the truth much more unsettling?
Depositphotos
View gallery - 3 images
Perhaps one of the most pervasive longstanding technology conspiracy theories is that your smartphone is constantly listening in on your private conversations. Almost everyone at some point has felt the eerie synchronicity of seeing an ad served up on a social media platform that exactly corresponds to a recent conversation. It’s certainly unnerving, and the most simple explanation is one of direct surveillance. Of course Facebook, Google and Apple are all listening in on your private conversations with friends, catching key words, and then serving you tailored advertisements. And of course they would deny this is happening.
The problem is, outside of anecdotal cases, no one has ever been able to find clear evidence that this is actually happening.
Editor's note: Readers often ask us for follow-ups on memorable stories. What has happened to this story over the years? This article was originally published in 2019 but it has been re-edited and updated with new information current as of April 15, 2025. Enjoy!
In 2024 a big news story emerged purporting to finally offer the smoking gun evidence proving once and for all that private conversations are tracked by smartphones to tailor ads to individual users. Investigative news site
404 Media revealed the massive media conglomerate Cox Media Group
(CMG) had developed a system it called Active Listening. The system could apparently capture what it called "real-time intent data" using a smart device's microphone. This "voice data" could then be paired with AI processes and other "behavioral data" to serve up highly targeted advertisements.
Exactly how this Active Listening system actually worked was unclear but almost immediately every major tech company distanced itself from CMG. Amazon claimed to have never worked with CMG as an ad partner, while Google and Meta swiftly severed any ties with the company. Even CMG went into damage control mode
stating the Active Listening product
had been "discontinued to avoid misperception."
As far as anyone could understand, the proposed CMG system wasn't listening through a phone's microphone 24/7, instead it was using those small slivers of voice data that are recorded and uploaded to the cloud in the moments after you activate your voice assistant with a "Hey Google" or "Hey Siri" command. While the revelation certainly rekindled the "my smartphone is listening to me all the time" conspiracy, it didn't debunk some of the basic reasons why this idea is still technically untenable. And to understand this we need to go back a few years.
In 2019 Mobile cybersecurity company Wandera conducted a series of experiments to understand how your smartphone could be consistently listening in to your private conversations. These experiments busted the urban myth but also pointed to a the truth about how companies like Facebook sometimes serve up such disturbingly accurate advertisements that is much more complex, and unsettling.
Facebook admits listening to private conversations
In early August 2019,
Bloomberg News published a story
revealing how Facebook had contracted an external company to transcribe audio conversations conducted through the Facebook Messenger app. The process was engaged to test the accuracy of an automatic transcription algorithm Facebook was rolling out, and the company claimed all users who opted in to the transcription service were aware of the potential human review system. While
some reports questioned
how transparent Facebook’s notification process actually was, the story rapidly spread across media outlets, with a vast
array of headlines
dramatically affirming “
Facebook admits it was listening to your private conversations.
”
To the average headline skimmer, whose primary knowledge of news comes from glancing across headlines that pop up in social media streams, this was enough to reanimate years of conspiratorial assumptions. The news story was akin to throwing gasoline on the burning embers of a myth that had almost been extinguished.
Even the media outlet that broke the
43799802.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了关于手机是否通过麦克风秘密监听用户对话的争议。尽管许多人曾感受到看到相关广告的诡异巧合，但并无确凿证据表明手机在持续监听对话。2024年，媒体曝光了Cox Media Group的“主动聆听”系统，该系统通过语音助手激活后上传的小量语音数据来投放精准广告，但该系统并非持续监听。2019年，网络安全公司Wandera的实验也表明手机并未持续监听。尽管Facebook曾承认对外包的Messenger音频进行人工转录以改进算法，但声称用户知情。文章指出，广告精准投放更多依赖复杂的数据分析，而非简单的麦克风监听，这一真相比想象中更复杂和令人不安。

data.title: OpenAI releases image generation in the API
data.author: themanmaran
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：OpenAI图像生成API的使用体验、价格、技术实现及应用场景

不同观点：
• [cuuupid] 认为API在政府和军事相关任务中的拒绝率很高，这可能会促使承包商使用中国开发的开源模型，从而带来安全隐患。同时提到有某种特定层级的API访问几乎没有任何内容审核，且一些国防承包商已经在使用该层级，但未说明如何申请。
• [johnyzee] 抱怨在使用图像生成时遇到了复杂的验证流程，包括添加支付方式、组织验证，甚至需要提供生物识别信息，体验非常糟糕。
• [tezza] 和 [film42] 分享了使用图像生成API生成图片的实际案例和花费，认为对于个人娱乐来说价格尚可接受，但若用于商业产品则成本过高。
• [alasano] 提供了一个自建的本地工具，涵盖了所有API选项，并增加了内置遮罩创建和成本跟踪功能，认为OpenAI的Playground并未完全展示所有功能。
• [Imnimo] 对需要大批量生成图像的应用场景表示好奇，认为大多数情况下单次图像生成已足够，不明白为何需要大量生成。
• [minimaxir] 认为API的定价较高，生成的图像质量低于竞争对手模型，且生成时间较长，提示需要复杂的提示词增强才能获得理想结果。
• [hombre_fatal] 对API的实现方式表示兴趣，特别是其同步生成图像的方式，而非更常见的异步处理，认为这种设计在AI图像生成中较为独特。
• [badmonster] 详细列出了API的定价，指出对于初创公司而言，这种价格可能过高。
• [jumploops] 认为新模型基于自回归生成图像，比扩散模型在遵循文本提示方面更加准确，并提供了具体例子支持这一观点。
• [gitroom] 抱怨使用API的验证流程过于复杂，认为这些额外的步骤会将用户推向其他替代产品。
• [qhwudbebd] 指出API在图像生成端点上存在技术问题，特别是新旧模型在参数设置上的不一致性，导致使用不便。
• [gervwyk] 希望API能够更好地支持SVG图像生成，并认为当前AI工具在生成SVG图像方面表现不佳，Canva仍是最佳选择。
• [_pdp_] 分享了将API集成到平台中的实际应用案例，指出API在广告和营销材料制作中的潜力，但也指出其并非完美，特别是在图像编辑方面仍有改进空间。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是API的价格和图像生成质量，部分用户认为价格偏高且图像质量不如竞争对手。
• 另一个争议点是API的验证和使用流程复杂，特别是支付和生物识别信息验证步骤，让一些用户感到不满。
• 技术实现上，部分用户对API的同步处理方式和新旧模型参数不一致问题提出了质疑，认为这增加了使用难度。
• 部分用户分享了API的实际应用案例，展示了其在商业和个人项目中的潜力，但也指出了需要改进的方面，如图像编辑功能和SVG生成支持。

data.title: Why Autistic Women Have Been Overlooked for Decades
data.author: EA-3167
data.article_summary: 《Off the Spectrum: Why the Science of Autism Has Failed Women and Girls》一书指出，自闭症诊断长期存在性别偏见，尤其忽视了女性患者。许多自闭症女性为了避免社会排斥，采取了“伪装”（camouflaging）和“掩饰”（masking）策略，努力融入常人社会。这种行为与传统自闭症表现不符，传统上自闭症以社交隔离为特征。然而，这种伪装可能带来沉重的心理代价，例如更高的精神疾病住院率。研究显示，自闭症女性往往通过抑制自我刺激行为（如手部拍打）来避免显得与众不同，但这也增加了她们的心理负担。作者Gina Rippon呼吁临床医生采用更细致的问题来识别自闭症女性，而不仅仅依赖于传统的诊断标准。

I
t’s been
more than 30 years since the award-winning film
“Rain Man,”
starring Dustin Hoffman and Tom Cruise, put a spotlight on autism — or, more specifically, on a specific type of autism characterized by social awkwardness and isolation and typically affecting males. Yet as far back as the 1980s, at least one prominent autism researcher
wondered
whether autism’s male skew might simply reflect the fact that autistic females were, for some reason, going undiagnosed.
Over the past decade, spurred by the personal testimonies of late-diagnosed women, autism researchers have increasingly examined this question. As it turns out, many
autistic
women and girls are driven by a powerful desire to avoid social rejection, so powerful, in fact, that they may adopt two broad strategies — camouflaging and masking — to hide their condition in an attempt to better fit in with neurotypical peers and family members.
“Off the Spectrum: Why the Science of Autism Has Failed Women and Girls,”
by Gina Rippon (Seal Press, 352 pages).
Such behavior is “at odds with the traditional picture of autism,” writes Gina Rippon, an emeritus professor of cognitive neuroimaging at Aston University in Birmingham, England, in her new book
“Off the Spectrum: Why the Science of Autism Has Failed Women and Girls.”
And while the ability to blend in might seem like a positive, it can ultimately take a heavy toll. Rippon points, for example, to surveys showing that by age 25, about 20 percent of autistic women have been hospitalized for a psychiatric condition, more than twice the rate of autistic men.
In the U.S., the rate of autism has been
increasing
since at least 2000, and many autism researchers, including Rippon, believe more inclusive diagnostic criteria, coupled with increased awareness, have contributed to the rise. Last week, however, Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr.
dismissed this idea
and insisted that the condition is caused by environmental factors. The National Institutes of Health has begun work on a
research initiative
that aims to look into this further.
Rippon spoke with Undark about how autistic individuals who use camouflaging and masking, including some males, often pay a high price for putting on their “best normal.” Our interview, conducted over Zoom, has been edited for length and clarity.
Undark: In the book, you write that clinicians may need to ask finer-grained questions to identify autistic girls and women. You gave a really interesting example, “Does your child have friends?”
Gina Rippon:
How autism has always been identified is through social isolation. If you read the very early reports, it’s almost intentionally isolated — [individuals with autism] didn’t seem to want any contact with other people, or care if they didn’t have it. So, the issue about friends was key: “Does your child have any friends?”
If the answer is no, then that’s a red flag for the autism checklist. If the answer is yes, but you’re not asked, “Does your daughter find it difficult to make friends? Or if she makes friends, is it just one child that she gets kind of fixated with and then there’s some breaking up?’’ There’s not the kind of deep dive that is necessary.
UD: In the past decade, researchers have increasingly turned their attention to camouflaging and masking. Can you explain what these terms are? And what do findings from brain imaging studies suggest about these behaviors?
GR:
Way back in the 1980s, when people started to notice that there weren’t many girls [diagnosed with autism], there was a kind of almost off-the-cuff comment that maybe girls were just better at hiding their differences: They weren’t causing any disturbance in the classroom, or something like that. It turns out — particularly via a lot of really powerful personal testimonies of late-diagnosed women — that they had actually spent all their lives disguising the fact that they had the difficulties associated with being autistic.
They had lots of sensory difficulties. They needed to calm themselves down by what’s called stimming: hand flapping or unusual bits of behavior, which they desperately tried to suppress because they didn’t want to stand out as being odd or weird. Therefore, they “camouflaged,” tried to blend in with everybody else.

data.title: One quantum transition makes light at 21 cm
data.author: Brajeshwar
data.article_summary: 这篇文章主要介绍了银河系Messier 81的地图，该地图通过非常大型阵列（Very Large Array）的数据绘制，展示了这一螺旋臂恒星形成星系在21厘米波长辐射下的情况。文章解释了氢原子的自旋翻转跃迁会发出21厘米波长的光，这是宇宙中最重要的一种辐射波长。氢是宇宙中最常见的原子，其质子和电子的自旋有50/50的概率对齐，这种对齐状态能量较高，当它们转到反向对齐时会发出21厘米波长的光。这一量子跃迁不仅产生了一种“魔法长度”的辐射，还可能帮助我们揭示宇宙中最神秘的秘密，比如通过21厘米天文学绘制气体云的位置和密度。文章还讨论了光的连续和离散过程，指出21厘米波长在理解光如何产生方面具有关键作用。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：21厘米氢线（氢原子的 forbidden  transition）、其物理意义、实际应用以及精确性。

不同观点：
• **对于“ forbidden transition”的解释**：
  - [wasabi991011] 认为“forbidden transition”只是在简化模型下才被视为 forbidden。在更现实的模型中，这只是概率较低的普通跃迁，尤其是在电偶极近似下被禁止的跃迁可以通过磁偶极相互作用发生。
  
• **21厘米线的实际应用**：
  - [mjd] 提到21厘米线被用于先锋号探测器的铭牌上，作为与外星文明交流的长度基准。
  - [mcswell] 指出21厘米波长曾被提议用于SETI（搜寻地外文明计划）的无线电通讯。
  
• **对21厘米波长精确性的质疑**：
  - [lud_lite] 询问21厘米是否是精确值。
  - [hackrmn] 对21厘米这一“精确”波长感到困惑，因为厘米作为单位是历史上人为定义的，而非基于物理常数。
  - [amiga386] 通过引用维基百科指出，最精确的测量结果为21.106114054160 ± 0.000000000030厘米，而非正好21厘米。

• **对21厘米线跃迁的物理理解**：
  - [joemag] 最初对跃迁如何满足角动量守恒感到困惑，但意识到光子作为自旋1粒子，可以通过数学解释该跃迁。
  
• **对实验和技术的讨论**：
  - [imoverclocked] 认为该理论让我们能够更深入地观察过去，具有实际意义。
  - [belter] 提到在科幻作品《接触》中，外星信号的频率是氢线频率的π倍，暗示21厘米线的特殊性。
  - [CamperBob2] 指出通过氢脉泽（H-maser）可以实现对21厘米跃迁的实验室测量，并解释了如何通过保持低温来观测跃迁线宽。

补充讨论：
• **其他关联和个人经历**：
  - [kccqzy] 表示对21厘米波长感到新奇，因为习惯于更短的波长。

This map of the galaxy Messier 81, constructed from data taken with the Very Large Array, maps out this spiral-armed, star-forming galaxy in 21 centimeter emissions. The spin-flip transition of hydrogen, which emits light at precisely 21 centimeters in wavelength, is in many ways the most important length for radiation in the entire Universe.
(
Credit
: NRAO/AUI/NSF)
Key Takeaways
Across the observable Universe, there are some 10^80 atoms, and most of them are simple hydrogen: made of just one proton and one electron each.
Every time a hydrogen atom forms, there’s a 50/50 shot that the proton and electron will have their spins aligned, which is a slightly higher-energy state than if they’re not aligned.
The quantum transition from the aligned state to the anti-aligned state is one of the most extreme transitions of all, and it produces light of precisely 21 cm in wavelength: arguably the most important length in the Universe.
Ethan Siegel
Copy a link to the article entitled http://Why%2021%20cm%20is%20our%20Universe’s%20“magic%20length”
